All five begin fully in frame, toes on a taped line, then explode into a flat-out head-to-head sprint across forty metres of concrete, arms driving, chests dipping at a strip of tape, decelerating still inside the frame. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level. Bright, high-contrast, sports-ad punch.

Thick fog hangs still over a crushed red-brick clay court, softening the sagging net, a leaning umpire chair and two drag brooms hooked on the chain fence; the clay glows dull terracotta through the murk. One adult performs alone: a tall Ecuadorian man in his thirties, hair tied in a short tail, wearing a white long-sleeve and slate trousers, shoes printing arcs in the clay. Working a few metres of baseline, he spins a silk flag into fast horizontal rifles, snaps it around his body, then launches a high double toss that vanishes into the fog before dropping back into his hands. One continuous shot, the camera craning down from high above to eye level, keeping him fully framed. Gritty documentary texture.

Soft overcast daylight flattens a close-mown grass tennis lawn edged by a tall clipped hedge, chalk lines still crisp, a low net strung across the middle and a wooden roller parked at the corner. Nothing stirs, no wind, no leaves moving. Two adults stand on the turf alone: a broad Maori man in his thirties, sleeveless olive top, and a slender Iranian woman in a pale grey long-sleeve, hair knotted high. Each plants their feet on one small patch of grass, hauling thick battle ropes into rolling alternating waves, then rearing up and slamming both ends into the lawn, spray flicking from wet blades. One continuous shot, a slow orbit around them, both fully framed throughout. Dreamy, muted, music-video softness.

Fireworks burst over black river water, their colour smeared across the rain-slicked concrete slabs of a riverside esplanade where mooring bollards and a raised drawbridge stand black against the sky. Crouched at a painted seam with feet on the slab and both entirely in frame are two adults: a heavily muscled Bahamian man in a black singlet, and a tall Czech woman in her thirties, blonde ponytail, grey crop top and navy shorts. They launch together, racing head-to-head down fifty metres of esplanade, spray fanning from their shoes, dipping at an imagined line and coasting to a stop without ever leaving frame. Spectators crowd the railing above. A static tripod at eye level holds one continuous shot. Epic, drenched in colour.

Soft overcast daylight sits on a corporate campus quad, its mown lawn bordered by mirrored office blocks, a drained reflecting pool and a bare flagpole; the air is completely still. Five adults train on the grass, nobody else in sight: a huge Fijian man in a grey tee, a stocky Danish woman with cropped blonde hair, a lean Egyptian man in black, a tall Black woman in maroon, and a barrel-chested white man in his fifties. All begin fully in frame, boots on turf, and stay framed while heaving heavy sandbags between partners, hip-driven tosses of two or three metres, absorbing catches in a deep squat, rotating around a loose ring. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-out revealing more of the surroundings. Epic, cinematic restraint.

Three adults take over a squash court in a Miami athletic club, pale hardwood glowing under even ceiling panels, the front wall scuffed with ball marks, a glass back wall reflecting nothing but the empty gallery. A muscular Dominican man in red shorts, a compact Korean-American woman with a bleached buzz cut, and a lean Egyptian-American man in a black tee take turns at a padded low box. Each runs three strides, punches both hands onto the top, tucks knees through, lands quietly and rolls a shoulder; the next follows with a one-handed speed vault back. Paper scraps tumble across the boards. All three stay fully in frame, feet on the wood between vaults. One continuous shot, the camera orbiting slowly.

Golden hour over a scrubby grassland on Miami's western edge, a lone leaning fence post and a distant water tower; beyond it a strip of flickering neon and a searchlight beam sweeping the sky. Five adults line up fully in frame on the short grass, each holding a three-meter silk ribbon: a tall Sudanese-American man in white, a curvy Cuban woman in scarlet, a wiry Filipino man in gold, a broad Russian-American woman in violet, a bearded Greek-American man in teal. They tear across the field in a staggered line, ribbons snapping into long arcs, then bound high and whip the silks into loops before sprinting back. All five stay framed. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level.

One continuous shot pans slowly left to right across a packed gravel crossroads deep in the taiga, past a leaning signpost, a rusted fuel drum and a wall of black spruce. Two adults stand on the gravel, both fully in frame, feet planted. A stocky Korean man in his thirties with a buzzcut, orange shell jacket and grey joggers charges four strides and kongs over a low weathered supply crate, knees punching cleanly through his arms. A tall Nigerian woman in her forties, long braids, navy hoodie, answers with a dash vault, spins and kongs back the other way. Heavy snowfall drops straight down through motionless air; both stay framed throughout, boots crunching flat gravel.

Warm tungsten work lamps hang between towering bare steel racks in a shuttered taiga distribution warehouse, torn packing slips and pale paper scraps tumbling weightlessly through the amber beams. Two adults crouch shoulder to shoulder on the polished concrete at the aisle head, both entirely in frame with feet on the floor. A wiry Ethiopian woman in her twenties, cropped afro, lilac crop top and black tights, snaps away first; a broad Finnish man in his late thirties, sandy ponytail, faded green tank, hauls himself even. They tear the length of the aisle toward a taped finish line while one continuous shot dollies slowly out, revealing more of the racking; near the end he surges at the lens and his shoulders leave the frame.

Inside a ballet rehearsal studio carved into a timber-clad taiga arts house, wooden barres line one wall and a floodlight rig rakes hard white light across chalk-scuffed black marley, throwing enormous shadows onto the mirrorless plaster. Two adults square up, both fully in frame, socks and wraps planted on the vinyl. A freckled Irish woman in her thirties with a red topknot and yellow sports bra snaps jabs; a lean Colombian man in his twenties, teal shorts, slips low, rolls under a hook and pops back grinning. They trade playful bursts, ducking and bobbing a couple of metres across the marley. The static tripod holds at eye level for one continuous shot; he bounces forward until his shoulder crosses out of frame.

Deep beneath the taiga lies a decommissioned bunker hall: ribbed concrete vaults, dripping overhead pipes, a rusted blast door cranked half open. Low practice lamps carve deep shadows while haze rolls and slow spotlights sweep the damp concrete floor. Three adults hold en garde, all fully in frame, feet on the slab. A silver-haired Brazilian man in his fifties advances behind a sport foil; a broad-shouldered Somali woman in her thirties, white jacket, blue socks, parries quarte and ripostes; a compact Vietnamese man in his twenties fleches past them, resets, and lunges again. They work the full length of the hall in one continuous shot as the camera orbits slowly around them, blades ringing, all three staying in frame.

A small timber judo dojo in a taiga settlement: green tatami squares, a rack of folded belts, dust hanging motionless in the shafts of daylight falling from high windows. One adult stands alone at the centre of the mat, fully in frame, bare feet on the tatami — a lanky Japanese-Peruvian man in his late twenties, dyed platinum hair, oversized cream vest, wide charcoal trousers. He hits sharp popping isolations, ticking his chest, rolling a slow wave from one fingertip to the other, freezing mid-glitch. Spectators watch from a raised bench gallery behind a wooden railing, never on the mat. Air is perfectly still; one continuous shot tracks sideways at a walking pace.

Summer has stripped an old taiga arena down to its painted concrete slab, faded faceoff circles still ghosting under scarred dasher boards while tungsten work lamps burn orange in the roof trusses. Five adults spread across the slab, every one fully in frame with shoes on the paint: a broad Māori woman in her forties, a lean Egyptian man in his thirties, a silver-bearded Danish man, a small Filipina woman in her twenties, a tattooed Chilean man. A disc floats out; two of them lay out horizontally, skidding a metre on their hips, then bounce up to feed the next huck. Air hangs dead still. One continuous shot pans slowly left to right.

Numbered bays and coiled charging cables fill a cavernous taiga bus depot, acid-green and pink neon tubes staining the striped asphalt while shredded ticket paper tumbles slowly through the colored beams. Two adults face each other, both fully in frame, barefoot on the asphalt. A heavyset Cuban woman in her thirties, gold hoops, white cropped tee, rocks a wide ginga; a slim Algerian man in his forties, shaved head, loose red trousers, answers with a low au, sweeps a meia-lua past her waist and ducks under her return kick. They circle within a few metres, trading cartwheels and esquivas, while one continuous shot orbits slowly around the pair.

Neon spills from a tall pylon sign across the faded asphalt of a hypermarket parking lot on the edge of the taiga, empty stall lines running out toward black timber and a rack of bent trolleys. Far above the treeline, fireworks bloom and fade in soft green and gold. One adult begins dead centre, fully in frame, sneakers flat on the asphalt: a muscular Jamaican woman in her fifties, silver locs tied back, magenta windbreaker, holding two long ribbon streamers. She explodes into a sprint, carving the streamers into wide spirals, then breaks into a bounding side gallop clear across the lot. One continuous shot cranes down from high overhead to eye level, keeping her fully framed.

Rain hisses across a grey ash plain under a misty taiga sunrise, puddles splashing between low cinder cones and a spine of bleached driftwood. Four adults line up on the ash, all fully in frame with spikes on the flat crust: a rangy Sudanese man in his twenties, a compact Polish woman in her thirties with a wet blonde plait, a broad Samoan man in his forties, a sinewy Bolivian woman in her fifties. In turn they pound out long approach runs, hit a scratched takeoff line and sail into the soft ash, landing in grey sprays. One continuous shot tracks sideways at a walking pace; the last jumper runs straight past the lens, half leaving frame.

A provincial taiga stadium sits abandoned: striped natural grass, sagging floodlight masts, a blank scoreboard above rows of entirely empty plastic seats. Hazy dust-gold afternoon light lies over everything, the air itself unmoving. Six adults stand in a loose file on the turf, all fully in frame with boots on the grass — a tall Ukrainian woman in her forties, a stout Ghanaian man in his thirties, a wiry Korean woman, a bearded Turkish man, a freckled Canadian woman in her fifties, a young Nepali man. Gripping a canvas hose, they sprint it off its reel across the whole pitch, then drop the coupling and jog back, chests heaving, all six staying in frame. One continuous shot pans slowly from left to right.

A converted timber workshop deep in the taiga now serves as a training box: black rubber tiles, a chalk-dusted barbell rack, frost feathering the small windows, one bank of hard floodlights blasting in from the left. Inside, one adult dances on a single tile square — a broad Buryat woman in her thirties, hair in twin knots, oversized grey hoodie, baggy olive cargo trousers, scuffed high-tops. She fires hard jabs across her body, snaps into a buck jump that lands heavy, freezes mid-kill-off with her ribs shuddering, then unloads again. The still air holds the chalk she kicks up. She stays fully in frame, feet returning to the same tiles. One continuous shot, panning slowly from left to right.

Blue hour settles over a drained dry dock at a river shipyard, keel blocks in rows, a gantry crane black against the sky, distant headlights on the causeway smearing into long light trails. The wet concrete holds a dull sheen. Boots planted on the slab, five adults space out along the dock floor, none leaving frame: a huge Icelandic man in his forties, a compact Indian woman in her twenties, a grey-templed Kenyan man, a broad Mexican woman in her thirties, a tattooed Georgian man. They hoist medicine balls overhead and drive them down, ball after ball cracking off the slab and spitting water, catching on the rebound. One continuous shot cranes down from high above to eye level.

Midday sun hammers a wide bay of firm damp sand beneath low taiga cliffs, black jetty pilings leaning out of the shallows and ribbons of dry sand streaming low across the flat. One adult holds the centre of frame, feet planted on the packed sand: a broad-shouldered Pakistani man in his thirties, shaved head, bright coral rashguard, black shorts, ankles taped. Rooted to one spot, he fires spinning hook kicks and jumping tornado kicks, each pivot ripping a fan of wet grit into the sunlight before he lands squared and reloads. His shadow is short and hard. One continuous shot dollies slowly out, revealing more cliff, more bay, more empty sand.

Soft overcast light flattens a hillside vineyard where trellised vines run in trained rows over compacted soil, tractor ruts still holding rainwater, and grey surf crashes against the rocks far below the taiga shoreline. Four adults hold a tight square on the soil, all fully in frame, feet down: a tall Croatian woman in her twenties with a wet-look bob, a stocky Thai man in his forties, a freckled Australian woman in her thirties, a wiry Lebanese man in his fifties. Silk flags in tangerine and cobalt whirl around their bodies, snap flat, then launch into synchronized quad tosses caught blind behind the back. One continuous shot dollies slowly in toward them.

Rain slicks the black granite of a sunken plaza in a taiga boomtown's small banking district, glass towers rising over dark pines, water beading on a ring of steel bollards. Five adults form a tight circle, each rooted to one square of stone: a lanky Yakut man in a red windbreaker, a silver-haired Danish woman in navy, a heavy-shouldered Nigerian-Russian man in yellow, a young Kazakh woman with a pink braid, a compact Brazilian man in white. They trade eight-bar breaks — pickup steps, toe-heel riffs, a rattling shim-sham chorus — metal plates cracking off the wet granite and throwing spray. Nobody moves off their square, and all five stay fully in frame. One continuous shot, orbiting slowly.

Strung tungsten lamps light a half-bored road tunnel through taiga bedrock, grey shotcrete ribbed with drill scars, cable spools shoved against the wall, torn survey paper tumbling in the draught. Scattered down the raw floor with boots on the shotcrete, six adults keep entirely within frame: a heavy Russian-Buryat man in his forties, a sinewy Haitian woman in her thirties, a tall Norwegian man, a short Indonesian woman in her twenties, a grey-bearded Uzbek man, a broad Argentinian woman. Wooden staffs blur through figure-eights, roll across shoulders and backs, and fly up into short tosses caught behind the head as they shift a few metres. One continuous shot circles handheld at chest height.

Inside a fabrication shed at a taiga river shipyard, stacked hull plates and an idle overhead crane frame a floor of rust-stained steel. Daylight drops in hard shafts from clerestory windows, mixing with drifting haze that moving spotlights slice open. Four adults face off in pairs, all fully in frame, feet on the plate: a tall Malaysian woman in her thirties, a barrel-chested Serbian man in his forties, a lean Rwandan man in his twenties, a silver-haired French woman. Shinai crack together as they drive forward with stamping fumikomi steps, cut men, cut kote, and reset a couple of metres back. One continuous shot orbits slowly around the drill.

A fencing hall in a taiga sports academy, rented out for a party: the metallic piste strip laid over dark rubber, magenta and green stage lights washing the walls, steam creeping from floor vents. Three adults dance on the strip. A big-bellied Punjabi-Russian man in a black kurta, a tall Nepali woman with gold bangles, and a sinewy Ghanaian man in a white vest drive a fast chaal step, shoulders shrugging on the beat, then leap with heels kicking back and wrists spinning above their heads. Guests watch from the bleachers behind a railing, off the floor. All three start fully framed, feet on the strip; the man in the kurta advances until the lens crops his knees. One continuous shot, slowly dollying out.

Bright even lamps flood the interior of an old taiga barn: wide plank flooring worn smooth, hay bales stacked to the loft ladder, harness and tack hanging on hand-hewn posts. Three adults stand on the boards, all fully in frame — a springy Dominican man in his twenties in a mustard tee, a tall Estonian woman in her thirties with a blonde crop, a compact Chinese man in his forties. Taking turns, each lifts a knee into a high windup, strides, and fires a hard throw into a padded target nailed to a bale, whooping when the boards thud. Not a draught moves inside. A handheld camera circles them at chest height in one continuous shot.

Rows of cold kilns line an abandoned brick factory hall on the taiga's edge, clerestory panes shattered, portable tungsten lamps casting long amber pools over a floor of broken brick tile. One adult stands alone at the far end, fully in frame, spikes on the tile: a rangy Somali-Swedish man in his thirties, shaved head, faded grey singlet, taped left ankle. He sprints twenty metres down the hall, hits a chalked board and links the phases — hop, long reaching step, then a final jump into a sand-filled crate, dust bursting up. Nothing else moves in the hall. One continuous shot orbits slowly around him, holding him fully in frame.

Golden hour lies across an old stone threshing floor on a bluff above a taiga valley: a ring of worn flagstones, stacked rye sheaves, a low dry-stone wall, chaff and fine dust skating low over the slabs in the evening draught. One adult occupies a single stone square, fully in frame, feet on the flags: a wiry Mongolian woman in her forties, dark braid whipping, faded olive tank, patched work trousers, palms already grey with stone dust. She snaps down into burpees — chest to flagstone, feet driven back under her, then an explosive jump with hands clapped overhead — over and over, breath steaming. One continuous shot dollies slowly out, widening onto the valley.

Mist floods the taiga valleys below a flat sandstone plateau where a line of faded cloth pennants and a hand-stacked cairn shudder in a hard cold wind, the hardpan crusted between tufts of sparse scrub. Sunrise comes soft and pearlescent. One adult holds the middle of the plateau, fully in frame, boots on the hardpan: a broad Punjabi-Canadian woman in her fifties, long grey-streaked braid, saffron dupatta snapping like a flag, indigo tunic. Rooted to one spot, she claps high overhead, springs into scissoring bhangra jumps, punches a heel out from a deep crouch and rolls her shoulders back into the bounce. One continuous shot pans slowly left to right.

Hazy dust-toned afternoon light hangs over a rooftop terrace of concrete pavers, the taiga city's cold towers stacked beyond a low parapet, dead planters and a stripped pergola at one side while dry leaves skate and curl low across the slabs. One adult starts near the parapet, fully in frame, trainers flat on the pavers: a compact Vietnamese-Australian man in his thirties, undercut, charcoal long-sleeve, oxblood shorts. He loads deep and fires a standing broad jump, sticks the landing, then chains three bounding leaps across a few metres of paver, arms scything. One continuous shot is held on a static tripod at eye level; he stays fully framed.

Flat overcast light on a stony plain at the taiga's dry southern edge, tight-packed dark pebbles varnished by rain, a stunted larch and a stack of weathered stone cairns far off. One adult crosses the ground alone: a stocky Evenk man in his forties, weather-lined face, black hair tied back, red sash over a padded grey jacket, canvas shoes. He sinks into a deep wide-legged crouch, hands cocked at his chest, then explodes forward in long low pounces, landing silently, sweeping one leg wide, rising and springing again, covering fifteen meters across the frame. Rain streaks slant past and puddles burst underfoot. He remains fully in frame. One continuous shot, the camera orbiting slowly.

Storm light bruises the sky over a dry lakebed of cracked pale clay ringed by black larch, a salt-rimmed puddle glinting near a half-buried tractor tyre. Not a leaf moves. Two adults begin standing on the clay, both fully in frame: a broad Romani-Spanish man in his thirties, dark curls, sleeveless denim; a tall Sudanese-British woman in her twenties, orange headwrap, teal leggings. She drops to her hands and he lifts her ankles; they charge a wheelbarrow crawl a few metres over the tiles, laughing as she reaches a scratched line, then swap roles and blast back. One continuous shot tracks sideways at a steady walking pace, keeping both framed.

A closed highway overpass arcs above a taiga river, its lane paint bright on the asphalt, orange plastic barriers strung across both ends, morning mist swallowing the far ramp and softening the pines below. The air is completely still. One adult stands squarely in the middle lane, fully in frame, spikes on the paint: a beaming Nigerian-German man in his twenties, dreadlocks bundled up, lime tee, white shorts, wrist chalked. He winds the discus back in wide slow arcs, drops into a rotational spin on the same square of asphalt, and rips it out over the barrier, finishing with a delighted stagger. The camera never moves: a static tripod at eye level, one continuous shot.

Soft overcast light sits on a tar-and-gravel roof deck above a converted taiga textile loft, a squat brick water tank at one end and vent stacks breathing lazy white steam across the membrane. Two adults hold one small patch of roof, both fully in frame, cleats on the gravel: a powerful Puerto Rican woman in her thirties, high ponytail, royal-blue jersey, and a lean Korean-American man in his twenties, backwards cap, white sleeves. They alternate hard swings off a rubber tee, hips whipping through, netting behind snapping with each crack, resetting a ball without ever leaving their spot. The camera cranes down from high above to eye level in one continuous shot.

Snow falls heavily on an abandoned drive-in lot in the taiga, rusted speaker poles, a torn white screen sagging on its frame, cracked asphalt and gravel showing through the drifts. Four adults dance in a tight ring: a broad Sikh-Siberian man with a saffron turban, a slim Tatar woman in an embroidered green kurta, a grey-bearded man from Kerala in a blue phulkari shawl, a strong Estonian woman in orange. They swing into a fast circling step, arms lifting, clap overhead on the beat, drop to one knee, spring up with heels flicking, and rotate positions inside a few meters. The still air muffles everything. All four stay fully in frame, boots on the asphalt. One continuous shot, panning slowly left to right.

Rain hammers a festival pier of painted steel plate jutting into a black taiga river, a rusted crane barge moored beyond. Harsh midday sun cuts through the downpour. Five adults begin fully in frame, feet on the wet plate: a burly Slavic man in red, a tall Somali woman in white, a freckled redhead in orange, a compact Korean man in navy, a silver-haired woman in green. They run a pepper drill, two pairs plus a rotating feeder — forearm bumps, sets, downward hits — sneakers skidding through splashing puddles across a few meters. Then the redhead chases a shanked ball toward the lens and ends half out of frame. One continuous take, locked-off tripod at eye level; spectators crowd the far quay behind barriers.

Harsh midday sun bleaches a narrow walkway of trodden red earth between clipped tea rows in a hardy nursery clearing rimmed by taiga larch, bamboo drying racks and stacked wicker baskets throwing hard little shadows. The heat sits dead calm over the rows. Two adults face each other on the packed earth, both fully in frame: a tall Thai man in his thirties, silk shirt knotted at the waist, and a curvy Afro-Cuban woman in her forties, white vest, cropped bleach-blonde hair. Holding one spot, they cut hands into sharp frames, whip through fast spins and drop into clean death-drop dips, snapping straight back up on the beat. One continuous shot pans slowly from left to right.

A faded grand hotel lobby in a taiga mining town: veined polished marble underfoot, tarnished brass columns, a chandelier under a dust shroud, low practice lamps pooling light and leaving the corners in deep shadow. Four adults grip a thick hemp rope, all fully in frame, shoes squeaking on the stone: a huge Tongan man in his thirties, a wiry Ukrainian woman in her twenties, a bearded Ethiopian man in his forties, a compact Korean woman. Two against two, they lean back and heave, boots skidding a metre across the marble, one pair collapsing in a heap before scrambling up to haul again. One continuous shot orbits slowly around them.

Midday sun bakes the packed sand floor of a working gravel pit gouged out below the taiga treeline, a silent conveyor arm overhead, ridged spoil heaps behind and two short flagged stakes planted far down the flat. Three adults stand at the start line, all fully in frame with bare feet on the sand: a broad Māori man in his twenties, a lean Kazakh woman in her thirties, a freckled Portuguese man in his forties. They settle prone, heels toward the stakes; on a shout they scramble up, sprint the length of the pit and dive full-stretch, skidding on their ribs for the flags. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level.

Six adults hold a tight cluster on straw stubble in a taiga clearing, black spruce walls and a leaning haystack behind them, thunderheads stacked purple-grey overhead. A tall Punjabi man in a red kurta drives one shoulder up, snapping his wrist skyward while tucking both heels under him; beside him a stocky Korean woman in a mustard tunic answers with squat-drop pulses, knees splayed, fists punching overhead. Two lean Nigerian men and two broad Russian women in indigo trade the count, springing on the spot without drifting a step. All six stay fully framed throughout, boots planted in the stubble. One continuous shot, the camera panning slowly from left to right across the still, windless field before the rain breaks.

Blue hour cools a broad sandbar in a shrunken taiga river, pale sand smoothed between bleached driftwood snags, a strung work lantern throwing beams in which fat snowflakes drift and glitter. Two adults stand ankles lashed together with a strip of red cloth, both fully in frame, feet on the sand: a stocky Uzbek woman in her thirties, teal fleece, and a rangy Jamaican-Canadian man in his twenties, yellow beanie, black tracksuit. Counting aloud, they lurch into a stumbling three-legged sprint, find a rhythm, and tear the full length of the bar to a driftwood marker, whooping. One continuous shot circles handheld at chest height, keeping both in frame.

Cold daylight slants through the high windows of a converted taiga hangar skate park, catching plywood transitions and a taped flat bottom while industrial fans push loose flyers and grey dust skimming over the smooth wood. Two adults hold the flat, both fully in frame, feet on the plywood: a lean Sri Lankan man in his thirties, black turtleneck, and a tall Ukrainian woman in her forties, cropped silver hair, oxblood vest. Wooden staffs whirl in tight figure-eights, roll across shoulders and down the spine, then flip up into low tosses caught blind as the pair drift a few metres. Onlookers lean on a mezzanine railing above. One continuous shot dollies slowly in.

Cheerful energy fills the quay of a river port cut into the taiga: stacked rust-orange containers, a yellow gantry crane parked overhead, larch forest crowding the far bank. Six adults spread across the reinforced concrete apron, all six framed head-to-toe, feet planted. A wiry Kenyan man in lime shorts pounds two balls at once, then whips one behind his back; a tall Filipina woman in teal answers with a spin-dribble handoff, and a bearded Swedish man snaps a low push-pass through a partner's legs. Three teammates in candy-bright jerseys orbit, clapping for the ball. They shuffle only a few metres. Midday sun blazes while stray snowflakes drift through the light beams. One continuous shot, the camera craning down from high above to eye level.

Light rain glazes a gravel median walk running between pollarded limes down a boulevard in a taiga river city, iron lamp standards glowing early, wet leaves swirling low over the compacted stone. Five adults gather around a heavy tractor tyre, all fully in frame, boots on the gravel: a huge Georgian man in his forties, a broad Ghanaian woman in her thirties, a sinewy Chilean man, a tall Finnish woman in her fifties, a stocky Indian man in his twenties. Two at a time they wedge fingers under the rubber, drive hips through and flip it end over end down a few metres of path, steam rising off their shoulders. One continuous shot pans slowly left to right.

Dead-calm midday over a taiga clearing: a mown turf airstrip runs straight between the spruce, an orange windsock hanging limp, chipped marker cones along one edge, a tethered glider parked at the treeline, shadows tight and black. The rope comes taut. Anchoring it are four adults — a barrel-chested Uzbek man in his fifties, a tall Angolan woman in her thirties, a wiry Czech man in his twenties, a solid Peruvian woman in her forties — braced two against two, all fully in frame with boots dug into the grass. They lean, heave and stamp without shifting off their patch, heels carving short furrows, one pair dropping to a knee before hauling themselves upright again. One continuous shot dollies slowly in toward them.

An abandoned toll plaza straddles a pass road through the taiga, glassless booths under a sagging steel canopy, faded lane paint arrowing across the concrete, hazy dust-gold afternoon light lying heavy and unmoving over everything. One adult crouches in starting blocks in the third lane, fully in frame, spikes set on the paint: a powerfully built Cameroonian woman in her thirties, cornrows tied back, black-and-gold speedsuit. She rocks into set, holds, then explodes out — shins low, arms driving — hammering three violent strides along the lane paint before pulling up barely two metres on. One continuous shot is held on a static tripod at eye level; she stays framed throughout.

A raw poured concrete slab caps an unfinished tower above a taiga river city, rebar spines bristling at the edges, a crane hook swinging idle, tarps sagging over stacked bags. Hazy amber afternoon light drifts with fine construction dust, the air otherwise slack. Two adults crouch at one end, both fully in frame, boots on the slab: a stocky Kazakh woman in her thirties, hair in a red bandana, denim vest; a tall Sudanese-Italian man in his forties, dusty grey overalls. On a shout they shove empty steel drums into a rolling run clear across the deck. One continuous shot circles handheld at chest height, and he finally rolls his drum past the lens, half out of frame.

Four adults drill on the flat concrete stage of a half-restored open-air amphitheater terraced into a Roman park hillside, cypress spikes and a rusted lighting truss standing behind them. A broad-shouldered Nigerian-Italian man in an orange jersey weaves a ball between plastic cones with his stick; a wiry blonde woman in grey mirrors his toe-drags, while a stocky greying man in navy and a tall Filipina woman in red exchange quick backhand dekes two metres away. Spectators watch from the tiered stone seating above, never stepping down. One continuous shot in soft overcast daylight, the camera orbiting slowly around them, everyone fully in frame.

Noon glare hammers a high grassy shelf above a Roman ring road, a rusted shrine post and a toppled stone bench marking the flowering turf. Five adults begin bunched at centre, every one fully visible, feet in the grass. A rangy Somali woman with braided hair bolts first, cutting hard left; a silver-haired Italian man in charcoal lunges for her shoulder and misses, then peels after a heavyset Brazilian woman in a black tracksuit. Two younger men in grey and oxblood scissor across the whole meadow, sliding on the slick turf as they reverse direction. Far below, traffic light trails streak through the haze. One continuous shot, a handheld camera circling slowly at chest height, all five staying in frame.

Blue hour drains the colour from an old cobbled arch bridge over the Tiber, its iron lamps just warming, the parapet patched with sandbags, black water sliding beneath. Two adults work a ball across the rounded stones: a tall Ethiopian-Italian woman in a charcoal tracksuit rolling step-over after step-over, and a stocky bearded man in his forties, maroon jacket open, cutting the ball back and driving it thirty metres along the empty roadway. Nobody else is on the bridge. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly inward; both start fully framed with feet on the cobbles, then the woman surges at the lens and ends cropped at the waist.

Inside a small Roman yoga studio — light bamboo flooring, one mirrored wall, a dusty palm in a clay pot — three adults play capoeira. A muscular Brazilian man with locs swings a low ginga; a silver-haired white woman in cropped teal answers with an au cartwheel; a slender Japanese-Italian man in white ducks under her heel and rolls out, the three trading places inside a couple of metres of bamboo. Big industrial fans lift loose paper scraps and glittering dust into the bright even overhead light. No one else is present. One continuous shot, epic and burnished, the camera craning down from high above to eye level while all three stay fully in frame on the visible floor.

Harsh floodlights rake in from one side of a Roman wrestling room, throwing hard shadows across the red foam mat; climbing ropes hang along the back wall and the windows are taped over. Three athletes work jumping kicks: a compact Vietnamese-Italian woman in yellow launches switch-kicks into paddles held by a tall bald man in black, then spins and drives a flying roundhouse at a second pair of paddles held by a freckled ginger woman in blue. They cover barely two metres. Nobody else is in the gym. One continuous shot, bright and punchy, the camera dollying slowly toward them, all three fully framed with the mat clearly visible.

A repurposed railway viaduct now runs as a narrow elevated park above Roman rooftops, its tapered concrete planks flanked by oleander troughs and a rusted signal gantry. Two adults run routes down it: a long-limbed Ghanaian woman in a lilac crop top sprinting a deep post, and a lanky pale man in his thirties, grey shorts, floating the ball ahead of her. She snags it over her shoulder at full stride. Overcast light, petals skittering low across the planks; nobody else appears. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly in — both begin fully framed on the deck, then he jogs past the lens and leaves frame at the shoulders.

Under a Roman ring road, a tiled pedestrian underpass runs long and empty, one wall gridded in cracked cream tile, a dead vending alcove and a bare work floodlight blazing from the left. Two adults stand in that hard light on the tiled concrete, both fully in frame, feet down. A slim Vietnamese woman in a grey slip dress rattles a chain of pull-backs, heel drops ringing off the walls, then hooks into a paddle-and-roll. Facing her, a heavyset Greek man in a black shirt answers with a scuffed wing-out, arms flung wide, shoes barely leaving a metre of floor. Air is dead still. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly back to reveal the tunnel.

Under the black glass of a commercial greenhouse outside Rome, tomato gantries recede into misted pipework and only a few low practice lamps burn, carving deep shadows along the wide concrete walkway. Six adults sprint the aisle in resisted pairs: a towering Sudanese man leaning into a thick band anchored by a stocky woman in maroon, a grey-bearded man dragging a loaded sled, a Peruvian woman in green driving beside him, and two more in black digging out shallow, punishing strides for fifteen metres. Fans stir loose paper and dust through the beams. No one else is here. One continuous shot, camera craning down from high overhead to eye level; all six stay framed.

Midday sun bleaches the top deck of a parking garage beside a Roman airport road — faded yellow bay lines, a toppled cone, low hills shimmering past the barrier. One athlete works the empty painted concrete alone: a tall mixed-race woman in her thirties, cornrows tied back, teal singlet and white spikes, driving a five-step rhythm over a row of low training hurdles set across the deck. No other person is anywhere on the structure. Still air, hard shadow. One continuous shot; she starts fully in frame with both feet down, and the camera cranes from high above to eye level as she clears the last hurdle and passes so close her legs exit the frame.

Floodlights on scaffolding wash a cobbled old-town square in Rome, the dry fountain ringed with bunting, a shuttered gelateria behind. Six adults form three facing pairs on the rounded stones and heave weighted canvas sacks back and forth — a burly Sicilian man in a mustard tee catching low and grunting, a tall Kenyan woman in pink firing hers chest-high, a shaved-headed man in denim, a laughing woman with braids, and two more taking short bracing steps to absorb each throw. Locals cheer from balconies and behind the fountain railing, never on the cobbles. One continuous shot, playful and bright, the camera tracking sideways at walking pace; all six stay fully framed.

A loading bay inside a Roman freight depot: one roller door half up, stacked blue pallets, sealed concrete polished by forklift tyres, steam curling from a wall vent through the bright overhead strips. Three practitioners in dark hakama work shinai — a compact older Japanese woman calling strikes, a broad Croatian man answering with lunging men cuts, and a lean Egyptian man in his twenties driving forward on the same small stretch of floor. Bamboo cracks against bamboo; heels slap and slide. No one else is present. One continuous shot, cold and shadowed, a handheld camera circling slowly at chest height with all three fully in frame.

Thick fog sits over a mown launch field outside Rome where balloon envelopes lie folded in long nylon heaps, a wicker basket tips on its side and a limp wind sock hangs from its pole. One athlete trains alone on the short grass: a stocky Māori-Italian woman in her late twenties, black compression top, orange shorts, hair in a knot, driving a weighted sled four metres, resetting, driving again with shoulders low and calves shaking. The air itself is perfectly still. No one else is on the field. One continuous shot, clean and energetic, the camera dollying slowly toward her; she stays fully in frame the whole time.

On a chalk plateau above a hazy coastal plain, a flint cairn and one wind-bent thorn mark the springy turf. Five adults box under flat overcast light: a rangy Ivorian man snapping one-two-hooks into mitts held by a compact silver-haired woman, a broad Turkish-Italian woman rolling under and doubling her left, her partner shouting counts, while a fifth — a lean man in a torn grey vest — circles the pairs correcting elbows. They stay inside a few metres of grass. The air is utterly still and nobody else stands on the down. One continuous shot, epic in scale, the camera dollying slowly out to reveal the plateau; all five remain fully framed.

Blue hour over a bare grey granite plateau in the hills beyond Rome: a house-sized glacial boulder, a leaning cairn, a lit chapel ruin far off whose beams catch drifting snowflakes. Two adults tumble across the swept stone — a willowy Vietnamese woman in a dove-grey unitard linking cartwheel into round-off into cartwheel, and a muscular man in his forties, deep brown skin, black leggings, chasing her line and covering eight metres of rock with the same chain. Nobody else is up here. One continuous shot, dreamy and desaturated, the camera craning down from high above to eye level; both stay entirely within frame, feet finding granite each landing.

Rain films the cracked mud of a drained paddy on the plain south of Rome, dead reed stubble at the bund line and a stone farmhouse blurred in the wet distance. One woman works there: broad-shouldered, Ghanaian, forties, in a soaked orange singlet and mud-black leggings, hair wrapped in a red cloth. She squats under the lip of a tractor tyre, drives it up on edge, and slams it over; steps in, hops through the hoop, and heaves it back the other way, covering only a few metres of glassy ground. Water beads on the rubber and the reflected sky. One continuous shot, a handheld camera circling slowly at chest height, keeping her whole body in frame.

Inside a Roman velodrome the banked timber track curves away into low practice lights, haze hanging thick while spotlights swing across the flat grey concrete infield and stacked barriers. One performer plays with a big hoop: a bright-eyed Colombian man in his twenties, pink vest, gold shorts, tossing the hoop high, rolling it back to himself, then diving headlong through it and popping to his feet, all within a few metres. Spectators clap from the seating tiers above the track, never on the infield. One continuous shot, playful and upbeat, the camera panning slowly left to right; he stays fully in frame with the concrete visible beneath.

A quarry cutting floor of sawn white marble stretches under flat overcast light, stepped benches glowing faintly, a wire-saw rig parked at the edge, a turquoise pool of rock-flour water in the far corner. One athlete moves across it: a tall Somali woman in her early thirties, close-cropped hair, plum singlet, chalk on her palms, driving a long approach then punching hop, step, jump down twelve metres of stone and landing in a soft dust cloud. The air is completely still and nobody else is in the pit. One continuous shot, dreamy and pale, the camera panning slowly left to right, keeping her fully framed.

Mist softens a brick-paved square in a village outside Rome — a small war memorial, a striped bakery awning just rolling out, plane trees dropping leaves that swirl low across the red pavers. Three adults run double dutch on a single patch: a bouncy Roman woman in a canary tracksuit turning one pair of ropes, a lanky Senegalese man opposite her turning the other, and a compact woman in her forties with a grey buzzcut skipping fast between them, knees snapping, feet barely leaving a metre of brick. Neighbours watch from doorways and a low railing. One continuous shot, cheerful and warm, the camera dollying slowly out; all three stay in frame.

Rain falls lightly on the rolled clay strip at the centre of a sports ground outside Rome; the surface goes mirror-dark between the crease marks, a white sightscreen stands at one end, poplars drip beyond the boundary. Two adults shadow box there, feet never leaving a small square of clay: a lean Argentinian man in a soaked navy vest slipping and rolling under imagined hooks, and a strong-shouldered woman in her forties, hair plastered flat, red shorts, pivoting and firing quick doubles. A scatter of spectators sits under the far stand's roof. One continuous shot, dreamy and silvered, the camera craning down from high above to eye level, both fully framed.

A service strip of compacted red dirt runs between tilted solar panel rows outside Rome, dust haze softening the afternoon into brass, a squat inverter shed humming at the end. Four adults tumble down it in a laughing relay: a springy Japanese-Italian woman in lime leading with cartwheel into round-off, a broad man with a sandy beard chasing her line, a tall Ivorian woman in white linking three round-offs, and a wiry older man finishing with a slow one-handed cartwheel. They cover ten metres of dirt. The air itself hangs motionless and nobody else is on site. One continuous shot, upbeat and sunny, a handheld camera circling slowly at chest height with all four framed.

A disused foundry casting hall outside Rome: packed black sand underfoot, cold ladles hanging from a gantry, shafts of daylight falling through high grimy windows while a failing neon tube flickers and a watchman's beam sweeps the far bay. Three adults shoulder a thick timber log and jog it fifteen metres across the sand — a huge Samoan-Italian man setting the pace, a rope-muscled woman in a cut-off tee gripping the middle, a wiry silver-haired man at the tail — then drop it in one synchronised crash, sand bursting up. Nobody else is inside. One continuous shot, epic and monumental, a handheld camera circling slowly at chest height, all three fully in frame.

Fog drags across a flat black basalt pavement, its ropy stone cracked into plates, and far off over the sea fireworks blossom and fade in muffled colour. Four adults hold one spot: three bases — a broad Nigerian man, a strong pale woman with a blonde plait, a compact Turkish man — lock hands and dip, then launch a slight Filipina flyer in white straight up, arms tight, before catching her clean and setting her back on the rock. All four begin with feet on stone and stay within a metre. Nobody else is out here. One continuous shot, bright and punchy, the camera orbiting slowly around them, everyone fully framed.

Storm light presses down on a freight yard outside Rome, walls of sun-bleached containers forming a corridor, a crooked light mast and a puddled drain at the corner. Three adults own one square of concrete pavers, all three whole in frame, feet planted from the first beat. A tall Ethiopian man in a black waistcoat opens a stomping break — stamp, brush, ball-change — steel taps cracking off the steel walls. A compact Argentine woman in scarlet rides a cramp roll, ankles blurring; a grey-bearded Dutch man answers with rattling stamped riffs. Nobody drifts from their square metre; the air hangs dead before the rain. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly in toward them.

A cove of black volcanic sand below tilted lava stacks near the Roman coast, a bleached driftwood spine half-buried, afternoon haze turning the light bronze and grainy. Three adults play a fierce dodgeball scramble across a few metres of sand: a tall Brazilian woman in a violet swimsuit firing a hard flat throw, a stocky bearded man twisting away and skidding on one knee, and a slim Korean-Italian man in yellow diving full-length, coming up spitting grit and slinging the ball back. Nothing else stirs on the beach and no one else is present. One continuous shot, dreamy and soft-edged, the camera dollying slowly in, all three fully framed.

Fog swallows the apron beside a hangar at an old Roman airfield; faded yellow taxi lines run away into nothing, rubber chocks lie scattered, a mothballed airframe looms as a grey suggestion. Three adults tumble across the painted concrete — a powerful Jamaican-Italian woman in black hurdling into round-off, back handspring, back tuck; a lean man in his thirties with a topknot matching her line; a shorter woman in maroon finishing with a whipped double handspring — covering ten metres. The air is dead still and nobody else is on the field. One continuous shot, cold and noirish, the camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace with all three fully in frame.

A weathered wooden promenade runs above grey surf outside Rome, shuttered kiosks and striped pilings receding under a flat overcast sky while confetti and torn paper scraps tumble through the air from some finished festival. Four dancers attack a long diagonal on the decking: a tall Ethiopian woman in slate leading with grand jeté after grand jeté, a broad Polish man in black cutting a soaring sissonne, a lithe older woman in oxblood, and a young man in white chaining assemblés down twelve metres of planks. Onlookers watch from a railed terrace above. One continuous shot, epic and swelling, the camera dollying slowly in, all four fully framed.

Kernels lie spilled in golden drifts across the dusty concrete slab of a grain silo yard on the plain outside Rome, a rusted auger arm hanging overhead, thick fog erasing everything past the weighbridge, a crooked finish line chalked on the concrete. Four adults race in burlap sacks along it: a rangy Ukrainian man in a black hoodie hopping hard, a compact Ghanaian woman in orange gaining beside him, a heavyset man in a grey shirt going down in a laughing sprawl and scrambling up, a woman with a bleached crop bounding past them all across ten metres. Air motionless; no one else in the yard. The camera dollies slowly inward in one continuous shot, cold and shadowed, all four fully framed.

Storm light presses down on a Roman courtyard floored in patterned ceramic tile, potted lemon trees at the arcade edge, an iron wellhead capped and dry. Six adults each hold a small tile square and dribble hockey balls through tight cone clusters at their feet: a stocky Sardinian man in a red shirt flicking toe-drags, a tall Eritrean woman snapping the ball between her stick blades, a lanky bald man, a woman with a grey plait, a young man in denim, a broad woman in green, sticks clacking. Neighbours lean over the balcony rail above. One continuous shot, gritty and documentary, the camera craning from high overhead down to eye level, all six framed.

A Roman intersection long since given over to pedestrians lies drowned in fog, its asphalt painted with a huge geometric mural gone chalky under steel bollards and dark shuttered shopfronts. Five adults shadow box out on the paint, each rooted to a patch no wider than a doormat: a rangy Senegalese man slipping and countering, a stocky woman in her fifties with cropped white hair pivoting off her back foot, a young Roman man in a soaked hoodie doubling jabs, a tall woman in green rolling under, a bearded man in black weaving low. Nothing else moves; nobody else appears. Craning down from high above to eye level, one continuous shot holds all five in frame.

On a levelled olive terrace above a Roman valley, gnarled trunks stand in rows and a torn tarpaulin snaps hard on its cords in the wind while light rain lacquers the pale earth into a shining skin. Two adults anchor thick battle ropes around a trunk and go to work on one spot: a broad-shouldered Māori woman in a soaked black tank driving alternating waves that spray water off the ropes, and a lean grey-templed man in a wet white shirt slamming both ends down together, mud jumping. No one else is on the hillside. One continuous shot, dreamy and rain-blurred, the camera craning down from high above to eye level, both fully framed.

Midday sun drops straight into a clearing in oak woods outside Rome, packed earth and dry leaf litter blazing between ivy-wrapped trunks, a split log stack at the edge. One athlete works a battered tractor tyre laid flat: a powerfully built Iranian-Italian woman in her thirties, dark braid, blue tank and grey shorts, chalked hands, hauling a sledgehammer overhead and slamming it down, alternating grip, feet planted inside a single metre of ground as leaves jump with each impact. The woods are perfectly still and nobody else is there. One continuous shot, bright and energetic, the camera orbiting slowly around her, keeping her fully in frame.

Golden hour on a firm red sand flat between coastal dunes near Rome; tamarisk clumps bristle on the ridge and fine sand streams low across the ground in long copper ribbons. Three adults throw standing flips without travelling: a compact Algerian man in black snapping a standing back tuck, a tall woman with a blonde undercut punching hers higher and sticking the landing, and a broad man in his forties, grey vest, following with a slow tucked back somersault. Sand bursts from their heels each landing. Nobody else is out on the flat. One continuous shot, low and noirish, the camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, all three fully in frame.

Shafts of daylight fall through the high windows of a Roman gymnastics hall, striking the blue spring carpet floor while thin steam drifts from a wall vent and hangs in the beams; a chalk bowl and stacked mats sit at the edge. One dancer owns a single square metre: a striking Cape Verdean man in his late twenties, cropped bleached hair, silver mesh top and black flares, whipping duckwalk spins into a hard death drop, snapping back up and dropping again, arms slicing. A handful of onlookers watch from the raised viewing balcony behind glass. One continuous shot, bright and punchy, the camera dollying slowly out; he stays fully framed with the floor visible.

A whitewashed cement rooftop above Roman alleys is spread with trays of drying chillies, a rusted water tank at one corner, fog banks rolling in below the parapet while dusty afternoon light turns everything ochre. Three adults train on one small patch of terrace: a sinewy Thai-Italian woman in red shorts driving roundhouse after roundhouse into pads braced by a heavyset bald man who grunts and steps in, while a lean older man in grey feeds a second pad so she pivots and switches legs. Nobody else is up here. One continuous shot, epic and burnished, the camera orbiting slowly around them, all three fully in frame.

A smooth red sandstone bench sits above a sea cliff south of Rome, pocked with rain potholes and scoured bare at the rim, heavy surf breaking white far below. Five adults run shuttles across it under a merciless midday sun: a rangy Kenyan man exploding off a cone and touching down at ten metres, a stocky woman with a black bob turning hard beside him, a bearded man in a soaked grey tee, a tall Vietnamese woman in yellow, a wiry older man last, all reversing, dropping a hand, sprinting back. Nobody else is on the headland. One continuous shot, noirish and hard-shadowed, the camera orbiting slowly, all five framed.

A sawmill yard outside Rome lies under a black shelf of storm cloud, log stacks squared up beside a blade shed, the dirt thick with damp sawdust. Four adults compete shovel to shovel, each planted at their own sand heap: a broad Romanian man in a canvas jacket flinging long arcs, a wiry Eritrean woman in orange gloves working faster and lower, a heavyset man with a red beard, and a woman in her fifties with a grey braid, sand cutting through the heavy motionless air. Nobody else is in the yard. One continuous shot, moody and slate-toned, the camera panning slowly left to right, all four fully in frame.

A convention hall outside Rome sits half struck: grey commercial carpet running to the horizon, bare truss overhead, stacked booth panels and coiled cable at the edges, daylight pouring in hard shafts through the clerestory windows. Four adults hammer burpees, each on their own carpet square: a tall Dominican woman in cobalt dropping flat and exploding upward, a heavy-framed man in black clapping overhead at the top, a lean Japanese man in white cycling fast, and a freckled woman in her forties matching him breath for breath. The air is completely still and nobody else is inside. One continuous shot, bright and energetic, a handheld camera circling slowly at chest height, all four framed.

Warm tungsten work lamps hang low over a curling sheet in a small Roman rink, the pebbled ice glowing amber inside painted house rings, plastic curtains and loose scoresheets fluttering where big fans push dust down the hall. Three adults play broomball in sneakers: a compact Icelandic-Italian woman in a red beanie scrambling after a rubber ball, a broad man in a green hoodie skidding sideways to block, and a lanky bald man swinging his broom and going down hard, sliding a metre before scrambling up. Nobody else is in the rink. One continuous shot, epic and golden, the camera panning slowly left to right, all three fully framed.

Golden hour floods a cracked acrylic hard court on the edge of Rome, the net sagging, a rusted umpire chair leaning, umbrella pines black against the glow while confetti and paper scraps tumble across the paint. Six adults hold their own spots and stickhandle: a tall Icelandic woman in cream flicking a ball between cones, a stocky Roman man toe-dragging fast, a lean Nigerian man in violet, a woman with silver curls, a young man in a mesh vest and a broad woman in denim, blades clicking in rhythm. Nobody else is on the court. One continuous shot, dreamy and honeyed, the camera panning slowly left to right, all six framed.

An enormous tidal sand flat lies exposed near the Roman coast, rippled and wet, stranded mooring posts leaning, a raised causeway crossing the far distance where midday sun turns passing traffic into long glinting streaks. Six adults race in sacks across the sand: a rangy Sudanese woman leading in blue, a heavyset bearded man crashing down and rolling up soaked, a wiry man in red gaining, a woman with a grey crop bounding steadily, and two more thrashing over fifteen metres. Water sheets from every landing. No one else is out on the flat. One continuous shot, cold and noirish, the camera dollying slowly in, all six fully framed.

On a cut limestone bench in an abandoned quarry north of Paris, one continuous shot follows two men. A tall Black man in a soaked charcoal tracksuit and a stocky older white man with grey stubble and a rust-red windbreaker each fold one leg up, fold arms across the chest, and hop into a bump duel, colliding shoulder to shoulder, staggering, recovering, hopping again on compacted rock aggregate that shines with thin rain. Snowflakes drift through the beams of a work lamp near a rusted conveyor and stacked drill rods. A handheld camera circles slowly at chest height. Both stay fully in frame, feet driving the wet stone, the mood inky and neo-noir.

Inside a deserted indoor sprint arena in Paris, blue polyurethane lanes stretch past folded high-jump mats and a coiled timing cable. Four adults stand fully in frame on the track at the start: a lean Vietnamese-French woman in a mustard dress, a broad-shouldered Black man in braces and a white shirt, a freckled redhead woman in teal, and a wiry Middle Eastern man in navy. They swing out, then explode into lindy hop aerials, one partner whipped over a hip and flipped clean to the floor, then the other pair mirrors it with a back-to-back roll. Harsh floodlights rake from one side, the air still. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly out to reveal the empty arena, bright and punchy.

A cavernous aircraft hangar outside Paris: painted grey concrete stretching under a wingless fuselage shell, chain hoists dangling, colored stage lamps and cold neon tubes bleeding magenta and cyan across the floor. Four adults begin fully in frame, feet planted — a tall Somali man in black shorts, a muscular Latina woman with a braid, a pale bearded man in a torn grey tee, a compact Japanese woman in maroon. They break into a running line, flicking a rugby ball backward hand to hand, drifting hard across the hangar, looping the ball down the chain and back again as they cover thirty meters. Air still, no one else present. One continuous shot, camera orbiting slowly, shadows long and neo-noir.

Five adults line up on the grooved asphalt of a closed runway outside Paris, floodlight masts blazing, a limp windsock and a chain of blue edge lights receding into the dark. All five stand fully in frame first: a rangy Kenyan man in orange, a Korean woman in white shorts, a heavy-set white man in grey, a South Asian woman in purple, a silver-haired man in a lime singlet. They crouch, then rip into a flat-out race down the centerline toward a taped finish, arms pumping, spikes rasping, one of them lunging at the line. Snowflakes drift through the floodlight beams. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, cheerful and bright.

Fog banks roll across the pale limestone forecourt of a small Paris museum, past a dry stone fountain and a glass canopy that fade in and out of the murk. Five adults start fully in frame, feet on the limestone: a bald Nigerian man in cobalt, a Portuguese woman with a topknot, a tattooed man in yellow, a Turkish woman in white, a Filipino man in red. They burst into a tight passing line over a few metres, the rugby ball snapping backward through five pairs of hands, resetting, attacking again with a pop pass. Spectators watch from behind a rope line on the steps, never on the stone. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly out across the misty square. Bright, energetic.

Midday glare bakes a fenced court wedged between Parisian housing blocks, chain-link diamonds throwing shadows, a bent rim and a mural of faded blue arcs on the wall. One man stands centre on the painted black asphalt, fully in frame, sneakers planted: lanky, Vietnamese-French, thirties, in a white tank, black cargo trousers, silver rings. He fires a chest hit that ricochets into his shoulder, freezes, then rolls a slow wave from fingertips to fingertips before snapping into stuttered neck ticks and a dime stop. Adult onlookers watch from behind the fence, never on the court. Stray snowflakes drift through the hard light. One continuous shot, a handheld camera circling him slowly at chest height.

Snow piles on the raked red dirt of a floodlit ball diamond in the Paris suburbs, a bent backstop and a shuttered ice-cream kiosk behind it, neon from the ring road flickering while a searchlight sweeps the field. Three adults stand roped ankle-to-ankle at the plate, all three fully in frame, feet down. A tall Haitian woman in yellow calls the count; a short Polish man in green and a lean Korean woman in violet match her, and the bound line lurches into a staggering sprint down the base path, snow spraying. Near the end the woman in yellow surges at the lens, her shoulders passing out of frame. One continuous shot, handheld, circling slowly at chest height.

Red painted tarmac of a Paris cycle expressway glows under pink and green neon signage, steam curling up from grated vents, the ribbed underside of an overpass arching above. Five adults begin fully in frame, feet on the lane: a broad Maghrebi man in black, a tall Dutch woman with cropped blonde hair, a wiry Black man in a yellow crop top, a Brazilian woman in grey, an older Vietnamese man in blue. Two lean hard into resistance bands anchored by partners while the fifth drives a weighted sled, all grinding forward the length of the lane, torsos angled low, feet slapping. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level; nobody else is anywhere in the frame. Soft, floating, dreamlike color.

Blinding midday sun sits over a coastal salt pan, crusted white flats divided by low mud dikes, a wooden rake left standing and a pyramid of harvested salt behind. Three adults stand fully in frame first: a muscular Spanish woman in a cut-off orange shirt, a slim Korean man in rolled linen trousers, a broad Black man with locs in a sky-blue tee. In ankle-deep brine they erupt into a stomp-splash fight, driving heels down to blast sheets of water, scooping kicks, ducking and spinning within a few meters. The air is otherwise perfectly calm. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling slowly at chest height; late on, the Spanish woman lunges at the lens and her shoulder leaves the frame. Bright and punchy.

Rain streaks through an apple orchard outside Paris, splashing puddles between clover and grass, a ladder leaning on a gnarled trunk, crates of fruit darkening in the wet. Six adults stay fully in frame on one patch of turf, feet in the flattened clover: a stocky Ghanaian man in braces, a tall Polish woman in a polka dot dress, a tanned Italian man in white, an Indian woman with a swinging plait, a freckled woman in green, a silver-haired man in denim. In three pairs they hit lindy hop aerials on the spot — swing-out, hip catch, flip over the back, land, repeat — sun blazing through the shower. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace. Playful, saturated, joyful.

Mist hangs low over a green synthetic pitch at a Paris training ground, sagging goal nets and a battered floodlight pylon dissolving into pale sunrise. Two adults stand fully in frame on the turf beside a tractor tire dragged onto the halfway line: a heavy-shouldered Māori-descended woman with a topknot in a black vest, and a slim older Algerian man in a faded grey sweatshirt. They alternate sledgehammer strikes, hauling the head overhead and slamming it down into the rubber, the tire jolting, breath steaming, feet rooted to one spot. The air is dead still. A scattering of spectators sits high in the empty stands beyond the perimeter fence. One continuous shot, static tripod at eye level, soft and dreamlike.

Portable floodlights blaze over a chalky gravel path cutting through a Provençal-style lavender field near Paris, tarpaulins and marker flags snapping violently in the wind, a stone barn dark on the ridge. Three adults stand fully in frame with feet on the gravel: a barrel-chested Samoan man in a black singlet, a rangy Irish woman with a red braid, a shaven-headed Egyptian man in olive. He hoists her across his shoulders in a fireman's carry and sprints thirty meters down the path; at the turn they swap, the woman hauling the third man and driving back, gravel spraying. One continuous shot, the camera craning down from high above to eye level. Vast, heroic, wind-torn; no one else in sight.

Black thunderheads stack over a sunflower field north of Paris, seed heads bowed brown, a rutted farm track and a leaning irrigation pipe marking the edge strip. Five adults toe a scratched line in the dry cracked soil, every one framed head to toe. On a shout they burst away together down the strip: a heavy-thighed Senegalese man in white, a wiry Turkish woman in blue, a freckled Irish man in green, a compact Japanese woman in orange, a grey-templed Spanish man in maroon, all driving hard across the frame and staying inside it. Dust kicks; the air is utterly still. One continuous shot, the camera craning down from high above to eye level as they run.

Light rain glosses the fired clay tiles of a brickyard courtyard near Paris, pallets of stacked bricks and a sagging tarp shelter framing the reflective ground, paper scraps tumbling across it in the gusts. Five adults stand fully in frame, feet on the tile: a broad Dominican man in a yellow jersey, a tall Norwegian woman with a blonde bob, a wiry Indian man in navy, a strong-shouldered Black woman in white, an older Greek man in a grey cap. Each drives repeated bat swings at a ball on a tee, loading the hips, cracking through, resetting and swinging again, spray flying off the barrels. No one else is present. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, crisp and vivid.

A road tunnel under Paris sits closed to traffic, sodium strips buzzing along the asphalt, orange cones and a taped lane running between tiled walls; a stray neon sign at the mouth flickers while a searchlight sweeps the entrance. Four adults are fully in frame, feet on the road: a huge Ivorian man in a red vest, a compact Danish woman in black, a tattooed Latino man in shorts, a tall Kurdish woman with a headband. They squat, grip and hurl a tractor tire over, chasing it a few meters, flipping again, alternating pairs with whoops. Harsh floodlights blast in from one side. No one else is in the tunnel. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly out. Upbeat and bouncy.

Pink and blue light from a distant yard sign washes a freight depot platform outside Paris, its weathered concrete streaked with damp; container stacks and empty flatbed wagons crowd the rails behind, loose tarpaulins and a torn banner whipping in strong wind. One woman holds the platform, fully in frame, feet planted: early thirties, Brazilian, athletic with a high ponytail, a cropped white tee and green shorts, scuffed sneakers. She works a basketball in one spot — hard low crossovers, a snapping between-the-legs series, a behind-the-back wrap and back again, shoulders dropping, ball drumming the concrete. Nobody else appears anywhere. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling slowly at chest height, colors smeared and dreamy.

A dusty wind hazes an open railway platform on the outskirts of Paris, tactile-edged concrete underfoot, a rusted signal post and a peeling timetable board behind; far over the rooftops fireworks burst and fade. Three adults stand fully in frame, feet flat: a slim Roma-French woman in a black ruffled skirt, a grey-bearded Spanish man in a waistcoat, a tall Black woman in deep red. On their own small squares they drive flamenco zapateado — heel-toe bursts hammering the concrete, faster, faster, then a sudden freeze — arms curling overhead in slow braceo, wrists rotating, before another storm of footwork. No one else is on the platform. One continuous shot, slow dolly-in. Grainy, plain, documentary.

Portable floodlights throw hard cones across a wind-packed snowfield outside Paris, fence posts and half-buried hay bales marking the crust; dry leaves and pale petals swirl low over the snow. Five adults stand fully in frame, boots pressed into the surface: a bulky Icelandic man in a red shell, a Tamil woman in a yellow puffer, a lean Black man in grey, a freckled woman with a green beanie, an older Japanese man in navy. Hands clasped, they run a long crack-the-whip, the chain swinging wide and accelerating until the tail runner is slung out across the snow, skidding, laughing, then rejoining as they surge again over open ground. One continuous shot, slow dolly-in. Soft-focus, glowing, hypnotic.

Hard noon light splits a cloister courtyard behind a Paris seminary: arcaded stone walks, a dry octagonal fountain, ivy blackening one pier. Three adults hold the centre of the worn flagstone, all fully in frame with feet down. A broad Samoan man in a black tee and a tall Colombian woman in charcoal lock wrists into a cradle; a small Ukrainian woman in white steps in, dips, and is punched straight up, arms pinned tight, before dropping back into their arms. They set and launch again without shifting off their patch of stone. Shadows cut razor-sharp; nothing else moves. One continuous shot, a handheld camera circling them slowly at chest height.

Golden hour floods a low concrete drying patio behind a roasting workshop on the Paris outskirts, burlap sacks stacked along a wall, wooden rakes leaning, green beans swept into ridges. Five adults hit a wedge formation on the smooth slab, every one fully framed, feet down. A silver-haired Chinese woman in a white crop jacket snaps a knife-edge point; behind her a tall Brazilian man in cobalt, a stocky Danish woman in coral, a lean Indian man in mint and a broad Jamaican woman in lilac catch the same count — chest pop, wrist flick, drop to a knee-brush and up. Nobody travels; the evening air is glassy still. One continuous handheld shot, circling slowly at chest height.

Magenta and cyan wash a small Paris proscenium stage, gilt plaster boxes glowing at the edges, a half-raised velvet drape, a dusty ghost lamp shoved into the wings. Three adults plant themselves on the black plywood deck, all fully in frame, bare feet down. A broad Punjabi-French man in a saffron kurta springs into knee-snapping jumps, arms scissoring overhead; a slim Egyptian woman in emerald pumps shoulder shrugs on the offbeat; a grey-haired Chilean man in indigo drops into deep squat bounces, fists thrown up. They never leave their spot. Seated silhouettes fill the darkened house beyond the stage lip. One continuous shot, the camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace.

Crushed decomposed granite covers a raised park terrace above Paris rooftops, edged by a clipped hedge, a weathered pergola, and a stone balustrade. Under a hard midday sun three adults stand fully in frame, feet in the grit: a compact Japanese-French woman in a lilac tee, a tall Nigerian man in white shorts, a sturdy blond man in a green vest. They swing their arms, load, and fire standing broad jumps forward, landing deep, immediately bounding again in a chain of three or four leaps a few meters across the terrace, gravel skittering, then jogging back to the start line to repeat. Nothing else moves; the terrace is otherwise empty. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling slowly at chest height. Sunny and playful.

Late gold rakes a coal stockyard beside a shuttered Paris-basin plant: black conical heaps, a stalled bucket conveyor, a chalked circle scuffed into the dust. Five adults keep to that circle on the coal-dust ground, all whole in frame, feet planted. A heavyset Georgian man in a grey singlet cranks a rubber training disc through two long preliminary swings, coils, and rips a standing power throw; a tall Kenyan woman in navy answers with a half-turn wind, hips leading, arm trailing. Three more — a stocky Peruvian woman, a bald Finnish man, a broad Vietnamese man — rotate through the circle. Fireworks bloom silently far off. One continuous shot, panning slowly from left to right.

Warm tungsten work lamps hang between the columns of a colonnaded terrazzo arcade in Paris, throwing pools of amber onto the polished floor while paper scraps and torn flyers tumble along the ground. Three adults are fully in frame, feet planted: a lean Vietnamese man in a black tracksuit, a muscular Afro-French woman with a bandana, an older Italian man in a grey hoodie. Each holds a spot and drills power moves — the woman spinning windmills shoulder to shoulder, the young man swinging flares between his hands, the older man dropping into a controlled headspin before freezing on one elbow. Nobody else appears. One continuous shot, the camera craning down from high above to eye level. Deep shadows, brass highlights, noir mood.

A decommissioned turbine hall on the Seine: green casings the size of boats, cable trays overhead, a work floodlight blasting from one side and leaving the far end black. Two adults face off six paces apart on the checker plate steel, both fully in frame, boots down. A wiry Algerian man in a dust-grey vest launches three clubs in flat double spins; a tall Norwegian woman with a shaved head and a red flannel feeds them straight back, stepping in and out to keep the pattern alive. Handles slap palms; nothing else stirs. Near the end she drifts toward the lens until her shoulders leave the frame. One continuous shot, panning slowly left to right.

Soft overcast light flattens a film-studio backlot street outside Paris: painted asphalt pavement between plywood café facades, a lonely lamp post prop, a parked dolly and empty light stands. One woman stands fully in frame at the near end, feet on the pavement — mid-forties, Filipina, compact and strong, black uniform trousers, a white shirt with rolled sleeves, a snare drum slung at her waist. She launches into a marching drumline routine, sticks blurring through rolls and rim accents as she strides the length of the street, snapping crisp pivot turns at the facades and marching back, knees driving. Nothing else moves; the backlot is deserted. One continuous shot, camera craning down from high above to eye level. Cheerful and bouncy.

A storm sky presses low over a flat grey asphalt parade ground near Paris, faded painted formation lines fanning out, a bare flagpole and a long perimeter wall behind; beyond it, distant traffic drags red light trails across the dusk. Four adults stand fully in frame, shoes on the asphalt: a heavy-set Black man in a khaki tee, a lean Ukrainian woman with a bleached crop, a bearded North African man in grey, a tall Chinese woman in a red windbreaker. In two ankle-tied pairs they lurch into three-legged sprints, hips banging, one pair nearly toppling, careering thirty meters across the ground before wheeling back. One continuous shot, camera orbiting slowly. Grainy, unstaged, documentary-plain; no bystanders anywhere.

A cracked white salt crust runs to the horizon under a bruised pre-storm sky outside Paris, broken only by a low dike, an abandoned surveyor's tripod, and pale fireworks bursting far off over the coast. Three adults stand fully in frame, shoes on the crust: a tall Algerian man in white fencing whites, a compact Korean woman in a plastron, a silver-haired Dutch woman in grey. With sport foils they trade bouts — advance, explosive lunge, parry and riposte, retreat — the pair driving each other twenty meters across the flat while the third circles in and takes over the blade, salt puffing under their feet. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level. Nobody else exists here. Soft, floating, dream-lit.

Level minus two of a Paris car park, painted numbers on stubby pillars, a lone strip lamp buzzing above and long shadows pooling on the epoxy-coated concrete. Six adults pair off in a bright, upbeat line, all fully in frame with feet on the floor. A stocky Thai woman in pink wraps snaps a switch-step teep then a rear shin into the pad; her partner, a bearded Russian man, absorbs it and rotates the pad low for a chopping leg kick. Beside them two more pairs — Ivorian, Portuguese, Korean, Australian — hammer the same one-two, each fighter rooted to a single spot. Air is dead calm. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level.

Golden light slides down a Haussmann courtyard's yellow walls: bicycles chained to a rail, a bin alcove, laundry strung across a balcony. Three adults set up on the interlocking pavers, all fully in frame, feet planted. A powerful Cuban woman in a red jersey loads and rips dry swings with a weighted wooden bat, hips snapping open. A wiry Japanese man in white kneels to one side and feeds soft tosses into her barrel; a tall Dutch woman in blue rests a bat on her shoulder, then steps up and lashes ball after ball off a rubber tee into a mesh net. Neighbours lean over balcony rails, watching from above. One continuous shot, static tripod at eye level.

Purple-black cloud stacks over a hotel roof deck near Montparnasse, an infinity pool gone flat as slate, folded umbrellas lashed shut, zinc rooftops falling away behind. Four adults hold squares of light travertine tile, all fully in frame, feet down. A broad Nigerian man in a black rash top rolls under an imagined hook and answers with a short right; opposite him a lean Argentine woman in silver mirrors the slip, pivoting on the ball of her foot. Two more — a grey-haired Vietnamese woman, a freckled Scottish man — shell up, dip, and snap doubles into the heavy air. Guests watch from a glassed terrace above. One continuous shot, static tripod at eye level.

Golden hour pours down a pedestrianized Paris shopping street, granite setts glowing, shuttered awnings and a wrought-iron balcony above, torn festival paper tumbling along the ground. Four adults begin fully in frame, feet on the setts: a tall Black man in loose grey, a sinewy Korean woman in a red practice skirt, a bearded white man in a tank top, a curvy Brazilian woman in blue.
