Five adults own the court, feet on the asphalt and fully in frame: a lanky Thai man in his twenties, red jersey; a strong Black woman near thirty, gold headband; a stocky white man in his forties, white tee; a tall Indonesian woman in green; a grey-templed Latino man in navy. In one continuous shot they attack the rim in waves, driving hard, euro-stepping past a defender and finishing off the glass within a few meters of the paint. A handheld camera slowly circles at chest height. No spectators.

Mist lifts off a riverside ball field on Bangkok's edge, raked red dirt crisp inside a bamboo backstop, air completely still. Six adults spread across the infield, all fully in frame, cleats in the dirt: a beaming Thai woman in her twenties, yellow jersey; a burly Samoan man in his forties; a slight white woman near fifty, grey cap; a tall Kenyan man in orange; a freckled redheaded man in his thirties; a broad Japanese woman in blue. Cheerful and bright, they rotate through windups, firing long throws base to base, then sprinting the length of the diamond to back up the next thrower. One continuous shot, camera panning slowly left to right across the whole field. Nobody watches.

Red painted tarmac of an elevated cycle expressway over a Bangkok canal, closed for the morning, banner poles snapping and loose fabric whipping in strong wind. Soft overcast daylight keeps colors clean and punchy. Three adults occupy the lane, fully in frame with shoes on the tarmac: a rangy white man in his thirties, rolled sleeves and braces; a powerful Thai woman near thirty in a swinging cobalt dress; a compact Black woman in her forties, yellow blouse and saddle shoes. One continuous shot, static tripod camera at eye level, as they trade lindy hop aerials — a swing-out into a hip flip, then a back-to-back toss — landing and recovering within a few meters. Bright, joyful, athletic. No bystanders at all.

Coastal salt evaporation pans near Samut Sakhon: crusted white salt flat cut by narrow dykes, conical salt mounds and abandoned wooden rakes. Misty sunrise, rain streaking down and puddles splashing underfoot, everything shadowed and noir. Four adults stand fully in frame, feet on the crust: a tall Thai man in his thirties, black shirt; a stocky white woman near forty, wet grey hoodie; a lithe Sudanese woman in her twenties, red wrap top; a bearded Turkish man in his fifties, olive coat. Ankles tied in two pairs, they lurch into a stumbling three-legged race, finding rhythm and covering thirty meters of pan, spray flying. One continuous shot as the camera cranes down from high above to eye level. Nobody else.

An experimental apple orchard outside Bangkok: netting frames, windfall fruit, a floor of clover and grass. The sky bruises purple right before rain and fog banks roll between the rows; the look is unpolished, handheld documentary. Four adults stand fully in frame, feet in the clover: a stringy white man in his forties, braces and rolled trousers; a strong Thai woman in her thirties, red skirt; a tall Caribbean man near fifty, grey vest; a compact Korean woman in her twenties, mustard blouse. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace: one couple whips into an over-the-back lindy flip while the other answers with a side flip, both dancers landing light and shifting only a couple of meters. No spectators anywhere.

Improbable heavy snowfall settles on a green synthetic turf pitch by the Chao Phraya, floodlight pylons and blank banners fading into white; the air itself is otherwise calm, dreamlike, desaturated. Three adults begin fully in frame, boots on the turf: a tall Dutch woman in her thirties, blonde bun, cobalt kit; a wiry Thai man near twenty-five in white; a broad Nigerian woman in her forties, crimson sleeves. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly in, as they run a hard pepper drill — bump, set, then a controlled downward hit — shuffling a few meters between contacts. Near the end the woman in cobalt chases a dig toward the lens and ends partly out of frame. Nobody else on or near the pitch.

Harsh midday sun bleaches a chalky gravel path through a coastal lavender research plot near Bangkok, drying racks tilted along one edge and surf breaking loudly beyond the low dune. The mood is hard-shadowed and noir despite the color. Five adults stand fully in frame, feet on the gravel: a lean Thai man in his thirties, black shirt; a broad white woman near fifty, grey braid; a tall Ghanaian woman in her twenties, indigo top; a compact Japanese man in olive; a rangy Latino man in his forties, faded red. Legs in burlap sacks, they hop furiously, collide, tumble and scramble up over a few meters toward a chalk line. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly out to reveal the field. No onlookers.

Light rain slicks the dry cracked soil of a strip at the edge of a Bangkok sunflower trial field, irrigation pipes stacked nearby and a leaning scarecrow frame stripped to bamboo. The wet ground mirrors distant fireworks bursting silently over the horizon — soft, dreamy, unreal. Two adults stand fully in frame, feet rooted in scratched circles: a powerful Polynesian woman in her thirties, purple singlet and black shorts; a tall Egyptian man near forty, shaved head, faded grey tee. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly in, as each winds up, unwinds through a full spinning discus turn and releases with a shout, then resets on the same spot. Nobody else in the field.

A brickworks yard in Bangkok's outskirts, fired clay tiles laid flat as a floor, stacked pallets and a squat kiln chimney behind. Improbable snowfall powders the tiles; the air is otherwise still and the palette pops bright and athletic. Five adults hold their spots, all fully in frame, feet on the clay: a striking Thai person in their twenties, neon-green mesh top; a tall Black woman in her thirties, silver bodysuit; a lean white man near forty, red trousers; a curvy Filipina woman in gold; a broad Brazilian man in his fifties, white tank. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly out, as they snap through hand performance, whip into fast spins and crash into clean death-drop dips, rising in unison. No audience.

A Bangkok road tunnel closed to traffic: asphalt burning orange under sodium lamps, jet fans bolted overhead, blades of daylight falling from high vent windows while neon warning strips flicker and a service searchlight sweeps the tiles. Neo-noir, wet-looking, cavernous. Four adults stand fully in frame, cleats on the asphalt: a tall Black man in his twenties, white gloves and black compression; a strong Thai woman near thirty, red jersey; a stocky white man in his forties, grey hoodie cut off; a rangy Indian woman in navy. One continuous shot as the camera cranes down from high above to eye level; they run deep routes far down the tunnel, breaking hard and hauling in over-the-shoulder catches. Nobody else.

Weathered concrete stretches long along a Bangkok rail freight platform, container stacks on one side, tattered tarpaulins and a rusted loading crane snapping and cracking in strong wind. Misty sunrise turns the depot pastel and dreamlike. Two adults begin fully in frame with feet on the concrete: a compact Thai woman in her twenties, magenta leotard under grey shorts; a tall Ukrainian man near thirty, white tank and black trousers. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level as they sprint long down the platform, hurling round-off back handspring back tucks in sequence, stuck landings echoing. On his final pass he tumbles straight toward the lens and finishes partly out of frame. No bystanders in the depot.

Storm clouds stack over an open commuter railway platform north of Bangkok, tactile-edged concrete underfoot, still hanging fans, a shuttered ticket kiosk and an empty track. The air is dead calm and the light silvery, dreamy. Four adults stand fully in frame, feet on the platform: a slim Thai man in his thirties, blue vest; a tall Norwegian woman near forty, red braid and green trousers; a broad Jamaican man in his twenties, orange shirt; a small Chinese woman in her fifties, purple tunic. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly in, as two pairs pass spinning clubs, weaving crossing patterns and stepping a few meters apart. At the end the orange-shirted man advances until he is partly out of frame.

A manufactured snowfield built for a Bangkok winter festival: crusted wind-packed snow, half-melted ice sculptures, scaffold towers throwing floodlit night glare. Confetti and paper scraps tumble through the beams, and the whole scene reads soft and dreamy, colors bleeding. Three adults stand fully in frame, boots pressed into the snow: a tall Thai woman in her twenties, glittering blue jacket; a wiry Black man near thirty, bare-armed in white; a solid Argentine woman in her forties, red scarf and black leggings. One continuous shot, camera panning slowly left to right, as they spin poi in fast three-beat weaves, adding buzzsaws and full body turns without leaving their footprints. Nobody else is present.

Inside a Bangkok monastery cloister, worn flagstone forms a square courtyard ringed by carved teak eaves, with a bodhi tree shedding leaves that swirl low across the stones under a bruised pre-rain sky. Shadows deepen; the mood is quiet and noir. Three adults stand fully in frame, feet on the flagstone: a shaven-headed Thai man in his forties, grey trousers and singlet; a lean Ethiopian woman in her twenties, ochre top; a stocky white man near fifty, faded black tee. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly in, as two crouch and the third vaults leapfrog over them, then they rotate, chaining vaults over a few meters. Robed adult monks watch from the shaded arcade behind the pillars.

Rain hammers a smooth concrete drying patio at a Bangkok hillside coffee cooperative, tarpaulin racks half-rolled and burlap sacks stacked against a low wall; puddles burst and streak under a black pre-storm sky. Deep shadows and slick reflections give it a noir weight. One adult occupies the slab, fully in frame throughout: a tall Thai woman in her thirties, wet hair slicked back, soaked black leotard over grey tights, bare feet planted on the concrete. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly out to reveal the racks and dripping eaves, as she snaps into a double pirouette, holds, then unleashes a run of fouetté turns, water spraying off her whipping leg, staying on one spot. No one watches.

On the black painted plywood stage of a small Bangkok proscenium theater, faded velvet drapes hang beside half-struck painted flats and an empty orchestra pit yawns below. Low moody practice lamps carve deep shadows; leftover confetti and paper scraps still tumble down from the fly loft, and the tone stays cheerful and bouncy. One adult performs, fully in frame: a compact Vietnamese man in his twenties, dark bob, canary shirt and white trousers, feet on the plywood. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly out to reveal the whole proscenium, as he carves huge ribbon spirals, snaps figure-eights, then adds a split leap and quick turns without leaving his mark. Beyond the pit, an audience watches from the seats.

A raised park terrace above a Bangkok canal, crushed decomposed granite underfoot, banyan roots buckling the planters and strings of festival bulbs glowing neon over the water. Fireworks burst far across the skyline. Colors pop hard and clean. Four adults face off in pairs, fully in frame with shoes in the granite: a huge Thai man in his forties, orange singlet; a powerful white woman near thirty, blonde crop and grey tee; a broad Nigerian man in his twenties, green shorts; a solid Peruvian woman in her fifties, red long-sleeve. One continuous shot, camera slowly orbiting, as they heave weighted sacks chest-high to partners who absorb and heave back, shifting a couple of meters. Onlookers line the railing above, off the terrace.

Blue hour settles over a coal stockyard outside Bangkok, black dust ground stretching between conveyor gantries, coal mounds and squat cooling towers. The air is perfectly still, but the palette is punchy and vivid. Three adults stand fully in frame, shoes in the dust: a rangy Kenyan man in his twenties, white shorts and yellow vest; a strong Thai woman near thirty, teal top; a broad Bulgarian man in his forties, red long-sleeve. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, as they burst into long sprints across the yard, hauling ten-meter streamers that snake and crack behind them, then break into galloping bounds, covering the full width. Nobody else in the yard.

A colonnaded arcade runs beside a Bangkok temple market, terrazzo polished by decades of feet, squat columns painted mint green, steam creeping from a laundry vent between them. Only two work lamps burn, throwing long shadows. Three adults hold their ground: a heavy-built Thai man in a white vest, a tall woman with cornrows in orange, a middle-aged man in loose grey. They hammer heels into the terrazzo on the downbeat, ribcages snapping forward, arms whipping past each other's faces and stopping dead, then a low buck and a sharp shoulder throw. Market shoppers watch from behind the rope line beyond the columns. All three stay fully framed, feet on the stone. One continuous shot, handheld, circling slowly at chest height.

Inside a Bangkok power plant turbine hall, checker plate steel rings underfoot between green turbine casings and an overhead gantry crane. Neon and colored stage lights, rigged for an open day, throw magenta and cyan bars while big fans lift loose paper and dust into the beams. Bright, punchy, sport-ad energy. Three adults start fully in frame, shoes on the steel: a lean Thai man in his twenties, yellow singlet; a muscular Black woman near thirty, white compression top; a broad Greek man in his forties, blue shorts. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, as they burst through shuttle repeats between cones a few meters apart, palms smacking the steel before each hard pivot back. No spectators.

A film studio backlot street outside Bangkok, false shophouse facades with hollow balconies, dressing lamps on stands, painted asphalt pavement scuffed by tire marks. Blue hour after sunset drops everything into cool cinematic depth; the air is dead still. Four adults hold fixed marks, boots on the asphalt and fully in frame: a giant Thai man in his fifties, kilt-cut grey shorts; a powerful Nordic woman in her thirties, blonde plait and black tank; a broad Black man in his twenties, red tee; a heavyset Iranian woman near forty, olive singlet. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, as each squats over a weighted keg and hurls it backward over the shoulder, watching it arc. No bystanders.

Thick fog swallows a coastal military parade ground near Bangkok, flat grey asphalt marked with faded formation lines, an empty reviewing stand and bare flagpoles half-erased, surf crashing unseen beyond the wall. Noir and monochrome. One adult stands fully in frame, spikes on the asphalt: a lean Thai man in his thirties, close-cropped hair, black singlet, white shorts, chalked hands. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level as he rocks, then attacks a long twenty-meter run-up, hits a marked board, hangs, and lands hard in a sand box, sliding forward. His approach carries him toward the lens until the finish leaves him partly out of frame. Nobody else.

Harsh midday sun hammers a cracked white salt crust inland of Bangkok, shallow brine pools glinting and a rusted pump shed shimmering in heat haze. The air hangs completely still; the footage feels raw and unstaged. Three adults stand fully in frame, boots on the crust: a wiry Thai man in his twenties, sun-faded red shirt; a solid Senegalese woman near thirty, green tank and black shorts; a grizzled Spanish man in his fifties, white polo. One continuous shot as the camera cranes down from high above to eye level, catching them juggling a football in a tight ring — instep flicks, thigh taps, headers — keeping the ball airborne without stepping off their spots. No one else for kilometers.

Down on the lowest level of a Bangkok underground car park, epoxy-coated concrete gleams dully between fat pillars, taped bay lines running off into darkness under sparse low practice tubes that leave heavy shadow. Nothing moves in the air. One adult trains alone, fully in frame: a compact Thai woman in her thirties, tied-back black hair, grey sports top, black shorts, chalk on her palms, shoes flat on the epoxy. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly in, as she loads, swings her arms and explodes onto a tall plyo box, sticks the landing, steps down and repeats faster and faster, breath sharp, never leaving her small square. Unvarnished, sweat-real, no spectators anywhere in the garage.

An inner courtyard of a Bangkok apartment block, interlocking concrete pavers ringed by laundry lines that snap and flare in strong wind, a mango tree in a concrete planter and a chipped mosaic wall. Misty sunrise makes the colors clean and bright. Four adults hold a tight circle, sneakers on the pavers and fully in frame: a lean Thai man in his twenties, red tracksuit; a strong Black woman near thirty, denim vest; a wiry white man in his forties, yellow beanie; a compact Malay woman in green. One continuous shot, camera slowly orbiting, as each drops from bouncing toprock into fast six-step footwork and a freeze, staying on one spot. No onlookers.

Fog swallows a hotel rooftop pool deck high over Bangkok, light travertine tile still damp, a drained pool and folded loungers half-visible as fog banks roll through and the skyline appears only as ghosts. Colors stay crisp and energetic. Two adults stand fully in frame, bare feet on the travertine: a muscular Thai woman in her twenties, orange sports top and black shorts; a tall Danish man near thirty, blond crop, white tank. One continuous shot as the camera cranes down from high above to eye level, following them chaining cartwheels into round-offs and side aerials across a few meters of deck, rebounding and repeating in the other direction. Nobody else on the roof.

Granite setts of a pedestrianized shopping street in old Bangkok, floodlit at night by rigged work lamps, shuttered shophouse fronts and unlit paper lanterns hanging overhead, the air completely still. Long hard shadows, deep noir contrast. One adult stands fully in frame, boots on the setts: a huge Thai man in his forties, shaved head, taped wrists, sleeveless black shirt and grey shorts. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly in, as he chalks up, straddles a weighted keg, drops into a deep squat and hurls it backward over his shoulder, then walks a couple of meters to reset and throws again. Spectators watch from behind barriers at the street mouth.

A packed dirt farmyard outside Bangkok, a rusted tin barn with tarps snapping loose in strong wind, a raised water tank and two heaped sand piles. Soft overcast daylight flattens the shadows and gives the whole yard a dreamy, washed calm. Two adults stand fully in frame, boots in the dirt: a broad Thai woman in her forties, headscarf, blue work shirt; a tall Sri Lankan man in his twenties, bare-armed in a white singlet. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly out to reveal the barn and the fields beyond, as they race shovel against shovel, flinging fast bright arcs of sand into wheelbarrows and shuffling a few meters along their piles. Nobody watches.

On the red rubber tartan of a Bangkok university athletics oval, faded lane markings curve past banner poles and a low bleacher. Soft overcast daylight keeps everything friendly and bright, while improbable snowflakes drift down through slanting beams, catching the eye. Two adults stand fully in frame, feet inside marked throwing circles: a powerful Thai woman in her twenties, pink singlet and black shorts, hair in a topknot; a broad Ukrainian man near forty, buzzcut, yellow tee. One continuous shot, the camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, as each swings the discus, winds through a full spinning turn and releases with a grunt, then resets on the same spot. Adult spectators cheer from the bleachers, off the track.

Inside a date-export freezer hall on the Marrakech industrial ring, frost furs the overhead pipes, plastic strip curtains sway, and stacked blue pallets glow under floodlights blasting in from one side. Four adults train on the frosted concrete: a broad-shouldered Moroccan man in his forties wearing an orange thermal jacket, a wiry Senegalese woman in her twenties in teal fleece, a lean Dutch man in his thirties in a grey hoodie, and a compact Filipina woman in a red vest. They trade padded-stick strikes, parry high, duck and shuffle a metre back, breath steaming. Big fans stir loose paper and glittering dust. One continuous shot slowly orbits them; all four stay fully framed, feet planted, nobody else present.

Rain pockmarks a vast gypsum flat south of Marrakech, powdery white sand paling into thick drifting fog past leaning survey posts and salt-crust ridges. Five adults stand fully in frame, feet planted on the grit: a tall Brazilian woman in a yellow crop top, a stocky Korean man in blue shorts, a freckled Irish man in his fifties, a slim Amazigh woman in magenta, a muscular Nigerian woman in white. They settle into prone starts, then explode up on a shout, sprinting eight metres through splashing puddles with rain streaking sideways, and dive full-length for planted flags, skidding grinning through wet sand. One continuous shot pans slowly from left to right, all five staying fully in frame.

A converted badminton hall in Marrakech has been half-taken over by a rigging crew: colored stage lamps and neon tubes flicker over the green vinyl court, searchlights sweep the dead scoreboard, and a battered tractor tire sits alone between faded service lines. Two adults work it. A shaven-headed Egyptian man in his forties, thick forearms, sweat-soaked grey singlet, swings a long sledgehammer overhead and drives it down; a broad Polynesian woman in her thirties, black tank top and taped wrists, alternates from the other side, hips snapping, rubber shuddering. Their feet never leave one small patch of mat. One continuous shot tracks sideways at a steady walking pace. No spectators.

Fog swallows the crest roadway of a dam in the hills above Marrakech, concrete deck striped with faded white lane lines, spillway gates dropping away on one side, floodlight masts fading into grey. Six adults take turns on the cold slab: three women, three men, twenties to forties, in black, rust and pale grey layers, hair braided, shaved or tied back. One cheats forward and snaps a hook kick from a full backside rotation; another swings through into a low twisting layout; a third bounces straight into a scissoring double kick and lands square, each pass covering only two or three metres. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-out revealing more of the dam, all six fully in frame with feet on concrete.

Dusty haze softens a canal-side quay in Marrakech: grey cobble setts polished by years of feet, palm shadows lying long, a low ochre arched bridge downstream. Water sits glassy, the air unmoving. One adult woman, mid-thirties, Japanese, powerful shoulders under a lilac cropped top and charcoal leggings, hair in a tight bun, stands fully in frame on the cobbles, then drops to hands and toes and bear-crawls hard along them, hips low, knees hovering, covering ten metres in fast alternating drives before pivoting and crawling back. Onlookers watch only from the far bank, leaning on an iron railing above the water, never on the quay. One continuous shot orbits slowly around her; she stays fully in frame.

A sealed metro platform under Marrakech never opened to passengers: tiled concrete stretches long and empty, a boarded kiosk peels, and shafts of daylight fall from high clerestory windows into slow steam drifting from floor vents. One adult man, Colombian, late twenties, compact and springy, black long-sleeve top, red shorts, scuffed indoor boots, pushes a scuffed ball the length of the platform. He rolls it, fires step-overs, drags the ball back, cuts hard right, accelerates thirty metres through a bar of pale light, then chops inside again, shoulders dipping. Dust hangs where he passes. One continuous shot orbits slowly around him, tiled ground always visible, nobody else in the tunnel.

Midday sun hammers a barricaded boulevard in Marrakech, bleaching the crosswalk stripes on hot asphalt; ochre walls throw hard shadows, shuttered shop awnings sag, and the air is dead still. One adult woman, Kenyan, early thirties, long limbs, close-cropped hair, emerald tank top and black shorts, chalk on her palms, stands centre-frame with both feet on the road. She whips into a no-hand cartwheel across the white stripes, lands, immediately snaps a front aerial, then a second cartwheel back the other way, never straying beyond a few metres of painted crossing. Sweat flicks in the glare. One continuous shot tracks sideways at a steady walking pace beside her.

A faded grand hotel ballroom in Marrakech: honey parquet under crystal chandeliers, gilt mouldings, tall shuttered doors leaking one bank of harsh floodlight across the floor. Haze-machine fog hangs thick and moving spotlights swing through it. Two adults rehearse under a taut practice net. A tall Serbian woman in her twenties, blonde ponytail, white kit, steps her three-step approach, plants, and swings an arm through a tossed ball with a crack; a stocky Mexican man in his forties, grey shirt, sets and repeats the approach beside her. Guests watch only from the gilt balcony above, never on the parquet. One continuous shot cranes down from high above to eye level.

Floodlights on tall poles wash a train station forecourt in Marrakech, glazing dark basalt setts; a keyhole-arched arcade recedes behind, a dry tiled fountain basin sits centre, night air motionless. Four adults each keep a ball alive on their own square metre of stone: a shaven-headed Algerian man in a white tee, a tall Swedish woman with a red braid, an older Indian man in his fifties in a grey tracksuit, a stocky Haitian woman in orange. Balls snap between hands, crossovers low and vicious, between-the-legs, behind-the-back, double crossovers, all without a step off their spot. One continuous shot dollies slowly out, revealing the wide empty forecourt around them.

Thick fog sits over a short-grass plain outside Marrakech; cropped dry grass runs pale to nowhere, a leaning fence wire ticks, and dry leaves swirl low across the ground. Four adults work in two pairs on the turf. A rangy Somali man in his thirties holds mitts for a stocky Argentine woman with taped hands who fires jab-cross-hook, slipping and resetting; a grey-bearded Turkish man in a faded sweatshirt catches for a young Thai woman throwing doubled hooks and uppercuts. Leather cracks in the damp air. One continuous shot dollies slowly out; after the opening seconds the Argentine woman advances toward the lens and ends partly out of frame.

An open-air festival mainstage stands empty on scrubland outside Marrakech: a wide aluminium deck ringed by scaffold towers, coiled cable, a bare backdrop frame, all softened by dusty hazy afternoon light. The air itself is calm. Two adults, a heavily built Cantonese man in his forties in red silk trousers and a lean Tunisian woman in her twenties in gold, drop into deep crouches, then pounce forward in long low bounds, springing shoulder-to-shoulder across the full width of the deck, landing in stamped stances before pouncing back. One continuous shot tracks sideways at a steady walking pace; late in the take the man bounds toward the lens and ends partly out of frame.

Midday sun flattens a gravel service road threading a refinery outside Marrakech; silver storage tanks curve away, a cold flare stack spikes the sky, a sagging chain fence divides the dust. Nothing stirs but the two adults. A powerful Ghanaian man in his thirties, sleeveless yellow shirt, drives a ball low along the gravel; a tall Russian woman in her twenties, short bleached hair, black kit, chases it down thirty metres, cuts, and lashes a full volley back, both of them crossing the frame in long sprints, gravel spraying at every plant. One continuous shot cranes down from high above to eye level, keeping both fully visible on the road.

Soft overcast daylight over a small beach volleyball court in Marrakech, sand raked into neat lines, net sagging between weathered posts, faded plain banners hanging limp. Paper scraps tumble through the air like slow confetti. One adult woman, Puerto Rican, late twenties, dense shoulders, black braids tied back, purple sports top, grey shorts, bare feet dug into the raked sand, whips a speed rope. She builds tempo, crosses her arms, uncrosses, then rips a string of double-unders, rope hissing, sand puffing under her toes, never leaving her one spot. Onlookers sit only on wooden bleachers beyond the court line. One continuous shot orbits her slowly.

Light rain glazes a white coral sand beach on the Atlantic coast beyond Marrakech; the wet surface mirrors a pearl sky, bleached driftwood posts lean, dune grass beads with water. Four adults stand on their own small circles of sand: a heavyset Samoan man in his thirties, a tall Czech woman with rain-flattened auburn hair, a wiry Sudanese man in a soaked navy shirt, a broad Chilean woman in her forties in grey. Each sinks into a low glide, drives across the shot, torso unwinding, and punches the iron ball out with a shout, feet staying inside their patch. One continuous shot pans slowly from left to right.

Fog hangs motionless between towers of crushed car cubes in a scrap yard on the Marrakech outskirts; oil-stained concrete shines dully, an idle magnet crane sits still, rust dust coats everything. Three adults stand fully in frame along the long clear lane. A rangy Jamaican man in his twenties, red vest, accelerates out of a crouch; a broad Tatar woman in her thirties, blue singlet, runs away from him with an open palm back, takes the baton at full speed, and drives on; a lean Portuguese man in his forties, grey tee, receives the next pass twenty metres later. Spikes clatter across concrete. One continuous shot tracks sideways at a steady walking pace.

Inside a tall church nave in Marrakech's new town, worn stone flagstones stretch between pale plaster piers, and big floor fans push loose paper and grit skating across the floor under flat, even overhead light. Three adults face a chalk line: a huge Moroccan man in a sleeveless grey top, a broad Dutch woman with a blonde plait, a compact Nigerian man in his thirties. Each squats low, hugs a battered sand-filled steel barrel to the chest, then erupts upward and flings it back over one shoulder; it slams the flagstones behind, is rolled forward, and the next lifter sets up. One continuous shot, a slow orbit around them, all three fully framed.

Harsh midday sun bleaches a sandstone-paved forecourt below a tall arched façade in Marrakech; a dry stone basin sits off-centre and dried petals swirl low across the paving. Three adults use the whole square. A broad-chested Māori man in his thirties, white long-sleeve, backpedals a five-step drop, sets, and rifles a spiral twenty metres; a fast Lebanese woman in her twenties, teal shorts, sprints a deep route and hauls it in; a silver-haired Canadian man in his fifties runs the next pattern back the other way. One continuous shot orbits them slowly; near the end the receiver sprints toward the lens and ends partly out of frame.

Floodlights on tripod stands throw hard white pools across a frozen reservoir high in the Atlas above Marrakech; snow dust lies untouched on the ice, dark pines line the shore, tilted marker poles cast long shadows. Night air is dead calm. Two adults face off four metres apart, boots planted on the ice and both fully in frame: a lanky Brazilian man in his twenties in a lime beanie and black shell jacket, and a compact Uzbek woman in her thirties in a scarlet puffer. They pass juggling clubs in fast crossing arcs, stepping half a metre to catch, spinning doubles, sliding, laughing when one club skitters away. One continuous shot dollies slowly out across the bright ice.

Misty sunrise on a flat wave-worn rock shelf on the rocky coast north-west of Marrakech; tide pools glow pink, salt crusts rim the stone, and heavy surf breaks white on the reef behind. Six adults stand fully in frame, ankle-deep in a shallow spread of water on the smooth rock: a tall Norwegian man, a curvy Malian woman in yellow, a wiry Vietnamese man, a red-haired Scottish woman in her forties, a stocky Berber man in a soaked blue shirt, a young Greek woman in white. They stomp huge splashes at one another, sweeping arcs of spray, dodging, chasing a step or two sideways. One continuous shot dollies slowly in toward them.

Night on a beachfront-style promenade in Marrakech, its black-and-white mosaic laid in long rolling waves; neon across the boulevard paints the tiles pink and cyan, palms stand in rows, and fog banks roll through, softening every light into a halo. One adult man, Bulgarian, late thirties, enormous through the back and shoulders, shaved head, sleeveless charcoal top, stands alone on the mosaic. He rocks, winds the discus far behind him, then spirals through a low turn on the balls of his feet and releases with a roar, staying inside his small circle of tile. One continuous shot pans slowly from left to right.

Hard noon sun bakes a rooftop helipad above Marrakech: a painted white circle on grey concrete, antenna masts bristling at the parapet, torn paper scraps tumbling upward on the thermals. Six adults grip a thick rope in two teams of three. On one side a burly Croatian man in his forties, a compact Zulu woman in yellow, a bearded Bangladeshi man in grey; opposite, a tall Argentine woman with sleeve tattoos, a lean Korean man in black, a broad Irish woman in her fifties. They heave, boots skidding a metre across the paint, one team dropping to a knee, then collapsing backward in a knot. One continuous shot orbits slowly around them.

An idle car assembly floor outside Marrakech runs long under bright even overhead lighting: epoxy-coated concrete, dormant yellow robot arms folded at their cells, unpainted body shells hanging motionless from an overhead conveyor. Nothing moves in the air. Three adults work a marked lane a few metres long. A thickset Moroccan man in his thirties, grease-smeared white tee, squats, grips a tractor tire and drives it over with a grunt; a tall Ukrainian woman with cropped platinum hair flips it back; a stocky Filipino man in his forties chalks his hands and takes the next. Rubber slams flat on concrete. One continuous shot tracks sideways at a steady walking pace.

Under a glass canopy of pale steel ribs, a small transit plaza in Marrakech sits closed for the night; grey porcelain tile stretches between dark ticket gates, and floodlights outside blast in from one side, striping everything with hard shadow. The air is still. Six adults, wooden practice staffs in hand, hold a loose ring: a lean Tibetan man in maroon, a tall Ghanaian woman in white, a grey-bearded Spanish man, a muscular Indonesian woman in green, a young Danish man in black, a stocky Egyptian woman in orange. Staffs blur in figure-eights, roll across shoulders, flick up in tosses and snap back as they step a metre in and out of the ring, trading spins. One continuous shot orbits them slowly.

Misty sunrise on the weather deck of a cargo ship off the Moroccan coast: painted steel plate underfoot streaked with salt, container stacks lashed in rows, mooring bitts wet with dew, swell breaking white far off the rail. Two adults train in a clear bay of deck. A rangy Cuban man in his thirties, bare-chested under an open grey hoodie, and a broad-shouldered Filipina woman in her forties in a navy rash top, circle one another within a few metres, throwing air combinations, slipping imagined counters, rolling under, pivoting off the lead foot, exhaling sharply. One continuous shot dollies slowly in toward them; both stay fully in frame.

A small fight club in Marrakech has turned its octagon into a stage: colored lamps and neon tubes flicker over the vinyl-covered mat, searchlights sweep the chain-link, and cheap tiered seating rings the cage. One adult man, Nigerian-French, late twenties, springy and lean, gold tee, baggy cream trousers, headband, bounces through toprock across the mat, then drops his hands and swings into six-step footwork, knees carving circles, shoulders low, before popping back up. Spectators watch only from the seats outside the fence. One continuous shot orbits him slowly; in the final seconds he dances toward the lens and ends partly out of frame.

A city ice rink in Marrakech, borrowed for a rehearsal: white ice over faded painted lines, scuffed dasher boards, colored stage lamps and neon washing the surface pink and violet. The air hangs still. Two adults skate a few metres of clean ice. A slight Kazakh woman in her twenties, black practice dress, hair in a knot, sets an edge, snaps into a tight double and lands with the trailing leg extended; a tall Estonian man in his thirties, grey shirt and gloves, mirrors her, jumping, checking out, spraying ice on the landing. Spectators sit only in the stands behind the boards. One continuous shot dollies slowly out.

Night settles on a herringbone brick plaza outside a Marrakech university library, its glass frontage throwing red and blue neon spill across the bricks, palms motionless, a dry planter box at the edge. Four adults in hard-soled shoes hold a tight square: a slender Amazigh woman in a gold jacket, a stocky Korean man in denim, a tall woman with grey curls, a young man in a teal tracksuit. They rap out a shuffle-ball-change, drop into a rattling pull-back, then answer each other with paddle-and-roll runs before a single flapping wing lands them exactly where they began. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, all four fully framed on the brick.

Daylight drives in through high dusty windows of an old Marrakech roller rink, laying bright bars across the glossy maple oval; faded wall murals peel, a dead disco ball hangs, skates sit unrented on a rack. Nothing moves but one adult man, Punjabi, mid-thirties, stocky and powerful, embroidered orange kurta over black joggers, bare feet gripping the wood. He bounds into high bhangra hops, arms thrown overhead, shoulders bouncing, then sinks into squat kicks, snapping one leg out then the other, travelling a couple of metres and springing back. One continuous shot dollies slowly in toward him, polished floor always visible beneath.

Low practice lamps leave most of an indoor pool hall in Marrakech in shadow, catching only wet-looking non-slip ceramic tile, motionless lane ropes and the flat black water beyond. Two adults hold one spot on the deck. A tall Turkish woman in her thirties, shaved sides, red shorts and shin guards, whips roundhouse kicks into Thai pads braced by a squat Brazilian man in his forties, grey beard, sleeveless black top; he absorbs, turns the pads, and she switches stance and kicks again, hip rolling through, the crack echoing off tile. Swim-club members watch from a glass gallery above the deck. One continuous handheld shot circles slowly at chest height.

Golden hour floods a desert race circuit outside Marrakech; the pit lane's striped tarmac glows amber, shuttered garage doors run in a long row, and searchlights swing lazily overhead with a neon gantry stuttering at the far end. One adult woman, Ethiopian, early thirties, whip-thin but heavily muscled, cobalt crop top, black tights, hair braided tight, sets her hands on a loaded sled. She drives it forward in short violent strides, spine flat, sled grinding, and pushes it twenty-five metres down the painted stripes before easing off, chest heaving. One continuous shot cranes down from high above to eye level, keeping her fully framed on the tarmac.

A cavernous sound stage on the edge of Marrakech: matte black floor, a half-struck plaster set pushed to one wall, cable looms taped down, steam drifting from a floor vent through two dim practice lamps. Four adults in mismatched training kit — a rangy Moroccan woman in purple, a heavy-thighed Ghanaian man, a pale redhead in a cut-off hoodie, a wiry man in his forties — begin fully framed, feet on the black floor, then pound down a chalked lane in single file, driving alternating single-leg bounds, five per side, into a long final stride and a two-foot landing on a crash mat. One continuous shot, the camera tracking sideways at walking pace; the last runner surges past it and ends partly out of frame.

Warm tungsten work lamps stand on tripods in a courthouse great hall in Marrakech, throwing amber light across checkerboard marble between fluted columns and tall shuttered doors. The air is perfectly still. Six adults in bright mismatched kit spread across the floor: a wiry Dutch man in orange, a stocky Rwandan woman in green, a bearded Iranian man in white, a tall Australian woman with a red bandana, a young Peruvian man in blue, a silver-haired French woman in her fifties. A disc floats out; two of them sprint three metres and lay out full-length, skidding on polished marble, others cut and reset. One continuous handheld shot circles slowly at chest height.

Blue hour over a grey gravel outwash plain below the Atlas beyond Marrakech; braided meltwater channels gleam faintly, boulders sit scattered, and far off a highway draws thin streaks of headlight trails across the dusk. One adult woman, Norwegian, early thirties, tall and rangy, white long-sleeve top, navy shorts, hair whipping loose, carries a javelin above her shoulder. She builds a long approach across the gravel, folds into crossover steps, plants hard and unleashes the throw with a shout that carries. One continuous shot cranes down from high above to eye level; as she finishes she strides toward the lens and ends partly out of frame.

Soft overcast light over a skatepark on the edge of Marrakech: smooth cast concrete flat bottom, a scarred bowl lip, painted coping, a chain fence beyond which distant traffic drags long light trails through the gloom. Boards lie abandoned by the rail. One adult man, Ivorian, mid-twenties, slight and quick, faded green tee, red shorts, one sock rolled down, keeps a scuffed ball airborne on a single square of concrete. He flicks it foot to foot, catches it on a thigh, nods it twice off his forehead, rolls it around his neck and drops it back to the laces. One continuous shot tracks sideways at a steady walking pace.

A small boxing gym in Marrakech lit bright and even overhead; the canvas mat inside the taped ropes is chalked and scuffed, haze-machine fog hangs low and two moving spotlights sweep across it. Three adults train inside the ring. A broad Nigerian man in his thirties, gold shorts; a lean Moldovan woman in her twenties, black crop top; a compact Mexican man in his forties, grey singlet. Small cones sit at the corners; they explode two metres, slap the canvas, spin and sprint back, cutting hard, shoes squeaking, chests heaving. Members watch from folding chairs outside the ropes. One continuous handheld shot circles slowly at chest height.

Rows of silent looms fill a textile mill hall on the Marrakech industrial edge; warm tungsten work lamps hang low over a worn wooden plank floor and big fans push lint, dust and loose paper through the beams in slow glittering drifts. Two adults train in an aisle. A stocky Kyrgyz man in his forties, grey vest, holds two hand paddles high; a tall Trinidadian woman in her twenties, black uniform trousers and a red belt, retreats two steps, then bounds up into a flying front kick that cracks the paddle, lands, resets and launches a spinning one. Boards boom underfoot. One continuous handheld shot circles slowly at chest height.

Misty sunrise filters green through a dense bamboo grove behind a walled Marrakech garden; packed earth is strewn with dry curled leaves and pale light slants in bars between motionless stems. The air is windless and quiet. One adult woman, Filipina, late twenties, athletic, silver bomber jacket over a black bodysuit, white sneakers, stands on a small clear patch of earth. She snaps sharp robotic hits through her chest and shoulders, freezes, then rolls a smooth wave from fingertips to fingertips, dime-stops, and glides a half-step without leaving her spot. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level keeps her fully in frame, feet on the leaf-strewn earth.

A school basketball court in Marrakech has been rigged like a club: neon tubes and colored stage lamps saturate the polished maple, haze-machine fog thickens the beams and spotlights swing across the painted keys. Five adults spread over the hardwood. A tall Korean man in white dobok trousers, a muscular Cameroonian woman in a black crop top, a lean Iranian man in grey, a compact Swedish woman with a bleached buzzcut, a broad Bolivian man in his forties. Each pivots, whips a spinning hook kick through the haze, resets, then fires a back kick, drifting only a metre or two. Nobody else is present. One continuous take holds all five fully framed on the maple, filmed from a static tripod at eye level.

A bruised storm sky presses on a granite civic plaza in Marrakech; polished pavers hold a dull sheen, a dry bronze fountain sits off to one side, and low fog banks roll across the square as the first wind picks up. Four adults work a stretch of stone: a springy Malagasy man in his twenties, a tall Ukrainian woman in white, a stocky Egyptian man in a red vest, a slim Colombian woman with a long braid. They chain no-hand cartwheels into front aerials, landing in unison, resetting a metre back, hair snapping. Onlookers stay behind steel railings at the plaza edge. One continuous shot tracks sideways at a steady walking pace.

Bright even overhead lighting fills a steel mill rolling floor outside Marrakech: heavy steel plate underfoot, idle roller tables stretching away, a gantry crane parked overhead, cooled slabs stacked at the wall. Nothing in the air moves. Four adults each claim a plate: a lanky Senegalese man in a white tee and cargo pants, a stocky Vietnamese woman in a red boilersuit tied at the waist, a grey-templed Greek man in his fifties in black, a broad Māori woman in denim. They punch robotic hits through their chests, freeze, run arm waves across the line, tick their heads, and dime-stop, never shifting off their steel. One continuous handheld shot circles slowly at chest height.

A long gallery hall in Barcelona, pale oak planks underfoot, tall white walls hung with big abstract canvases, a velvet rope stanchion pushed aside. Even ceiling light falls without shadow; the air is perfectly still. Two adults in dark uniform trousers carry snares slung at the hip: a broad Catalan man in his fifties with a grey ponytail, and a tall Somali woman with close-cropped hair. They trade a rolling cadence, march eight crisp steps forward, snap a sharp about-face on the ball of the foot, and stride back, sticks flashing into buzz rolls and rimshots. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-out revealing more of the hall, both fully framed.

Light rain glazes the stamped concrete of a concourse plaza wrapping a Barcelona stadium, steel ramps overhead, ticket booths shuttered, puddles holding the grey sky. Three adults keep a ball alive: a tall Catalan woman with a red bun in a white tee digs low, a stocky Japanese man in his forties sets a clean high ball, and a lean Senegalese man in orange takes three quick approach steps, jumps and swings, cracking it down so it skids off the wet slab. They rotate roles and go again, laughing. Fans watch from the ramp balcony behind railings, none on the plaza. One continuous shot, handheld, circling slowly at chest height, all three stay fully framed throughout.

Mist hangs over a crushed red-brick clay court on a Barcelona hillside, its net sagging, a black cypress hedge behind, chalk lines half-erased. Two adults circle there and nobody else. A wiry Moroccan man in his late twenties, taped hands, charcoal shorts, faces a broad-shouldered Slavic woman around forty in a faded oxblood vest, both in worn gloves. They spar hard: doubled jabs, a slip under a hook, a rolling counter to the body, pivots kicking small ochre clouds from the clay, footwork carrying them only a couple of metres either way. Sunrise light comes low and grey; the air itself is dead still. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly in, both fighters fully framed, feet on the packed clay throughout.

Snowflakes drift improbably through hard midday sunbeams above a close-mown grass tennis lawn behind a Barcelona sports club, a weathered wooden umpire chair and low ivy wall framing the turf. Six adults stand in a loose arc: a tall Somali woman with box braids in cobalt, a silver-haired Catalan man in ochre, a stocky Japanese woman in white, a lean Brazilian man in scarlet, a red-bearded man in denim, a Tamil woman in emerald. Each holds a metre-wide spot, ticking isolations, strobing through stutters, flicking a wave shoulder to shoulder, then locking a freeze, knees flexing on the grass. Spectators watch from bleachers beyond the fence. One continuous shot, epic and wide, the camera dollying slowly out to reveal the lawn.

Blue-hour dusk over a broad concrete esplanade beside a Barcelona river channel, a rusted crane gantry looming and snowflakes turning through the lamp beams. Two adults hold the empty slabs. A tall Ethiopian man about thirty-five in a black thermal fires a hard flat throw; a compact Vietnamese-Spanish woman near forty-five, ponytail, teal jacket, twists her hips away, snatches the rebound and whips it back, then dives sideways along the concrete, rolls up and fires again from her knees. They cover only a few metres. No one else is around. One continuous shot, the camera craning down from high above to eye level, both figures fully in frame with feet on the visible concrete. Epic, cold, cinematic.

Thick fog hangs low and unmoving over the mown lawn of a Barcelona tech campus, a glass atrium glowing faintly and a rust-steel sculpture half-swallowed by white, a strip of tape marking a finish. Three adults race in canvas sacks: a broad Māori man in his forties, sleeves cut off, a lanky Danish woman about thirty in yellow, and a compact Ecuadorian man near fifty in navy. They bound hard across the grass, sacks slapping wet blades, one stumbling and tumbling shoulder-first before scrambling upright, all three crossing the tape metres from where they started. Colleagues cheer from a raised terrace behind a railing. Bright, energetic and clean. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly out to reveal the wide foggy quad, everyone fully framed.

A small squash court under a Barcelona sports club has been emptied and hazed: pale hardwood scuffed with black shoe streaks, glass back wall fogged, warm tungsten work lamps clamped to the tin. Fog drifts and two spotlights sweep slowly across the walls. One adult performs alone — a Punjabi man in his early thirties, lean, long hair tied back, wearing a loose plum shirt and grey trousers, spinning tethered practice poi with weighted fabric heads. He drives a fast three-beat weave, folds into a body turn, snaps into butterflies, tracing luminous circles while his feet shift only a metre. Dreamy, saturated, slightly unreal. One continuous shot, the camera panning slowly left to right, keeping him fully in frame with feet on the wood.

Rain has just passed over a stretch of short golden grassland beyond Barcelona's outskirts, the ground glossy and reflective, a lone carob tree and a crumbling stone wall dark against grey. Three adults train here and no one else. A heavyset Turkish man near forty in a soaked singlet, a rangy Kenyan woman about twenty-eight in navy, and a pale Polish man in his thirties take turns: a low penetration step, hands locking behind a knee, the drive lifting and turning the partner down into wet grass, the third sprawling flat then rotating back to feet. Movement stays inside a few metres. Air perfectly still, colours bruised and noir. One continuous shot, the camera craning from high above down to eye level.

Where two farm tracks meet outside Barcelona, packed grey gravel spreads under a leaning signpost stripped of its plates, bare plane trees on one side, a rusted irrigation valve on the other. Snowflakes sift through weak shafts of overcast light. Two adults dance: a Colombian woman in her late thirties in a wine-red wrap dress and low heels, and a tall Greek man about fifty in a charcoal shirt, cuffs rolled. He leads a cross-body pass, spins her twice under his hand, catches her waist, sends her out into a double turn and reels her back, shoes grinding arcs into the gravel within a few metres. Shadowed, smoky, noir-toned. One continuous shot, the camera panning slowly left to right, both fully framed.

An emptied distribution warehouse on Barcelona's industrial edge: polished concrete running the length of a long aisle between towering bare racks, tall windows throwing hard dusty shafts across the floor while big fans stir loose paper and grit into the light. Two adults work the aisle — a burly Samoan man in his mid-thirties in a torn training top and a lean Afro-Cuban woman near thirty with shaved sides, both in shorts and tape. They sprint side by side down the length of the shot, flicking a rugby ball backwards in flat lateral passes, hands soft, feet slapping concrete, covering many metres before turning back. No one else. Gritty, documentary texture. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly in, both fully in frame.

A ballet rehearsal room above a Barcelona courtyard, black marley floor, barres along one wall, a stacked pile of folding chairs in the corner; only two low practice lamps are on, carving deep shadow. One adult stands centre: a muscular woman in her thirties, brown skin, hair in a high knot, magenta leotard over black leggings, hard-soled shoes laced tight. She rips a heel-drop riff, folds it into a fast cramp roll, then stamp-brush-stamp bursts that rattle like hail on tin, arms loose, never leaving her square of vinyl. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, she stays fully in frame, feet on the floor.

Beneath a Barcelona hillside, a wartime bunker hall opens into damp bare concrete under low arched vaults, cable spools shoved aside and tungsten work lamps strung along one wall. Paper scraps tumble through the warm light. Three adults run it: a tall Ghanaian woman about twenty-six in canary yellow, a wiry Basque man in his thirties in white, and a broad Indonesian man near forty-five in blue. Sprinting flat out down the vault, the first slaps a baton up into the second's open palm, who accelerates away and feeds the third at full speed, all three covering the length of the hall. Bright, cheerful, kinetic energy in a grim space. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly out to reveal the vaulted hall.

A small neighbourhood judo dojo in Barcelona: green tatami mats butted edge to edge, a rack of folded gis, and tall clerestory windows spilling hard shafts of daylight across the room. The air is completely still. One adult trains — a heavyset Egyptian man in his late thirties, shaved head, taped fingers, in a grey vest and worn white trousers. He hoists a sand-filled medicine ball overhead, arches, then hammers it down into the tatami, catches the low bounce, and repeats, breath ragged, feet never leaving one square metre. A handful of club members watch from the balcony railing above, none on the mats. Raw, unpolished documentary feel. One continuous shot, the camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, keeping him fully framed.

An off-season ice rink in Barcelona sits drained to its painted concrete slab, scuffed dasher boards and empty plastic seats ringing it, a scoreboard dark overhead. Harsh floodlights blaze from one side only, throwing a long crisp shadow. The air is dead still and nobody else is inside. A single adult works the slab: a compact Mexican woman around thirty with a dark braid, in a hot-pink leotard and orange shorts, chalk on her palms. She snaps a cartwheel, links straight into a second, then punches a round-off and rebounds into another chain, travelling a few metres and bounding back. Cheerful, saturated, commercial energy. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly in, her whole body in frame and feet returning to the concrete.

A municipal bus depot parking hall in Barcelona stands empty overnight: asphalt marked with faded yellow bay stripes, idle fuel pumps against the far wall, a single bus door hanging open. Low practice lamps carve deep shadows and the air does not stir. Two adults own one bay each: a lean Dominican man in his twenties in a white tee and cargo pants, and a muscular Uzbek woman near thirty-five with a bandana, in green. He drops into windmills, hips whipping, then kicks into flares before spearing up into a headspin; she mirrors with a swipe combo and a freeze, both anchored to a metre-wide patch. Gritty, grainy, unglamorous. One continuous shot, camera panning slowly left to right, both fully framed.

Heavy snow falls across a deserted surface parking lot on Barcelona's outskirts, faded asphalt showing through in patches, a chain-link fence rattling and a torn banner snapping hard in the wind. Three adults train with hockey sticks and a hard ball: a stocky Finnish woman in her forties in a red beanie, a tall Haitian man about twenty-eight in black, and a slight Chinese man near thirty-five in grey. Each stays on one small patch, rattling the ball side to side through a tight cone gate, toe-dragging, pulling it back between their feet, shoulders faking hard. Nobody else in sight. Gritty documentary grain. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly out to reveal the wide white lot, all three fully framed.

Fine grey ash spreads flat on a volcanic plain inland from Barcelona, a low cinder cone behind and a line of surveyor's flags whipping violently in the wind, ash streaming off their poles. Four adults train, each on one spot: a broad Icelandic man about forty in orange, a lean Kenyan-Spanish woman near twenty-seven in white, a tanned Argentinian woman in her thirties in teal, and a heavyset Korean man in yellow. Each swings a ball wide across the body and whips it down at an angle, ash bursting in grey plumes, then lunges, scoops and fires again. Harsh midday sun bleaches everything; nobody else is here. One continuous shot, camera craning down from high to eye level, all four fully framed.

An empty football stadium outside Barcelona bakes under harsh midday sun, striped natural grass burnt at the edges, low dust skating across the turf, tiers of dark seats and a broken corner floodlight above. Five adults hold the pitch: a tall Congolese woman about thirty, a rangy Serbian man in his forties, a stocky Peruvian woman near twenty-five, a bald Dutch man, and a wiry Thai man, all in mismatched training kit. Gripping hands in a chain, they sprint into a widening arc, the anchor braking hard so the whip cracks and flings the tail runner sprinting away across the grass, arms wheeling. They cover long ground, all five staying fully in frame. Shadow-heavy, desaturated noir. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly out.

A crossfit box in a Barcelona warehouse unit, black rubber tiles underfoot, chalk bins and stacked bumper plates pushed to the walls, big floor fans dragging dust and loose tape scraps through bright even overhead light. Five adults take the open floor: a broad Algerian man in his thirties, a tall Swedish woman near forty with a blonde plait, a compact Nigerian-Catalan woman about twenty-five, a stringy Chilean man, and a heavy-armed Georgian man. One after another they whip no-hand cartwheels across the tiles, land clean and punch straight into front aerials, a few metres of travel each. Nobody else is inside. Grainy, honest, documentary. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, all five fully framed with feet down.

Snow pours into a shipyard dry dock near Barcelona's port, its wet concrete floor black and streaked, keel blocks and a rust-streaked bow towering at the far end. Neon strip signage flickers on a service shed while a searchlight sweeps across the basin. Two adults train and no one else: a huge Tongan man near thirty-five in a soaked navy hoodie and a lean Somali-Italian woman about forty-two in silver, both harnessed to thick resistance bands anchored to a bollard. Leaning far forward, they drive their knees hard, grinding metre after metre up the dock floor before the bands haul them back. Cold, high-contrast, noir. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, both fully in frame.

Fog swallows a wide firm beach north of Barcelona; packed damp sand runs flat to a barely visible stone breakwater, rain streaking down and hammering shallow puddles into splashing rings, a lone wrecked mooring post canted in the mist. One adult is out there — a broad Brazilian man in his early forties, close-cropped grey hair, in a soaked slate rash top and black shorts. He drives three sprinting strides, launches headfirst and belly-flops flat onto the wet sand, skidding forward with a sheet of spray, then scrambles up and repeats a couple of metres over. Vast, grey and cinematic. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, keeping him fully in frame and his feet on the visible sand.

Blue-hour light lingers over a vineyard on Barcelona's inland slopes, a wide tractor row of compacted soil running between trellised vines, a stone mas with one lit window and a stack of crates at the row's end. The air is still. Six adults line up on hands and feet: a tall Croatian man about forty-five, a compact Ivorian woman near thirty, a wiry Japanese-Spanish man, a strong-shouldered Romanian woman, a bearded Portuguese man, and a lean Sri Lankan woman, all in dark training kit. They explode into a bear-crawl race, hips low, palms slapping soil, hauling themselves the length of the row and kicking up dust. Cool, shadowed, noir. One continuous shot, the camera craning down from high above to eye level.

A sunken plaza in Barcelona's bank district, floored in black granite, glass towers rising on three sides, a dry stepped fountain and a stalled revolving door catching the last light before a storm. Bruised clouds mass overhead yet the air hangs motionless. One adult works there: a powerfully built Puerto Rican woman in her mid-thirties, curls tied back, in a citrus-yellow tank, black leggings and gloves, standing over a battered tractor tyre with a long sledgehammer. She winds it high, drops her hips and smashes the rubber, bounces the recoil, switches hands and swings again, never leaving her single square of granite. Office workers watch from a railed balcony above. Bright, punchy, upbeat. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace.

Deep in an unfinished Barcelona metro tunnel, raw grey shotcrete forms the floor, a fat yellow ventilation duct runs overhead and tungsten work lamps hang on cables while fans push dust and torn wrapping through the beams. Four adults fence with blunt sport foils, masks on: a tall Hungarian man in his forties, a compact Zimbabwean woman about twenty-eight, a stocky Catalan woman near fifty, and a lean Filipino-French man. In two bouts they drive long lunges, retreat, parry and riposte, advancing and giving ground many metres along the tunnel floor, blades ringing. No one else is present. Grimy documentary tone. One continuous shot, the camera orbiting slowly around the fencers, all four fully in frame with feet on the shotcrete.

Inside a harbour fabrication shed in Barcelona, the rust-stained steel plate floor runs flat under banks of even white lamps; a half-built ferry's rib cage fills the far end, green welding curtains hang in a row, a rolling scaffold tower sits parked. One adult owns the space: a broad-chested man in his thirties, tan skin, black curls, red hoodie sleeves shoved up, grey shorts. He backpedals seven quick steps, plants, and rifles a tight spiral thirty metres down the shed into a hanging net, then jogs to a new mark and repeats, sliding sideways before the throw. He stays fully in frame, boots on steel. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-out revealing more of the shed.

A fencing hall in a Barcelona sports centre, a metallic piste strip laid over dark rubber flooring, faded club banners and a rack of masks along one wall. Warm tungsten lamps glow while a flickering neon sign outside and a slow searchlight beam rake through the high windows. Three adults play with a flying disc: a rangy Angolan man about twenty-seven in maroon, a strong Ukrainian woman in her thirties in white, and a short Bolivian man near forty-five in grey. One flings a low disc, another sprints two steps and lays out horizontally, catching it inches above the rubber before sliding and popping up. Club members watch from a railed mezzanine. Moody noir. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly out.

A stone barn outside Barcelona has been cleared for training: wide plank wood underfoot polished by years of use, hay bales stacked to one side, a heavy tarpaulin hung across the far doorway as a goal. Bright even lamps hang from the beams and nothing in the room stirs. Five adults work the floor: a broad Senegalese man near thirty-five, a lean Bosnian woman about twenty-four, a greying Andalusian man in his fifties, a tall German woman, and a compact Vietnamese man. They feed each other crosses and hammer power shots, one meeting a waist-high ball with a full volley that cracks into the tarp, all inside a few metres. Gritty documentary grain. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly in.

An abandoned brick factory hall on Barcelona's edge stretches long and empty, broken brick tiles underfoot, two dead kiln mouths gaping in the far wall and painted steel columns marching down the middle. Bright even lighting fills the hall and the air is perfectly still. Six adults play: a tall Cape Verdean woman about thirty in pink, a barrel-chested Russian man in green, a slim Malaysian woman near twenty-five, a bearded Italian man in his forties, a freckled Scottish woman, and a wiry Peruvian man. They burst into flat-out sprints down the hall, then freeze mid-stride, wobbling absurdly, before exploding forward again across many metres. Nobody else. Playful, bouncy, upbeat. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level.

A circular flagstone threshing floor sits on a headland north of Barcelona, its ringing wall half-collapsed, a wind-bent fig tree at the edge and heavy surf crashing on the rocks below in the misty sunrise. One adult performs: a tall Kurdish woman around thirty-five, dark hair loose, in a slate cropped jacket, wide black trousers and bare feet, working a large wooden hoop. She flings it out, lets it roll back to her with backspin, then dives clean through it and rolls up onto the stone, repeating a couple of metres over. For the first seconds she is fully framed, feet on the flagstones; then she steps toward the lens and finishes partly out of frame. One continuous shot, static tripod.

On a flat mesa top of hardpan and sparse scrub, a sheer cliff edge drops away and fog banks roll steadily across the plateau while harsh midday sun burns overhead. Five adults train, no one else in sight: a heavy-shouldered Bulgarian man near forty holding mitts for a lean Ghanaian woman about twenty-six; a grey-templed Chilean woman with pads for a wiry Pakistani man in his thirties; and a tall Norwegian woman shadow-drilling beside them. Gloves crack into leather in fast one-two-hook-cross combinations, elbows tight, feet pivoting on the same patch of dirt, dust puffing under each turn. Sweat, squints, no polish — pure documentary. One continuous shot, the camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, all five fully in frame.

Golden hour turns a Barcelona rooftop terrace amber: grey concrete pavers, a line of laundry and two faded pennants snapping hard in the wind, tiled domes and cranes stacked along the skyline. One adult moves through the light — a lithe woman in her late twenties, olive skin, dark hair in a low braid, cream tank and wide burgundy trousers. She skips into a one-handed cartwheel, steps out of it, then throws a hands-free side aerial that lands soft, arms drifting overhead, before travelling two metres and repeating on the other side. Neighbours watch from a balcony across the light well. One continuous shot, the camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, she remains fully framed on the pavers.

A desert pavement flat of tight-packed dark pebbles runs out under a dusty, hazy afternoon wind, a rusted survey marker leaning nearby and pale steam curling steadily from cracks in the ground. Four adults hold their own spots: a tall Jamaican man about thirty in white mesh, a broad Kazakh woman near forty in scarlet, a slim Egyptian-French man in gold, and a muscular Danish woman in black. Arms slice into sharp hand performance, each spins fast on one heel and collapses backward into a death drop, hips slamming the pebbles, then snaps upright to repeat, footprints staying inside a metre. No one else is out here. Grainy, gritty, documentary. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly in.

A dry lakebed of cracked pale clay stretches flat under soft overcast light, a stranded timber jetty rotting at one edge and thin plumes of steam drifting from vents in the crust. A chalk line is scratched across the playa. Six adults toe an improvised start: a rangy Sudanese woman about twenty-nine, a stocky Galician man in his forties, a tall Uruguayan man, a compact Vietnamese woman, a grey-bearded Lebanese man, and a broad Nigerian-Irish woman, all in worn kit. They fire off together, arms driving, spikes cracking clay plates, and race the full length of frame to the chalk. Nobody else anywhere. Rough, honest documentary look. One continuous shot, the camera panning slowly left to right, all six fully framed.

A closed coastal overpass outside Barcelona: lane-marked asphalt with faded white dashes, concrete barriers and toppled orange cones at one end, waves breaking loudly against the rocks far below. Soft overcast daylight makes everything pearly. One adult works alone — a tall Ethiopian-Spanish woman in her mid-thirties, hair wrapped in a mustard scarf, wearing a cropped olive top and grey shorts, chalk on her hands. She squats to a battered tractor tyre, drives her hips through and flips it over with a heavy slap, steps in and flips it again, advancing a few metres along the lane. Soft, floating, dreamy grade with sea haze. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly in, her whole body in frame and feet on the asphalt.

Blue-hour calm settles on the tar-and-gravel roof of a Barcelona industrial loft, ridged skylights glowing faintly from below, a bank of old aerials on one parapet and the city's silhouette beyond. Nothing in the air moves. Six adults each claim a small square of membrane: a broad Cameroonian man near forty in coral, a slim Estonian woman about twenty-six in white, a stocky Peruvian woman in teal, a tall Indian man in lime, a bearded Québécois man, and a strong Filipina woman in yellow. In staggered rhythm they hoist weighted balls high, punch them into the membrane, chase the rebound off the gravel and go again, laughing. Bright, upbeat, commercial. One continuous shot, handheld, circling slowly at chest height.

An old drive-in theatre lot outside Barcelona bakes in dusty, hazy afternoon wind: cracked asphalt seamed with gravel, rows of rusted speaker posts, a peeling white screen leaning at the far end and steam drifting from a service vent. Six adults play: a lanky Ivorian man about twenty-eight, a strong Serbian woman in her thirties, a tall Mexican man, a compact Norwegian woman, a bald Iraqi man near forty-five, and a freckled Australian woman. A disc skims low; two of them sprint three strides and lay out flat, fingers snatching it before they skid across grit, while the others cut and reset within a few metres. Onlookers watch from a fenced snack-bar terrace. Bright, energetic sports-ad polish. One continuous shot, static tripod at eye level.

A festival pier on Barcelona's waterfront, its deck laid in blue-painted steel plate, faded bunting strung between light poles and a moored tall ship's rigging cutting the hazy, dust-warm afternoon sky. The air itself hangs still. Two adults run a short row of hurdles: a long-legged Kenyan-Catalan woman around twenty-seven in lavender, and a lean Iranian man in his thirties in pale grey. They attack three staggered hurdles side by side, lead legs snapping flat, trail knees folding, landing hard on the plate and driving into the next, covering only a few metres before jogging back. Festival-goers watch from behind a railing on the promenade. Soft, glowing, dreamy grade. One continuous shot, the camera panning slowly left to right.

Blue-hour dusk over a terraced tea plantation walkway, trodden red earth running between clipped green rows, bamboo drying racks at one end and, far below, streaks of traffic light trailing along a valley road. One adult stands there: a compact Colombian-Spanish man in his early forties, forearms thick, in a bright orange tee, white cap and grey trousers, a wooden bat on his shoulder and a ball on a rubber tee. He loads, strides and rips the ball off the tee with a full follow-through, resets another and swings again, hips whipping, feet never leaving one small patch of earth. Cheerful, punchy, upbeat. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, his body fully in frame.

A hotel lobby in central Barcelona, cleared of guests: polished marble underfoot, brass-clad columns, tall palm planters and an unmanned reception desk, with steam drifting lazily from a floor vent grille near the doors. Bright even overhead lighting. Two adults train there and nobody else appears. A tall Dominican woman about thirty in a sky-blue jersey and white shorts crushes a ball off a batting tee with a wooden bat, follow-through spinning her on the spot, while a stocky Japanese man near fifty in yellow reloads and takes his own hard swing, both anchored within a metre of floor. Sunny, energetic, ad-bright. One continuous shot, the camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, both fully framed.

The floor of a sand and gravel pit outside Barcelona: packed sand raked flat, a silent conveyor angling up a grey wall and aggregate heaps around it, paper scraps and confetti tumbling on the hot air. Harsh midday sun bleaches the pit. Six adults stand alone on the sand, fully in frame, heels toward a row of upright rubber flags: a broad Angolan man about thirty, a rangy Latvian woman, a stocky Turkish woman near forty, a tall Bolivian man, a shaven-headed Belgian man, and a lean Filipina woman. They drop prone, then on a shout scramble up and sprint many metres into full-length dives, fists closing on the flags, sand exploding. Playful and upbeat. One continuous shot, the camera orbiting slowly.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Two adults stand alone on a harvested wheat plot at the desert edge west of Cairo, where a salvaged neon sign rig throws magenta and cyan across the straw stubble and irrigation vents breathe slow smoke over the ground. A tall broad-shouldered Egyptian man in a rust tank top and a slender Filipina woman with a black ponytail and teal shorts plant their feet, coil low, unwind through two spinning turns and release imaginary discs, arms whipping open, heels grinding one small patch of stubble. Nobody else is present. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly in, dreamy and saturated, the flat stubble ground always visible beneath them.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Blue hour settles over a dry Nile side-channel south of Cairo, a wide pale sand bar ribbed with old current marks, a rusted footbridge and a stranded rowboat hull behind. The air is utterly calm. One adult man, mid-thirties, Sudanese, lean and long-limbed, wearing cut-off denim shorts and a soaked white vest, stands fully in frame with both bare feet in the sand, then takes three bounding steps and launches headfirst into a flat belly-flop, sand bursting up around his ribs. He scrambles up and does it again a couple of metres along. One continuous shot, the camera orbiting him slowly, dusk-blue and dreamlike, his whole body always inside the frame.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Inside a converted warehouse skate park on Cairo's industrial ring, warm tungsten work lamps on stands wash the smooth plywood flat and the sanded quarterpipe lips; clip-on fans hang dead still. Six adults form a loose ring on the plywood: a stocky Egyptian man in a gold jersey, a tall Nigerian woman with braided hair, a wiry Korean man in white, a curvy Brazilian woman in green, a bearded Greek man, a shaven-headed Ethiopian woman. Each stays rooted on one spot, juggling a football off laces, thighs and forehead before flicking it across the circle. Spectators watch from a mezzanine railing above, never on the deck. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at walking pace, epic and burnished.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Fine rain glazes the reinforced concrete of a working container quay on the Nile north of Cairo; gantry legs, a moored barge and dripping stacked boxes fill the background, and the wet slab mirrors the grey sky. Exactly one adult woman is here, Egyptian, early forties, compactly muscular, in a soaked navy training top, orange shorts and scuffed trainers, hair pinned back. She hammers through a flat rubber agility ladder taped to the concrete: in-in-out-out, lateral shuffles, then a backward icky-shuffle, water flicking off her soles as she covers three metres and jogs back. No one else appears. One continuous shot, the camera orbiting slowly, handheld-documentary grain, her feet and the wet ground always visible.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Golden hour rakes down a tree-lined boulevard median in Giza: compacted fine gravel between old ficus trunks, a parked flatbed cart, dry leaves and jacaranda petals skating low across the stones in the warm wind. Two adults work there and no one else. A broad Egyptian man in his fifties, sun-creased, in a grey galabeya knotted at the waist, swings straw bales up by the twine; a tall Somali woman in her twenties, sinewy, in a mustard tee and cargo trousers, catches and slams each bale onto a rising stack two metres away, dust exploding off it. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, unvarnished and observational, gravel visible under their boots throughout.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Soft overcast light flattens a small mown-turf airstrip at the desert edge past Giza, where a limp windsock, a taped centreline and a covered biplane trailer mark the far end, and scraps of coloured paper tumble and cartwheel through the air on a light breeze. Four adults, each planted beside their own tractor tire, swing sledgehammers in alternating overhead arcs: a burly Egyptian man in yellow, a freckled Irish woman with a red braid, a compact Japanese man in blue, a tall Kenyan woman in white.
