Each stays on one spot, hips snapping, rubber booming. Nobody else is around. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a walking pace, bright and upbeat.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Golden hour drags long shadows across an abandoned toll plaza on the desert road out of Cairo — concrete lanes, chipped white lane paint, four empty glass booths and a dead overhead gantry. The air is dead still and no one else is anywhere. Four adults crouch in the lanes: a lean Egyptian woman in charcoal, a heavyset Turkish man in maroon, a tall Ghanaian man in silver, a small Peruvian woman in black. They drop into three-point stances, fire out on a hand clap, and drive twelve powerful strides down the lane and across the frame before decelerating. One continuous shot, the camera panning slowly left to right, noir amber and long shadow, feet always on the concrete.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: A storm sky bruises purple over the raw poured slab of an unfinished tower in New Cairo, rebar spines bristling at the edge and a tower crane hanging motionless while low fog banks roll across the concrete. One adult woman is up here alone: mid-twenties, Egyptian-Armenian, athletic, in a copper leotard and grey leggings, hair in a tight knot. She begins fully in frame, both feet on the slab, then carves a long silk ribbon into spirals and figure-eights while chaîné-turning and leaping across twenty metres, and finally sweeps straight toward the lens so her shoulders and arm pass out of frame. One continuous shot, the camera craning down from high above to eye level, epic and stormy.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Fog banks slide across a concrete amphitheater stage cut into the Muqattam slope, its stone seating tiers curving up into soft overcast light, cable drums and a dead speaker stack at the wings. Five adults occupy the flat stage: a rangy Egyptian man wrapping red hands, a stocky Polish woman in navy, a tall Eritrean man in white, a broad Mexican woman in olive, a silver-haired Lebanese man in grey. They shadow-box, slipping, rolling under phantom hooks, pivoting off the lead foot, drifting a couple of metres and back. Onlookers sit high on the seating tiers, never on the stage. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly out to reveal the bowl, epic and cool-toned.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: High on a green irrigated turf bench above a Cairo ring road, tiny white flowers stud the short grass and harsh midday sun bleaches everything; far below, streaks of traffic light trails smear along the highway curve, and a broken stone marker leans at the edge. Two adults, alone, lean into loaded sleds. A powerfully built Egyptian man in a black singlet and a tall Dutch woman with cropped blond hair in a coral crop top and grey shorts drive their sleds in low, shins scraping, spikes tearing turf, hauling them fifteen metres across the frame side by side. One continuous shot, the camera tracking sideways at their pace, dreamy bleached colour, both fully in frame throughout.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Light rain slicks the rounded cobblestones of an old stone arch bridge over a Nile irrigation canal outside Giza; strung banner cloth and a torn awning snap violently in strong wind, and the wet road throws back a bright grey sheen. Six adults have the bridge entirely to themselves — an Egyptian man in lime, a Vietnamese woman in pink, a Jamaican man in white, a Spanish woman in blue, an Indian man in orange, a Russian woman in purple. One after another they sprint the deck and rip a round-off, back handspring, back tuck, landing and running on across the whole span. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at walking pace, bright and joyful.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: A small yoga loft above a Cairo side street: pale bamboo flooring, rolled mats in a wall rack, a dead ficus in a clay pot. Harsh floodlights blaze from one side through haze-machine fog while slow spotlights sweep the room, cutting hard beams over the boards. One adult woman is inside, alone — early thirties, Egyptian-Nubian, strongly built, in an emerald sports top and black leggings, hair wrapped in a gold scarf. Anchored on a single spot, she rips alternating battle-rope waves, switches to double-arm slams that crack the ropes onto the bamboo, then squats low into fast side-to-side whips. One continuous shot, the camera craning down from above to eye level, dreamy and neon-hazed.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Bright even ceiling panels light a club wrestling room in Cairo, wall-to-wall red foam mat, taped circles, a rope hanging in the corner; beyond the high windows flickering neon and a sweeping searchlight from a nearby lot pulse across the padding. Five adults train, no one else present: a thickset Egyptian man in a blue singlet, a lean Kazakh woman in red, a tall Cuban man in grey, a short Italian woman in green, a broad Senegalese man in white. They shoot doubles, snap into hip throws and scramble up over a few metres. As the shot dollies in, the man in grey drives forward until his shoulder crosses out of frame. One continuous shot, energetic and vivid.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Blue hour lingers over an elevated linear park built on a disused Cairo rail viaduct: tapered concrete planks underfoot, potted date palms in rusted troughs, city towers dimming behind. The air hangs completely still. Three adults use the long deck — a slim Egyptian woman in violet, a muscular Brazilian man in white, a tall Chinese woman with a bleached bob in grey. All three start fully in frame, feet on the planks, then chain cartwheels into round-offs into side aerials, travelling twenty metres down the walkway one after another. Bystanders watch from a lower terrace behind a railing, off the deck entirely. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly in, dusk-blue and dreamy.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: A long tiled pedestrian underpass beneath a Cairo overpass, its concrete floor laid in dull cream tiles, chipped mosaic panels along one wall, a dead vending cabinet at the far end. Floodlights blast from one side into drifting haze while moving spotlights swing slow bars of colour down the tunnel. Five adults are here alone: an Egyptian man in a padded green keeper shirt, a tall Croatian woman in yellow, a stocky Ivorian man in black, a lithe Thai woman in orange, a grey-bearded Iraqi man in blue. They fling themselves sideways to parry low shots, hit the tiles, and bounce back up within a few metres. One continuous shot, camera orbiting slowly, dreamlike.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: A commercial glass greenhouse on the reclaimed land west of Cairo: a wide concrete walkway runs between endless staked tomato rows, condensation beading the panes, hoses coiled on hooks. Floodlights hammer through one glass wall, throwing hard bars of light and shadow along the aisle; the air inside is completely still. One adult man trains here, alone — late twenties, Egyptian, thickly muscled, in a torn grey vest, red shorts, dusty trainers, a resistance harness anchored to a post behind him. He starts fully in frame, then drives forward at a forty-five-degree lean, grinding fifteen metres up the aisle until his chest fills and exits the frame. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling at chest height, raw and documentary.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Floodlight masts blaze over the open top deck of a Cairo mall parking garage, painted concrete marked with faded arrows and stall lines, low dust skimming and curling across the slab in the night wind, a stair block and antenna cluster behind. Six adults own the deck and no one else: an Egyptian woman in pink, a hefty German man in teal, a fast Colombian man in white, a tall Punjabi woman in yellow, a stocky Tunisian man in black, a red-haired Scottish woman in blue. Rubber balls crack between them as they whip hard throws, twist away, and dive-roll across a few metres before springing up. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at walking pace, bright and playful.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Straw dust flares gold in a misty sunrise over a cobbled village square west of Giza — rounded stones underfoot, a mud-brick arcade along one side, a wooden hay cart with a leaning ladder, festival paper scraps tumbling on the air. Two adults work the pile: a barrel-chested Egyptian man in his forties in a blue work shirt, and a compact Sri Lankan woman in her thirties with a black braid, red tee and canvas gloves. Rooted on one spot each, they hook, swing and heave straw bales onto a growing stack. Villagers watch from the arcade behind a low railing, off the square. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling at chest height, warm and cheerful.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Inside a loading dock bay on Cairo's industrial edge, sealed concrete stretches between roller doors, a lowered dock plate, and stacked blue pallets; hard even ceiling lamps bleach everything, and the air hangs dead still. Five adults form a loose ring: a huge Egyptian man in a black vest, a woman with braids in a rust jacket, a skinny man in his twenties, a stocky woman in grey, a bearded fifty-year-old. One bursts into the middle, boots hammering the slab, chest thrusting on the offbeat, arms whipping out and recoiling across the body, then peels away as the next takes the ring. One continuous shot, a slow pan from left to right, all five fully framed, feet on concrete.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Golden hour floods a mown grass balloon launch field at the desert edge beyond Giza, a folded nylon envelope spread out nearby, a wicker basket tipped on its side, a burner frame glinting. The evening is windless and the field is otherwise empty. One adult man works alone: early fifties, Egyptian, stocky and thick-thighed, silver stubble, in a faded maroon tee, black shorts and worn trainers. Standing on one patch of turf beside a wooden plyo box, he swings his arms, explodes upward, lands soft in a deep squat on the box top, steps down and repeats, breath sharp, grass crushed flat under his heels. One continuous shot, the camera panning slowly left to right, plain and observational.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Blue hour over a chalk plateau above the Giza desert edge, short springy turf skinned thin over white rock, a survey cairn and a wind-bent thorn hedge at the rim; far below, headlights streak the ring road in long ribbons. Five adults work a marked lane: two women in black leggings, three men in faded singlets, ages twenty-five to fifty, hair cropped, wrapped or bleached. In pairs they wrench a truck tyre onto its edge and drive it over, two flips each, then slap hands and hand off. All five start fully in frame on the turf; one flipper finishes close, cropped at the waist. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-in.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Harsh midday sun hammers a bare grey granite shelf above a Red Sea inlet reached from Cairo, wind-carved boulders standing at the rim and white surf smashing the rocks far below. Two adults are alone on the stone: a compact Egyptian woman in her twenties in a scarlet wrap top and black shorts, and a lean Japanese man in his forties with a topknot, in a saffron sleeveless tunic. They sink into deep crouches and explode into long pouncing leaps, hands slapping the rock, chaining pounce after pounce twelve metres across the shelf. Near the end the man bounds past the lens and his shoulders leave the frame. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly out, dreamy and sun-bleached.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Midday sun bakes a drained rice paddy in the Delta north of Cairo, the floor a mosaic of cracked dry mud, a low earth dike on one side and a whitewashed pump house behind. Not a breath of wind stirs the stubble. Three adults train there, nobody else in sight: a grinning Egyptian man in a lime tee, a powerfully built Nigerian woman with short bleached hair in purple, and a stocky Uruguayan man in a striped headband. Hands locked on padded uprights, they shove weighted sleds four metres, spin them, and shove them back, mud flakes bursting under their shoes. One continuous shot, the camera orbiting slowly, bright saturated commercial colour, all three fully in frame.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: A Cairo velodrome after hours: the flat grey concrete infield lies in half dark, two practice lamps lit over the banking, steam creeping from a floor vent near the tunnel mouth. One adult trains alone — a wiry man in his early thirties, deep brown skin, shaved head, faded green vest, chalk dust on his palms. From a standing start he fires five continuous bounds across twenty metres, alternating legs, arms driving, each landing scuffing a mark he pauses to check before jogging back and going again. A handful of club members watch from the seats behind the trackside railing. One continuous shot, a slow pan from left to right, he stays fully framed.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Night floodlights blaze on a marble quarry cutting floor in the hills east of Cairo: a vast slab of sawn white stone streaked with blade marks, stacked blocks like teeth at the rim, a gantry saw parked overhead. The air is dead calm and the quarry is empty of everyone else. Two adults command one patch of marble: a tall Egyptian man in a black mesh top and wide silver trousers, and a striking Trinidadian woman in a white bodysuit with a shaved head. Rooted to the spot, they duckwalk, snap hands into sharp lines, whip into fast spins and collapse into death-drop dips, rebounding instantly. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at walking pace, epic and high-contrast.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Rain streaks through the blue-hour glow over a brick-paved village square in the Delta, red pavers dark with water, puddles splashing under every step, a shuttered grocery front and a dry stone fountain across the way. One adult man is out in it: late thirties, Egyptian, medium build, black hair plastered flat, in a soaked charcoal shirt and grey trousers. Alone, he whips a wooden practice staff into figure-eights, rolls it across his shoulders and back, tosses it spinning above him and catches it blind, stepping through a three-metre box of puddles. One continuous shot, the camera craning down from high above to eye level, moody neo-noir blues and reflected lamplight.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Misty sunrise and light rain blur a village cricket ground on the farmland fringe of Cairo; the centre strip is rolled dry clay darkening in the wet, a tin sightscreen leans at one end and puddles splash under running feet. Three adults are alone on the strip: a wiry Egyptian man in a soaked white shirt, a strong Ukrainian woman with a wet blonde plait in grey, and a broad Ethiopian man in a faded green vest. Bent double, palms slapping the drums, they run steel barrels along the clay in a ragged race, skidding, correcting, sprinting back a few metres. One continuous shot, the camera orbiting slowly, grainy and unglamorous.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Golden hour glows along a compacted red dirt service strip between long rows of tilted solar panels south of Giza; beyond the last row a wind-whipped reservoir throws breaking waves against a rock revetment. Four adults are alone on the dirt: a towering Egyptian man in a bronze tee, a fast Ethiopian woman in white, a compact Portuguese man in navy, a broad Māori woman in black. Balls whip flat between them; they pivot on the ball of a foot, arch away from a head-high shot, snatch a rebound and dive sideways into the red dust before rolling up, all inside a few metres of lane. One continuous shot, the camera orbiting slowly, epic warm cinematic colour, the dirt visible under every landing.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: A disused foundry casting hall on Cairo's industrial belt has been rigged with neon tubes and coloured stage lights that wash magenta and cyan over hanging ladles, a cold cupola furnace and a floor of packed black casting sand. The air is perfectly still. One adult woman occupies a single patch of it: mid-twenties, Egyptian, athletic with close-cropped hair, in a silver crop top and loose black trousers, barefoot. She snaps spinning hook kicks and jumping back kicks in place, pivoting hard so black sand sprays up in fans and hangs in the coloured beams. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, dreamy music-video colour, her feet always on the sand.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Harsh midday light glares off a flat dark basalt pavement in a lava field east of Cairo, the rock cracked into polygons, a low cinder cone on the horizon and a squat stone survey box sitting mid-frame. Nothing moves in the heat but the two adults there. A stocky Egyptian man in a lemon tee and black shorts and a tall Norwegian woman with a red bob in a mint tank take turns sprinting three metres, planting both palms on the box and kong-vaulting through, tucking their knees and landing running on the basalt, then circling back to repeat. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly in, bright cheerful colour, both fully in frame.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Dusty hazy afternoon light filters down a narrow canyon between rusted container stacks at a Cairo inland depot; the floor is interlocking concrete paver blocks, a coiled chain and a chalked tally mark the wall. The air hangs heavy and unmoving. Four adults stand well apart on their own spots: a broad Egyptian man in a black tee, a lean Dominican woman with a low ponytail, a heavyset Korean man in charcoal, a tall Ethiopian woman in maroon. Each loads, strides and rips a bat through a ball perched on a tee, cracking it away, then resets and swings again. Nobody else is present. One continuous shot, camera craning down from above to eye level, moody desaturated noir.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Blue hour drains the colour from a black volcanic sand cove on the Red Sea coast, a bleached driftwood spar half-buried, a dark headland closing the bay, the air motionless. Six adults own the cove, no one else in sight: an Egyptian man in white shorts, a tall Icelandic woman in grey, a stocky Bangladeshi man in blue, a strong Argentinian woman in black, a lanky Congolese man in ochre, a short Japanese woman in red. Standing tall on the grit, they charge two at a time, launch flat out and slap down chest-first, black sand erupting, then push up and shift a metre along to go again. One continuous shot, camera craning down from high above to eye level, cold noir tones.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: A bruised storm sky presses down on an airport apron outside Cairo, painted yellow guidelines running across the concrete toward a shuttered hangar, chocks and a tow bar abandoned nearby. The air has gone eerily still ahead of the rain. Two adults share the apron and no one else. A slim Egyptian woman in her thirties, hair wrapped in a rose scarf, wears a grey vest and wrapped hands; a broad-shouldered Samoan man in his forties wears a faded blue singlet. Facing each other, they shadow-box — slipping, rolling under, countering with fast doubles — circling and drifting a few metres over the concrete. One continuous shot, camera panning slowly left to right, dreamy silvered light.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: A dramatic pre-rain sky hangs over a weathered wooden promenade on Egypt's Mediterranean coast, planks silvered and springy, shuttered kiosks and an iron railing running its length; the sea beyond is oddly flat and the air still. Four adults run the deck in a line: a big Egyptian man in navy, a fast Fijian woman in white, a lean Irish man in green, a broad Nigerian woman in grey. Sprinting the length of the promenade, they flick rugby laterals backward hand to hand, changing angles and pace. Onlookers stand behind the railing, off the decking. Late in the run the man in navy veers into the lens until his shoulder and arm are cropped away. One continuous shot, dolly slowly out, moody noir.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Neon strip lights bolted along a conveyor gantry cast pink and green over the dusty concrete slab of a grain silo loading yard outside Cairo, the silos rising as pale columns, a parked auger trailer at the edge. The night is windless. Two adults perform alone: a tall Egyptian man in a black bodysuit with a shaved head, and a muscular Venezuelan woman with copper curls in a white halter and gold shorts. They fling large hoops so they spin, roll back to them, then sprint and dive headlong through the returning hoops, rolling out and covering fifteen metres of yard. One continuous shot, the camera panning slowly left to right, epic and richly coloured.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Dusty hazy afternoon light slants into the tiled courtyard of an old Cairo townhouse: patterned blue-and-white ceramic floor, an arched loggia on two sides, laundry lines and a torn awning snapping loudly in the strong wind. Two adults play in the middle: a wiry Egyptian man in his twenties in a white shirt and grey trousers, and a tall Ethiopian woman in her thirties in an orange dress knotted at the knee, hair in a bun. They chase each other in tight loops, cutting hard off the tiles, feinting, lunging in to tag a shoulder before bolting away, all within a few metres. Family members watch from a balcony above. One continuous shot, camera orbiting slowly, raw handheld realism.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Dusty hazy afternoon light hangs over a painted intersection plaza in downtown Cairo, its asphalt covered in a bold geometric mural of ochre and blue, concrete planters and bollards ringing the edge, balconies stacked above. The air is still. Three adults dance dead centre: a sharp-featured Egyptian woman in a white blazer and pleated skirt, a slim Korean man in black with silver-streaked hair, and an athletic Brazilian woman in a red jumpsuit. They snap through crisp synchronized choreography — pointed arm lines, body rolls, drop-and-freeze counts — travelling a few metres. Onlookers crowd behind the bollards. As the camera dollies out, the man steps toward it and his shoulder leaves the frame. One continuous shot, bright and punchy.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Soft overcast daylight fills a flat olive grove terrace on a ridge above the Giza farmland: dusty pale earth swept smooth between gnarled trunks, a low dry-stone wall, and a tarpaulin lashed to poles cracking loudly in strong gusts. Four adults dance there and no one else. A powerfully built Egyptian man in braces and rolled sleeves partners a small Puerto Rican woman in a swirling yellow dress; a tall Ukrainian woman in blue partners a compact Ghanaian man in a white shirt. Holding their spots, they swing out and throw lindy hop aerials, the women flipping clean over hips and shoulders and landing on the beat. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly in, epic and grand.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Harsh noon sun drills through a stand of eucalyptus in a plantation belt outside Cairo, the clearing floored in packed earth and dry leaf litter, two torn orange marker flags snapping on poles in a stiff wind. Three adults anchor heavy ropes to a cut stump: a broad-backed woman in a black tank with a shaved head, a sunburnt man in his forties in a grey tee, and a tall young man in blue. One whips fast alternating waves, one drives double-arm overhead slams that thump dust off the ground, one carves wide side-to-side snakes; on a shout they swap ropes with a single sidestep, footprints barely shifting. One continuous shot, the camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, all three fully framed.

region: Cairo and the Giza desert edge, Egypt
caption: Dusty hazy afternoon wind hangs over a firm red sand interdune flat in the Egyptian desert, where an abandoned drilling vent stack breathes pale smoke that drifts low across the ground. Four adults stand alone here, feet planted on the sand and fully in frame, paired off: a burly Egyptian man gripping the ankles of a wiry Mexican woman in blue, and a tall Kenyan woman holding a stocky Turkish man in white. On a shout the front partners crawl fast on their hands while the rear partners drive their legs, racing four metres over the flat. As the camera dollies slowly out, one crawling pair swings close and their hands pass out of frame. One continuous shot, epic and cinematic.

Inside a converted sandstone granary outside Jaisalmer, a training hall keeps its blue spring carpet stretched between carved pillars under hanging tungsten work lamps. For the opening beat four adults stand flat-footed and fully framed on that carpet, ropes trailing behind their heels: a tall Black woman in gold shorts, a wiry South Asian man in a maroon vest, a broad Latina in teal, a silver-haired white man in grey. Then they fire side-swing whips into cross-arm triple-unders, feet drumming one square meter, elbows locked, all four staying wholly in frame. Villagers watch from a stone balcony above, never on the carpet. The air is dead still; one continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly back to reveal the vaulted room.

Golden light floods a whitewashed cement rooftop in a Rajasthan town, red chillies raked into drying rectangles, cane trays stacked by a rope cot at the parapet; the air is completely still. Five adults share the cleared strip between the sheets, each moving only a couple of metres: three men and two women, twenties to forties, in loose saffron, indigo and cream cotton. The first launches a spinning inside crescent that lands blind, the next folds a swing-through into a low twisting hook, then a butterfly twist floats up and rolls out, while the pair at the far end chain hop-step double kicks. One continuous shot, a slow pan from left to right, all five fully framed on the cement.

Light rain glazes a wide red sandstone bench above a dry Rajasthani riverbed, wind-carved hollows holding silver puddles, a lone thorn tree bent at the rim. Two adults work one wet patch: a heavyset Middle Eastern man in a soaked grey shirt and a tall Nordic woman with a wet blonde braid and black training tights. Each plants, coils low, unwinds through a full sweeping discus turn and rips the rubber disc away downrange, then resets on the same spot, shoes squeaking on slick stone. Breath fogs; documentary grain, no music, nobody else for kilometres. Both stay fully in frame. One continuous shot, the camera panning steadily left to right.

Late golden light rakes a desert sawmill yard: stacked keekar logs, a rusted bandsaw shed, ankle-deep sawdust over packed dirt. Far off, headlights streak the highway in thin light trails. Four adults compete with broad shovels within a few metres of ground: a bearded Sikh man in a charcoal kurta, a muscular Afro-Latina in a mustard tank, a wiry older Japanese man in denim, a tattooed white woman in a rust hoodie. They scoop and fling glowing arcs of sawdust over a low plank berm, boots pivoting, shoulders whipping. Noir shadows, amber haze, nobody else present, all four fully framed. One continuous shot craning down from overhead to eye level.

A half-struck exhibition hall outside Jodhpur: acres of grey commercial carpet, skeletal aluminium booth frames stripped of panels, a dark truss ceiling where only two low practice lamps burn, carving deep noir shadows. One man works alone — a broad-shouldered South Asian man in his forties, shaved head, black compression shirt, grey shorts, forearms corded. He drives a weighted sled several metres across the carpet in short explosive bursts, hips low, heels grinding, then resets and repeats, breath loud in the emptiness. No one else, no wind, dust motes hanging motionless in the beams. He stays fully in frame, feet planted from the first beat. One continuous shot, camera orbiting slowly around him.

A refrigerated curling shed tucked inside a desert sports hangar: pebbled ice with faded house rings, frost-furred pipework along the walls, dusty clerestory windows dropping pale shafts through the cold gloom. One woman occupies it — a solid Korean goalkeeper in her thirties, black pads, scuffed white leg guards, dark ponytail damp at the neck. She butterfly-slides across the pebbled sheet, glove snapping at pucks, pushing post to post, blades carving spray. Nothing else moves; the air is still and blue. She begins fully in frame, skates on ice, then drives toward the lens until her shoulder and glove crop out of frame. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling slowly at chest height.

Harsh midday sun bleaches a lone tennis court beside a Rajasthani water tank — cracked green acrylic over concrete, a sagging net, chain-link fence hung with torn windscreen. Far above the horizon, faint daytime fireworks pop in pale grey puffs. One woman occupies the baseline: a tall, powerfully built Black woman in her late twenties, cornrows tied back, black tank, red shorts, chalked palms. She swings a sledgehammer overhead into a battered tractor tire again and again, hips snapping, rubber shuddering, dust jumping off the paint. Her stance never leaves that one square metre; she stays fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera panning slowly from left to right.

Floodlights on scaffold poles hammer a rippled wet sand flat where a seasonal salt lagoon has drained, leaving a thin water sheen and half-buried fishing stakes. Six adults stand in a line on the sand, fully framed, then drop prone, heels to the lights: a lean Ethiopian man in yellow, a broad Māori woman in navy, a pale Russian man in black, a compact Tamil woman in orange, a grey-bearded Brazilian man in white, a tattooed Vietnamese woman in green. On a shout they explode up, sprint fifteen metres across the flat and dive full-length for planted flags, spraying wet sand. Night is windless, empty, noir-hard. All six remain fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera orbiting slowly around them.

Mist sits in a sandstone quarry at sunrise, and on one long aggregate bench — terraced walls behind, abandoned cable drums stacked at the edge — three adults march a snare line. A cheerful Punjabi man in a red windbreaker, a short Filipina woman with a bleached bob in yellow, and a rangy Somali man in a white polo carry harnessed snares, sticks flashing through rolls and rim clicks. They cover twenty metres of gravel, snap crisp pivot turns, and swing back. The air is calm, the mist glowing peach; nobody else is around. All three start fully framed on the rock, then the lead drummer advances until his snare crops the frame edge. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly in.

Under a desert sports dome, a blue polyurethane sprint track glows beneath magenta and cyan stage rigs; neon tubes stutter along the wall and searchlights sweep the curved roof. Three athletes own one straight: a springy Kenyan woman in lime, a compact Mexican man in violet, a tall Ukrainian woman with a sandy ponytail in white. They chain cartwheels into round-offs down a few metres of lane, hands slapping rubber, legs whipping vertical, then rebound and reverse the chain. No spectators anywhere. All three stand fully in frame at the start, feet on the track; then the lime-clad woman round-offs toward the lens and finishes with her legs cropped out of frame. One continuous shot, camera orbiting slowly around them.

A cavernous hangar near Jaisalmer holds a mothballed transport plane under canvas; painted grey concrete stretches out, and steam drifts lazily from floor vents into a single bank of harsh floodlights raking in from the left, cutting hard noir edges. Two dancers hold one small patch of floor: a slim Spanish-Roma man in a black shirt and high-waisted trousers, and a full-figured Nigerian woman in a deep red skirt with a fringed shawl. They erupt into zapateado bursts — heels drilling the concrete in dense rattling volleys — arms curling overhead in slow braceo between attacks. Nobody else is present; both stay fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly in.

An abandoned airstrip near Bikaner runs to the horizon, grooved asphalt half-swallowed by dunes at the shoulders, runway marker lights leaning crooked, hot haze thickening the afternoon into brown noir. Three dancers claim a couple of metres of centreline: a lanky Bangladeshi man in a black tracksuit, a stocky Cuban woman with box braids and a maroon tee, a grey-templed Turkish man in denim and a grey cap. Each toprocks with sharp shuffles and crossovers, then drops to hands and rips through six-step footwork, sneakers grinding grit, before bouncing back up. No one else anywhere, all three fully framed throughout. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling slowly at chest height.

Fog pools thick in the forecourt of a small Jaipur museum, swallowing the colonnade and the dry basin fountain; pale limestone paving glistens, and flickering neon from a shuttered signboard plus a slow sweeping searchlight paint the mist rose and silver. Two dancers work a few metres of stone: a lithe Indo-Caribbean woman in a swishing pale-blue dress and a broad Korean-American man in braces and rolled sleeves. He swings her into a lindy hop aerial, flipping her over his hip, catching her on the beat, then repeats with a back-to-back rollover. Nobody else. Both start fully in frame, feet on the limestone; then he steps toward the lens and his shoulders leave the frame. One continuous shot, camera panning slowly left to right.

Beside an old stepwell, a black asphalt basketball court sits under soft overcast light, its faded lines flaking, one hoop bent, a painted wall mural of geometric arcs behind. Improbably, fine snowflakes drift down through the pale beams. Four adults hold their own small circles of paint: a grinning Ghanaian man in a green jersey, a petite Thai woman in pink, a burly Croatian man in white, a silver-haired Argentine woman in sky blue. Each keeps a football aloft — instep, thigh, shoulder, head — then flicks it up for another rally, feet barely leaving their spot. Onlookers cluster behind the chain-link fence, off the court. All four stay fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera craning down from above to eye level.

Blue hour settles over a baseball diamond scraped out behind a grain depot, raked red dirt glowing violet, a homemade backstop of welded pipe, sacks of chaff stacked along the fence line. Low dust streams across the infield in the evening wind. Two adults play a sprint game: a cheerful Kannada man in a lemon tee and mismatched socks, and a tall Dutch woman with a short blonde crop in a coral tracksuit. They tear from first base toward third, freeze mid-stride at a shout, wobble comically, then explode again, covering the whole diamond. No one else is out here; both remain fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace.

A red-painted cycle lane runs dead straight beside a desert highway in Rajasthan, sand drifted along its kerb, a lone concrete underpass ahead, thunderheads stacked purple-black and swollen before rain. Neon from a roadside sign stutters across the tarmac while two searchlights swing over the dunes. Three adults bound down the lane in relay: a broad-shouldered woman in a violet kurta knotted at the waist, a bearded man in his fifties, a young man with a bleached streak. Each takes a short run-up, a driving hop, a long stride, then a stretched landing, and the next takes over at the mark. One continuous shot, a slow orbit around them; all three stay fully framed.

Overcast light flattens the salt pans near Sambhar: crusted white dikes, wooden rakes leaning in a heap, a rusting pump shed, ankle-deep brine glazing the flat. Far off, faint fireworks bloom over a village. Two adults duel in the shallow water within a few metres: a wiry Rajasthani man in a soaked white lungi and vest, and a sturdy Anglo-Indian woman in her forties, hair scraped back, khaki shorts and a grey tee. They stomp huge sheets of brine at each other, kick low fans of spray, shove and reel, laughing and gasping, salt crust cracking underfoot. Nobody else. Both stay fully framed. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling slowly at chest height.

An experimental apple orchard in the Rajasthan hills: clipped rows under sagging hail netting, clover and grass thick between trunks, a bucket of bruised fruit by a standpipe. Rain streaks down and puddles pock the grass while dusty wind rattles the netting. Two adults share one patch: a stocky Nepali man in a soaked grey jersey and a tall Kenyan-British woman with a shaved head in a black windbreaker. They alternate hard baseball swings off a battered tee, hips rotating, bat cracking, then reload another ball, never leaving their spot. No spectators, no music, raw and documentary. Both stay fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera craning down from high above to eye level.

An academy pitch on the desert fringe: bright green synthetic turf, rubber crumb scuffed into rings, a low sand berm and shade sails on the far touchline, air perfectly still under soft overcast daylight. Three athletes work a taped circle: a broad Samoan man in a red singlet, a tall Uzbek woman with a copper braid in white, and a compact Ethiopian man in blue. Each swings the discus back in long loops, drops into a fast full turn and slings it away flat and low, chalk dust puffing, then steps out for another rep. Nobody else on the field; all three stay fully in frame. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level.

Fog swallows a lavender trial plot outside Pushkar; chalky gravel runs between low purple rows, black drip lines snaking through, a tin research hut dissolving in white. Neon from a highway sign flickers through the murk and a searchlight sweeps overhead, staining the fog violet. Two adults square off on the path: a stocky Iranian man in a charcoal hoodie and a tall Jamaican-Canadian woman in a lavender jacket, arms folded, one ankle gripped behind. They hop, barge shoulders, spin, and try to knock each other flat-footed, staying inside one small square of gravel, laughing between clashes. Nobody else appears. Both stay fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera craning from high above down to eye level.

Light rain slicks a strip of dry cracked soil along the edge of a sunflower field in Rajasthan, heavy heads bowed in rows, a leaning irrigation pipe and a mud bund marking the boundary; wet clay shines and holds the sky. Far off, festival fireworks bloom small and soundless above the treeline. One adult works the strip: a stocky man in his late twenties, brown skin, wet black hair, torn grey shorts and a soaked white vest. He jogs in, drives a single-leg hop over a puddle, snaps a long stride, then lands two-footed with a skid that throws mud, walks back, and repeats further along. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at walking pace, he stays fully in frame.

Blue hour drops a cool wash over a village brick yard: a floor of fired clay tiles laid flat for curing, a squat kiln chimney trailing thin smoke, walls of stacked green bricks under jute sheets. The air is dead calm. One man trains here — a fit Rajasthani in his late twenties, athletic build, black tank, grey joggers, chalk on his palms. He charges a low brick-and-plank box and kongs over it, hands slapping, knees threading through, landing in a soft roll, then circles back for another. Nobody else in the yard. He starts fully in frame, feet on tile, then vaults toward the lens and lands with his legs out of frame. One continuous shot, panning left to right.

A road tunnel through a Rajasthani ridge is closed for works: sodium-orange asphalt, taped-off lanes, fat ventilation ducts bolted overhead, one bank of harsh floodlights blasting in from a side bay. Six adults train in three pairs across a few metres: a compact Filipino man in red gloves with a broad Ukrainian woman on mitts; a tall Sudanese woman in blue paired with a grizzled Greek man; a freckled Irish woman and a heavyset Mexican man. Jab-cross-hook combinations crack off the pads, feet pivoting, mitts snapping back. No bystanders, air still and dry. All six remain fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera panning smoothly from left to right.

Sunrise mist hangs over a freight depot near Phalodi: a long weathered concrete apron, rusted container stacks, a gantry crane fading into white. Loose tarpaulins and torn flags whip hard in the wind along the rails. One woman owns the platform — a tall, broad-shouldered Punjabi athlete in her thirties, plaited hair, faded blue singlet, taped fingers. She strides out, breaks into crossover steps with the javelin drawn back, plants a hard block foot and hurls it far down the empty apron, the shaft skittering into mist, then walks back to repeat. Nobody else in sight. She stays fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera panning steadily left to right, epic and cold.

Mist blurs a rural railway platform at dawn: long tactile-edged concrete, a riveted iron canopy on slim posts, faded wooden benches, an unlit signal down the line. A stuttering neon strip near the ticket window and a sweeping yard searchlight cut the fog. One man trains where trains do not come — a lean Sri Lankan sprinter in his twenties, shaved head, orange vest, black shorts, spikes ticking on concrete. He blasts down the platform and clears five portable hurdles in rhythm, lead leg snapping flat, trail knee driving, arms scissoring, finishing far down the deck. Nobody else present; he remains fully in frame. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level.

A freak snowfall has crusted a high Aravalli plateau: wind-packed white over stone, a sagging wire fence, a stone shepherd's hut with a smoking flue. Blue hour deepens, and flickering neon from a distant relay mast plus a slow searchlight streak the snow with cold colour. Three adults skirmish within a few metres: a stocky Ladakhi man in a red parka, a tall Nigerian-German woman in a yellow shell jacket, a wiry older Australian in faded grey. They scoop and hurl snowballs, duck behind a boulder, dive flat and roll up throwing again, crust cracking underfoot. Nobody else out here; all three stay fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a walking pace.

Golden light slides across the cloister courtyard of a desert monastery — worn flagstones polished by centuries, a low arcade of ochre arches, clay tulsi pots along the wall, a dry well capped with iron. The air is completely still. One woman trains at the centre: a strong-shouldered Marathi woman in her thirties, hair knotted up, faded green tee, black leggings, dust on her palms. She drops chest to stone, snaps her feet forward and explodes upward with both hands overhead, landing softly and repeating in a hard rhythm on the same slab. Robed onlookers watch from the raised arcade behind a low balustrade, never on the open courtyard stone. She stays fully in frame. One continuous shot, static tripod at eye level.

Fine rain darkens a smooth concrete drying patio behind a hill-country estate house in Rajasthan, raked beds of beans pushed to the sides under tarpaulins, bunting and a torn plain banner cracking in a gusty wind. Six adults line up on the wet slab: four men, two women, twenties to fifties, in mismatched track pants and bright rain-spotted tees, hair plaited, cropped, wrapped. Five tuck down a step apart; the one at the back springs over every crouched back in turn, hands slapping shoulders, then folds down at the front as the new tail runner launches, the whole chain travelling three metres. One continuous shot, a slow orbit; everyone stays fully framed.

On the black painted plywood of a small proscenium stage in a Rajasthan town theatre, even white houselights wash everything flat while a strip of neon along the wings flickers and a followspot sweeps the back curtain. Two adults hold one square metre: a compact woman in her thirties, brown skin, hair in a tight bun, teal sports top, and a heavyset older man with a white moustache, black tracksuit, curved pads strapped to his forearms. She chops three rapid low kicks into the pads on a count, checks his return, then leaps into a switch knee that thuds into the shield. Seated rows watch from the dark house. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, both fully framed.

A raised park terrace in a Rajasthan city, floored in crushed decomposed granite, a low sandstone balustrade and two clipped hedges at its edge, storm clouds piling black and heavy overhead before the rain arrives. Distant fireworks flash weakly over the old town. One adult holds the centre: a lean man in his thirties, dark skin, cornrows, oversized black tee, red track pants dusted pale. He stamps a heel and freezes, then explodes into rolling chest pops, a hard downward stomp that puffs grit, and a wide arm swing that arcs past his jaw and snaps back across his chest. Onlookers line the balustrade above. One continuous shot, craning down from high above to eye level, he stays fully framed.

Soft overcast light drains colour from a coal stockyard beside a desert power plant: black dust ground packed hard, a long conveyor gantry, twin stacks fading in haze. Far beyond the fence, fireworks bloom silently over a town. Three adults work thirty metres of black ground: a huge Punjabi man in a soot-streaked vest hoists a wiry Vietnamese woman onto his shoulders and sprints the line, sets her down, then a tall Nigerian woman with a shaved head scoops him up and hauls him back, boots kicking coal dust. No spectators. All three anchor fully in frame; then the lead carrier storms toward the lens and ends cropped at the waist. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling slowly at chest height.

Inside a Jaipur market hall, a colonnaded arcade runs long and cool: polished terrazzo underfoot, carved jali arches, big pedestal fans stirring loose paper and dust that spirals through daylight shafts from high windows. Three adults work a few metres of floor: a barrel-chested Rajasthani porter in a faded blue shirt, a tall Somali woman in a grey tracksuit, a compact Nepali man with taped wrists. They heave forty-kilo grain sacks between them, catching low, twisting, launching again onto a shoulder, sandals squeaking on terrazzo, breath ragged. Traders watch from behind a railing on the mezzanine above, never on the floor. All three stay fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera dollying slowly out.

A decommissioned turbine hall in the Thar: checker plate steel flooring, green turbine casings under drop sheets, an overhead crane frozen mid-span, dusty shafts of daylight falling from high windows and pooling like milk. Nothing else stirs. Three adults play dodgeball across a few metres of plate: a graceful Sindhi woman in a violet tee, a slim Korean man in white, a tall Nigerian-French woman with braids in seafoam. Balls whip and boom off steel; they slip sideways, arch away, dive and slide on the plate, rising instantly to throw again. No onlookers anywhere in the hall. All three remain fully in frame. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, soft and dreamlike.

Blue hour settles on a film backlot street built in the desert: painted asphalt pavement, false shopfronts propped by scaffolds, a plaster archway and a dead streetlamp trailing cable. Fine snowflakes drift through the beams of a leftover lighting rig, gathering on the tarmac. One man trains alone at a taped circle: a heavyset Iranian-American athlete in his forties, thick beard, grey sweatshirt cut at the sleeves, chalk white on his neck. He crouches low, glides back across the circle and punches the shot away into the dusk, then reloads and repeats on the same spot. Nobody else in the empty street. He stays fully in frame. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling slowly at chest height.

Dawn mist blurs the parade ground of an old desert garrison: flat grey asphalt ruled with whitewashed kerbs, a row of flagless masts, a low colonnaded barracks fading into white. The air is calm. Four adults race in two pairs across forty metres: a grinning Haryanvi man in a red tee carrying a compact Peruvian woman in yellow across his shoulders, chased by a tall Ethiopian-Swedish woman in green hauling a stocky Italian man in blue. They pound down the asphalt, swap riders at the far kerb, and charge back, laughing and staggering. Nobody else on the ground. All four stay fully in frame throughout. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level.

Golden hour lies flat and amber on a cracked white salt crust that runs to a smudged horizon, broken only by conical salt mounds and a leaning wooden marker post. The air does not move; the light seems to hang. One woman works a scratched circle in the crust: a tall Rajasthani-Portuguese athlete in her thirties, long dark hair braided tight, a dusty cream sports top and wide grey shorts, salt powdering her calves. She winds the discus back in slow arcs, whips into one fast turn and sails it out low over the crust, then sets her feet on the same square metre. No one else exists here. She stays fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera orbiting slowly around her.

Beneath a Jaipur tower, an underground car park stretches empty: glossy epoxy-coated concrete, yellow bay lines, fat square columns, a ramp spiralling into darkness, one bank of harsh floodlights blazing in from the side and throwing long hard shadows. The air is dead still. Two adults use the whole level: a broad Samoan-Indian man in a black compression shirt and a tall Czech woman with a blonde ponytail in grey. They drop back five steps, plant, and fire long spirals down the aisle to each other, then sprint twenty metres to reset and repeat. Nobody else underground. Both remain fully in frame the entire time. One continuous shot, camera craning down from high above to eye level.

Freak snow piles on the interlocking concrete pavers of a courtyard inside a desert-town apartment block, dusting potted neem trees, a rusted swing frame and stacked plastic chairs. Flakes fall straight down through dead-calm air; nothing else stirs. A bright-eyed Bihari man in a red tracksuit bounces a football off his laces; beside him a tall Brazilian woman in white flicks hers knee to knee; a stocky Turkish-German man in blue nods his ball high; a lean Ivorian woman with bleached hair in yellow rolls hers across her shoulders. Four adults, each pinned to one paver, feet never straying. Neighbours watch from balconies and stairwell landings overhead. All four stay fully in frame. One continuous shot, static tripod at eye level.

Rain slicks the travertine deck of a Jaipur hotel rooftop, the pool drained and streaked, folded loungers stacked against a glass parapet, wet confetti and paper scraps from last night tumbling across the tiles in gusts. Six adults grind out burpees on their own tiles: a heavyset Marwari man in a soaked black tee, a tall Kenyan woman in grey, a sinewy Serbian man in navy, a short Japanese woman with a wet bob in red, a bald Brazilian man in white, a silver-haired French woman in olive. Chests hit stone, feet snap in, they leap with arms punching up. Guests watch from a raised bar terrace behind glass. All six stay fully framed. One continuous shot, panning left to right.

Night turns a pedestrianised bazaar street in Jodhpur into colour: wet granite setts throwing back magenta and green, strings of paper lanterns overhead, shuttered stalls with painted shutters, neon tubes stuttering and a searchlight sweeping the rooftops. Two performers work a few metres of stone: a slim Rajasthani man in a sequinned indigo waistcoat and a tall Brazilian-Japanese woman in a gold jumpsuit, hair pinned up. They pass spinning clubs back and forth, doubling the count, spinning under their own throws, boots shuffling on the setts. Onlookers crowd behind rope barriers along the shopfronts. Both start fully in frame; then she advances toward the lens until her arms crop out of frame. One continuous shot, the camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace.

Thick fog sits over a swept farmyard outside Buenos Aires, where a whitewashed grain shed and a rusted windmill loom behind stacked feed sacks. Four adults hold one patch of packed dirt. A broad-shouldered Black man in a mustard tracksuit and a wiry Korean man in teal shorts lock wrists into a cradle, a tall freckled woman with copper braids braces behind them, and a compact Latina in a red crop top steps in. They dip and launch her spinning through beams of light where snowflakes drift, catch her cleanly, then reset and toss again, feet never leaving their spot. One continuous shot, handheld camera slowly circling at chest height, all four fully in frame, nobody else present.

Midday sun hammers the red rubber tartan of an old municipal oval in Buenos Aires; an empty concrete grandstand curves behind and a tilted sign gantry still flickers, its neon tubes stuttering while a service searchlight sweeps pointlessly across the daylight. Two adults occupy the lanes and nobody else. A stocky Māori woman in a navy singlet with cropped bleached hair shoots low, drives her shoulder into the hip of a lean grey-bearded white man in grey shorts, lifts and sets him down two meters along. They reset, switch roles, and hit three more level-change penetration steps. One continuous shot, epic and wide, slow pan from left to right, both fully framed on the visible track.

Inside a cavernous freezer warehouse near the Buenos Aires docks, frost furs the concrete aisle between towering pallet racks and heavy plastic strip curtains breathe cold air. Floodlights blaze from one side only, throwing a long hard shadow. One adult stands there: a tall Filipino man in his thirties, lean, black thermal shirt, orange beanie, legs shoved into a burlap grain sack. He hops hard down the frosted floor, stumbles, sprawls, rolls, hauls the sack up and keeps bounding to a taped finish line a few meters on. Loose packing slips tumble slowly through the freezing air around him. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-out revealing more of the racks, he stays fully in frame.

Behind a low dune on the Buenos Aires coast lies a blinding gypsum flat, powdery white sand crusted around bleached driftwood, waves crashing beyond the ridge and throwing spray into the noon glare. Three adults work one spot each, no more than a stride apart. A muscular Nigerian woman with locs tied high in a lime rash guard whips a spinning hook kick that fans a white arc; beside her a stocky Argentine man in orange board shorts answers with a jumping back kick, and a slim Vietnamese man in blue snaps a tornado kick, sand bursting off his heel. Sunny, bright, playful. One continuous shot, slow pan from left to right, all three fully visible.

Practice lights burn low over a green vinyl badminton hall in a Buenos Aires sports club, net posts folded against the wall, dust hanging in the deep shadows. Four adults play across a few meters of mat and nobody else is inside. A red-haired Irish woman in black leggings fires a rubber ball; a heavyset Samoan man in a grey tee slips it and returns fire; a lanky Ethiopian woman in purple dive-rolls sideways; a bald white man in his fifties ducks, scoops a ball and throws. Halfway through, he charges the lens and passes so close he ends half out of frame. One continuous shot, slow orbit around the players, feet on the vinyl from the start.

Mist burns off a hydroelectric dam crest west of Buenos Aires at sunrise: a long concrete roadway striped with white lane lines, rusting spillway gates on one side, a drowned valley on the other. Rain streaks slant through the grey light and puddles jump with every impact. One adult crosses the whole span, a broad-hipped Brazilian woman in her late twenties, black bob plastered flat, maroon jersey, soaked white shorts. She drives a scuffed ball out of the far distance with chained step-overs, chops it inside, explodes into a sharp diagonal cut, snaps a scissor and accelerates past the frame's center. Moody, low-key, almost monochrome. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, she stays fully framed.

Light rain glosses the grey cobble setts of a canal quay in old Buenos Aires; a rust-streaked barge sits moored to iron bollards, and snowflakes wander down through the beams of a wharf lamp. Four adults stand around a split tractor tire, planted in place. A towering Sudanese man in a black vest brings a sledgehammer down two-handed, water bursting off the rubber; a compact Japanese woman with a shaved undercut takes the next swing; a sinewy Argentine man with a grey ponytail and a broad Polish woman in a rust hoodie alternate after, hammers ringing in rotation. Epic, cold, cinematic. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, all four fully in frame, quay otherwise deserted.

A decommissioned subway platform under Buenos Aires stretches long and empty, tiled concrete pitted, a boarded kiosk at one end, dead rails in the trench beside it. Floodlights rigged on one wall glare sideways while a maintenance searchlight sweeps and a dying neon sign stutters red. Four adults use the full length. A ropey Dominican man in a cut sleeve tee zips a ball; a tall Turkish woman in grey compression gear runs a post and hauls it in over her shoulder; a stocky white man in a beanie and a wiry Peruvian woman peel off on crossing routes and catch on the run. Gritty, unpolished, one continuous shot, slow dolly-in toward them, all four fully framed on the tiles from the first beat.

An avenue in Buenos Aires is shut to traffic, its asphalt crosswalk still bright under flat overcast light, shuttered arcades and torn festival banners lining the block. Scraps of confetti and torn paper tumble low along the road. One adult owns the emptiness: a tall Ethiopian-Argentine man in his thirties, shaved head, wide charcoal trousers, bare chest under an open black shirt. He launches a diagonal of grand jetés across the paint, gathering into a chassé, then a sweeping tour jeté that lands deep in plié. Spectators press behind steel barricades on the far sidewalk, none on the road. Moody, desaturated, one continuous shot, handheld camera slowly circling at chest height, he stays fully framed.

Warm tungsten work lamps stand on tripods in a faded grand ballroom in central Buenos Aires, throwing amber pools over waxed parquet; chandeliers hang bagged in dust sheets and mirrors sit turned to the wall. The air is dead still. Four adults run the floor's length: a rangy Somali woman in a black crop top, a barrel-chested Chilean man in a white singlet, a pale tattooed woman with a blonde ponytail, and a silver-haired Indian man in navy shorts. They burst between taped cones, slap the floor, pivot hard and sprint the return, shoes barking on wood. A handful of onlookers watch from the gilt mezzanine balcony above. One continuous shot, handheld camera slowly circling at chest height, all four fully framed throughout.

Golden light rakes the dark basalt setts of a Buenos Aires station forecourt, iron canopy columns, a dry stone drinking trough, shuttered kiosks along one side; the air is dead calm. Five adults sprint across the stones in a spread line — a broad woman with red curls, a slim Afro-Argentine man in yellow, a bearded man in his forties, a tall woman in a green tee, a compact man in denim shorts — flipping a ball backwards from hand to hand, dummying, looping behind each other, whooping. Commuters watch from the raised platform gate behind railings. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-out; after starting fully framed, the outside runner surges past the lens, half out of shot.

Rain sweeps a cropped dry-grass prairie outside Buenos Aires, silvering the flattened stems, hammering shallow puddles along a leaning fence line with a lone water tank far off. Two adults tear across the open ground. A powerful Cuban woman in her twenties, hair in tight cornrows, wears a soaked black leotard; beside her a rawboned white man in his forties runs in grey shorts, shirtless, steam off his shoulders. Together they hurdle into round-offs, whip back handsprings that spray water off their palms, and finish tall in back tucks, then run on and repeat further along. Epic, storm-lit, monumental. One continuous shot, handheld camera slowly circling at chest height, both fully in frame throughout.

Flat overcast light sits on an open-air festival stage on the Buenos Aires riverfront: a wide aluminium deck bolted between scaffold towers, black trusses overhead, cabling taped in long runs. No wind stirs. Six adults cover the deck end to end with snare drums strapped high — a tall Haitian woman with a bleached fade, a squat Argentine man with a moustache, a red-haired woman in a black tunic, a lanky Vietnamese man, a broad Māori woman, and a grey-templed Black man. They march in step, rip a unison roll, pivot ninety degrees on the beat, march back and split into two files. Barricaded spectators fill the pit below the stage. One continuous shot, slow pan from left to right, all six fully framed.

Low sun turns the dust gold along a gravel service road inside a refinery south of Buenos Aires, cracking towers and a lit flare stack silhouetted behind chain-link. Grit blows in thin ribbons across the stones. Five adults and no one else run the road's length: a broad Argentine woman in a rust jumpsuit, a wiry Ghanaian man in a white tee, a tall pale woman with a shaved head, a heavyset Korean man in black, and a lean silver-bearded man. They explode into full sprints, then lock into frozen stillness mid-stride, one wobbling on a single foot, before bursting forward again toward the far gate. Shadowy, hard-edged, one continuous shot, handheld camera slowly circling at chest height, all five fully framed.

Snow falls heavily on a beach volleyball court by the Río de la Plata, the raked fine sand gone half white, a sagging net and pennants snapping violently in the wind off the water. Two adults hold single spots on the sand, a stride apart. A muscular Argentine woman in her late twenties, thick dark ponytail, blue thermal top, drops into a low spinning sweep that scythes sand and snow upward; opposite her a compact Kenyan man in a red long-sleeve counters with a jump spinning crescent kick, powder bursting off his pivot foot. Spectators huddle in low bleachers behind the court. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, both fully framed throughout.

Pink and cyan neon from a shuttered beach bar washes a cove of fine white coral sand outside Buenos Aires, waves collapsing in the dark behind and glowing briefly in the spill. One adult works alone under it: a thickset Argentine man in his forties, sunburnt, forearms taped, sleeveless denim shirt, canvas trousers. Standing on one patch of sand, he swings a small hay bale by its twine, pivots his hips and hurls it up onto a growing stack, then another, and another, chaff drifting through the colored light. His boots dig deeper with each throw. Dreamlike, saturated, slow-motion feel. One continuous shot, slow orbit around him, he remains fully in frame, the cove otherwise empty.

A riverside scrap yard in Buenos Aires at golden hour: oil-stained concrete swept into a long open lane, baled aluminium cubes stacked into a dull silver wall, a scarred ship propeller resting on trestles, an idle sorting conveyor. Nothing stirs but one adult — a lean woman in her late twenties, warm brown skin, dark ponytail, sky-blue jersey and black shorts — driving a scuffed ball down the lane. She rolls it, throws a double step-over, drags it hard across her body, snaps a sharp turn off the outside foot and accelerates, threading between two oil drums before spinning back the way she came. One continuous shot, the camera craning down from high above to eye level, she stays fully framed.

Daylight drops in solid shafts from the clerestory of a vast cathedral nave in Buenos Aires, lighting stone flagstones worn smooth between rows of stacked chairs and scaffolding lashed to one pier. Nothing moves in the air. Two adults train down the aisle's full length: a squat Argentine man in his fifties with a grey moustache, navy work shirt, and a tall Nigerian woman in her thirties, hair wrapped, in the same heavy trousers and boots. They haul a flaked hose from a coiled pile and sprint it out, canvas snapping and slapping the stone, then drop the nozzle, wheel around and pound back for the second length. Documentary-plain, one continuous shot, slow dolly-out revealing more of the nave, both staying fully framed.

Low golden light skims a sandstone-paved square before a Buenos Aires basilica, its columned portico throwing long bars of shadow, a dry fountain basin and worn stone benches at the rim; fine dust streams low across the paving in the wind. Three adults take turns over a two-metre patch: a tall woman with silver-streaked hair in a charcoal vest, a stocky man in his twenties in oxblood, a wiry man with a shaved head in olive. One skips into a hands-free front flip; the next hurls a butterfly kick that leaves the stone entirely; the third links a cartwheel with fingertips barely brushing down. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-in; all three remain fully framed.

Sunrise mist lies flat over a frozen lagoon outside Buenos Aires, snow dusting the ice between frozen reed clumps and a leaning wooden duck blind. The air is perfectly calm. Three adults skate the open sheet: a grinning Argentine woman with a blonde ponytail in a pink jacket, a burly Jamaican man in a mustard beanie, and a slim Japanese man in bright green. They dig in from a standstill with hard crossover starts, race away toward the reeds, then wrench sideways into hockey stops that blast white sprays into the mist, laughing before setting off again in another direction. Crisp, upbeat, candy-bright. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, all three fully framed.

Noon sun hits a broad shelf of smooth wave-worn rock below ochre cliffs on the Argentine coast, tide pools glittering in its hollows, mussels crusting the seaward lip. Everything is still except the three adults planted on the dry stone. A powerfully built Argentine man in black shorts and a tall Nigerian-Argentine woman in a white sports top lock arms into a base; a small sinewy Filipina in cobalt steps up, dips, and rockets skyward, snapping a toe-touch and a half twist against the glare before folding into their cradle. Without shifting their feet they load and fire her up again. Epic, huge, sun-hammered. One continuous shot, slow pan from left to right, all three fully in frame.

Sunrise mist hangs over a beachfront promenade in Buenos Aires paved in black-and-white mosaic waves, palms lining one side and a pier fading into grey beyond. Snowflakes drift through the low shafts of light. Six adults skirmish across a few meters of mosaic: a lithe Brazilian woman in lilac, a heavyset Turkish man in a white tee, a tall Black man with locs, a pale woman with a pink buzzcut, a stocky Argentine man, and a lean Indian woman in yellow. Balls fly, bodies twist away, two dive and roll up in one motion. Onlookers lean over a railed terrace above the promenade. Soft, dreamy, pastel. One continuous shot, slow dolly-out, all six fully framed.

Hazy afternoon wind carries grit across the painted concrete circle of a helipad atop an unfinished Buenos Aires tower, idle cranes standing black against the murk while a stuttering neon sign and a wandering searchlight paint the parapet. Four adults use the marked pad and only that. A rangy Argentine man in a black bodysuit chains three cartwheels into a round-off; a broad Samoan woman in grey follows his line; a wiry Egyptian man in a red tank and a tall pale woman with a bleached crop trade round-off rebounds, drifting only a few meters before circling back. Noir, cold blues, hard silhouettes. One continuous shot, camera craning down from high above to eye level, all four fully framed.

An idled assembly floor in a Buenos Aires car plant, epoxy-coated concrete stretching between empty jigs and a stopped overhead conveyor; magenta and green stage lamps and a neon tube glow along the tool racks. Four adults in metal-plated shoes take a spot each beside the line: a curvy Afro-Argentine woman in silver, a lanky Italian-descended man in his fifties, a short woman with a platinum bob, a broad man in a red boilersuit. Nobody travels — the woman in silver rips a syncopated buffalo, the man in the boilersuit fires back a rattling flap-heel run, and all four scuff a unison break. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, everyone fully framed, feet on the concrete.

Under the glass canopy of a Buenos Aires transit plaza, colored stage lights left from an event sweep magenta and green across grey porcelain tile, and steam rolls low from floor vents beside the ticket gates. One adult anchors the middle of the concourse: a heavily built Argentine man in his thirties, buzzed dark hair, sleeveless black top, forearms corded. He whips two thick battle ropes into alternating waves, drops into a wide stance for double slams that crack against the tile, then grinds out fast outward circles, sweat flying. Commuters watch from behind a glass balustrade on the upper walkway. Bright, punchy, high-energy. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-out revealing more of the plaza, he stays fully framed.

A grain bulker lies moored at a Buenos Aires river berth, its weather deck a wide plain of oxide-red painted steel between mustard hatch coamings, a stowed provisions crane and pale silos rising beyond the rail. The sky is bruised and low, rain minutes away; jacaranda petals blown off the quay skitter across the deck. Six adults pair off, each hugging one knee up: two women and four men, twenties to fifties, in windbreakers of teal, black and orange. Hopping on one leg, they barge shoulders and hips within a few metres of deck, spinning, staggering, laughing as one after another drops a foot and is out. One continuous shot, handheld, circling slowly at chest height, all six stay fully framed.

Even overhead lighting fills a small octagon cage in a converted Buenos Aires club, the vinyl mat scuffed grey, chain-link taut, a broken neon bar sign flickering beyond it while a house searchlight swings across the far wall. Two adults share the mat and stay on their spots. A compact Argentine woman in her twenties with a tight dark braid and a coral top drops flat, chest to vinyl, snaps her feet in and rockets into a tucked jump; opposite her a tall Black man in his thirties, shaved head, black shorts, matches her rep for rep, palms cracking down, both breathing hard and counting. Fans fill the ringside seats outside the fence. One continuous shot, slow orbit around them, both fully framed throughout.

Warm tungsten work lamps hang low over an old Buenos Aires rink, throwing amber pools onto white ice ruled with faded blue lines; the boards dented, the air dead still. Four adults, all fully framed with skates on the ice, cover the sheet: a stocky Argentine man in a battered practice jersey, a tall Nigerian woman with braids under a helmet, a rangy pale man with a broken-nosed grin, and a small Vietnamese woman in black. They stride backward hard, snap open-hip pivots to forward, cut a lap and reverse again, edges hissing. A thin crowd leans on the gallery rail above. One continuous shot, slow orbit; near the end one skater glides at the lens and ends partly out of frame.

Floodlights on tall poles blast a herringbone brick plaza outside a brutalist university library in Buenos Aires, dust skimming the bricks and glowing in the beams beneath concrete fins. Five adults hold their ground in a tight arc: a fierce Argentine woman in a scarlet ruffled skirt, a silver-haired Spanish-descended man in black, a broad Black woman in emerald, a slim Peruvian man with a knotted scarf, and a tall freckled woman in indigo. Heels detonate in rattling zapateado bursts, hands arc overhead in slow braceo between attacks, skirts snapping. Students watch from a low wall behind the planters. Playful, glossy, warm-toned. One continuous shot, handheld camera slowly circling at chest height, all five fully framed.

Colored stage lights swing across a shuttered roller rink in Buenos Aires, magenta and blue skating over glossy maple while old confetti tumbles up in the draft under a slowly turning mirror globe and faded surf murals. Four adults start fully framed on a few meters of floor. A powerful Argentine woman in black shorts leans hard against a thick resistance band anchored to a rail, chopping her knees; a tall Congolese man drags a weighted sled behind her; a stocky pale man with a red beard and a wiry Japanese woman in yellow anchor and swap. Moody, neon, high contrast. One continuous shot, slow orbit; at the end the sled driver bulls toward the lens and finishes partly out of frame.

Flat even light fills an indoor pool hall in Buenos Aires, glinting off still water beside a broad deck of non-slip ceramic tile, lane reels parked against a tiled fish mural. Nothing stirs but one adult: a tall Argentine woman in her late twenties, dark hair in a low bun, teal keeper jersey, padded shorts, gloves. She shuffles low, then hurls herself sideways along the tile to smother a rolled ball, pops instantly to her feet, sets, and dives the other way, palms slapping wet ceramic. A scattering of spectators sits in the poolside bleachers. Soft, dreamy, aquamarine. One continuous shot, camera craning down from high above to eye level, she stays fully in frame.

Rain films the striped tarmac of a pit lane at a Buenos Aires circuit, garage shutters half down, a stack of scuffed tyre barriers, puddles lying flat and still. One adult occupies the wet strip: a tall woman in her thirties, deep brown skin, hair braided back, white bodysuit with a violet sash, working a long silk flag. She spins flat figure-eights at the hip, rolls the pole across her shoulders, then launches a high toss that turns four times before she catches it blind and drops to one knee. Spectators cluster in the grandstand seats behind the fence. One continuous shot, a slow pan from left to right; starting fully framed, she steps toward the lens and ends cropped at the thighs.

A single bank of floodlights blazes from one side of a bare film sound stage in Buenos Aires, carving five figures out of the dark above a matte black floor; a white cyclorama curves in one corner and sandbagged stands sit dead. Paper scraps and confetti tumble slowly through the beam. Five adults dance on their own spots: a curvy Cuban woman in a fringed orange dress and a lean Argentine man in a black shirt trade a cross-body lead into a double spin; a tall Black woman in green and a stocky Korean man mirror them; a silver-haired man in white whips solo turns between the pairs. Bright, snappy, high-energy. One continuous shot, slow dolly-out, all five fully framed.

Shafts of daylight fall from high windows into the great hall of a Buenos Aires courthouse, striping checkerboard marble between fluted columns and a brass rail, while steam creeps out of floor vents and curls through the light. Three adults stand on their own marble squares. A compact Argentine woman with a slicked ponytail and black leggings swings her arms and punches a standing back tuck, landing on the same tile; a heavy-shouldered Nigerian man in a grey vest follows with a back tuck stepped into a whip; a lean Turkish man in navy adds a standing full twist. Shadowy, cold marble tones, deliberate. One continuous shot, handheld camera slowly circling at chest height, all three fully framed, hall otherwise empty.

Hazy afternoon light dulls a wide plain of fine grey gravel south of Buenos Aires, a braided dry channel cutting past a lone boulder erratic; the haze hangs motionless and no dust lifts. Three adults hold single spots on the stones. A sinewy Argentine man in a worn white dobok pivots and fires a spinning hook kick, gravel grinding under his pivot foot; a tall Black woman with a shaved head in black training gear answers with a spinning back kick into a pad; a stocky Korean man in his forties drills the same turn slowly, then at full speed. Handheld documentary flatness, unglamorous. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, all three fully framed.

Neon from a nearby cantina bleeds pink and green across the flat bottom of a Buenos Aires skatepark, graffiti crawling up the smooth cast concrete transitions behind a chain fence. Torn paper and confetti tumble across the slab in the night air. One adult works there: a lean Argentine woman in her twenties, dark undercut, oversized black hoodie, taped hands on a wooden stick. She dekes a ball through a line of cones with quick toe drags, pulls it wide, snaps a backhand-to-forehand switch, then drifts a couple of meters and runs the slalom back. Dreamy, saturated, unhurried. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, she stays fully in frame, nobody else present.

Chalk dust hangs over the taut canvas of a small boxing ring in a Buenos Aires basement gym, even overhead lights flattening every shadow, ropes sagging, the air completely still. Three adults work inside it, moving only a couple of meters. A broad Argentine man in a blue rash guard hooks a hip throw and dumps a rangy Ethiopian woman in black onto the canvas; she rolls out and scrambles up; a heavyset Ukrainian man with cauliflower ears shoots a low single on the winner, and the three churn through a scramble before resetting for another throw. Epic, monumental, deep contrast. Spectators fill the ringside seats beyond the ropes. One continuous shot, slow dolly-out revealing more of the room, all three fully framed.

Tungsten work lamps hang between rows of idle looms in a shuttered textile mill in Buenos Aires, amber light pooling on a scarred wooden plank floor furred with thread dust. Nothing moves in the long hall. One adult stands on a single board: a thickset Argentine man in his fifties, grey stubble, leather belt, sleeves rolled over heavy forearms. He squats over a weighted keg, grips its rim, drives through his hips and hurls it backward over one shoulder; it thuds behind him, dust jumping. He turns, drags it back to the same spot, resets his stance and throws again. Noirish, amber and black, heavy. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, he stays fully framed.

Midday sun cuts through a dense bamboo grove outside Buenos Aires, striping a clearing of packed earth littered with dry leaves; culms creak and fine dust slides low across the ground. One adult labors there: a strong Argentine woman in her thirties, dark hair knotted, sweat-dark khaki shirt, gloves, boots. She drives a spade into the earth and flings arc after arc of soil and leaves sideways into the light, moving a step or two along her trench with each set, breathing hard, shoulders burning. Noir contrast, bleached highlights and inky shade. One continuous shot, slow pan from left to right, she remains fully in frame with boots on the dirt, the grove otherwise deserted.
