One continuous shot, a slow dolly-in, moody desaturated noir.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Golden light rakes a compacted fine-gravel promenade running down the median of a desert boulevard, dusty cottonwoods lining it and an empty stone fountain basin at one end; the evening is windless. Three adults use the strip: a lean Sudanese man in a black tee, a compact Italian woman with a dark bob in olive shorts, and a heavyset Native American man in a red flannel. Beginning fully in frame with feet on the gravel, they break into a hard game of tag, cutting, faking, sliding low and lunging for the tag within a few meters, gravel spraying. Onlookers watch from benches behind the boulevard railing, never on the strip. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-out, cool noir contrast.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Thick fog drifts across a mown turf airstrip beneath an unseen red butte, a limp windsock and a sagging canvas hangar tent surfacing in the murk; far off, fireworks bloom as pale halos in the sky. One man performs alone: a broad-shouldered Māori man in his thirties, hair tied back, in a sleeveless white top and grey joggers. He starts fully in frame, both boots on the turf, then rips a wooden practice staff into figure-eight spins, rolls it across his shoulders, launches a high vertical toss and catches it behind his back, shifting a few meters as he works. One continuous shot, a slow pan from left to right; he then advances until his torso crops out of frame.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Dense fog swamps an abandoned toll plaza on a desert highway, concrete lanes striped with faded arrows, booths dark, a bent canopy beam overhead; the air is heavy and unmoving. Four adults share the lanes, nobody else in sight, all fully in frame with feet on the concrete: a hulking Icelandic man with a red beard, a thick-set Nigerian woman in a black singlet, a squat Mexican man in a chalk-dusted hoodie, and a tall Russian woman with a braid. One at a time they squat over a battered keg, swing it low between the knees and hurl it backward over the shoulder, all four scattering a few meters as it thuds down. Documentary grain and grey light, one continuous shot, a slow dolly-out.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Blue hour drops over the raw poured slab of an unfinished desert tower, rebar stubs and folded tarps at the edges, a red mesa going indigo past the open sides. Five adults have the deck to themselves: a tall Kenyan woman in lime, a broad Tongan man in black tights, a pale Czech man, a curvy Trinidadian woman in fuchsia, and a wiry Japanese man in white. Lined up shoulder to shoulder, all fully in frame with feet on the slab, they blast off together and attack a row of low hurdles, three strides between each, sprinting clear across the deck and pulling up grinning at the far end. One continuous shot, a slow pan from left to right, bright energetic commercial color.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: A bruised storm sky presses down on a flat concrete amphitheater stage carved into a desert canyon, empty stone seat tiers behind, two tilted light towers flanking it, while far below headlights streak in long trails along the valley highway. Two adults work the stage alone, both fully in frame with feet on the concrete: a stout Argentinian woman in her forties with a black ponytail and a mustard tee, and a lanky Sri Lankan man in his twenties in blue shorts. Facing off a few meters apart, they hurl a heavy sandbag chest-to-chest, absorbing each catch in a deep squat, then rotating into over-the-shoulder heaves and quick shuffles. One continuous shot, the camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, playful and punchy.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Night sits on a high flowering meadow bench above a desert basin, the only light the pink-and-blue neon of a roadhouse sign at the meadow's edge, an old fence line and a stock tank catching the glow; the air is dead calm. Two adults are out here alone: a heavyset Samoan-Scottish man in a torn grey jersey and a whip-thin Ethiopian woman in a black long-sleeve. Both start fully in frame with boots in the turf, then break into a hard run in line across the meadow, snapping flat rugby laterals back and forth, drifting wide, spinning out of a shoulder check and reloading. One continuous shot, a handheld camera slowly circling at chest height, raw documentary texture.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: A sunshower hammers a cobbled stone arch bridge spanning a red-rock wash, rain streaks flashing white in the vertical midday sun and puddles bursting between the stones, a carved parapet and a leaning iron lamp over the roadway. Three adults hold the bridge, no one else, all fully in frame with feet on the cobbles: a towering Sudanese woman in a soaked black tee, a barrel-chested Croatian man in denim, and a compact Hawaiian man with taped forearms. Rotating in a tight triangle, they heave heavy grain sacks to one another, catching low, driving up from the hips and flinging on again, boots skidding a meter or two across wet cobbles. One continuous shot, a handheld camera slowly circling at chest height, epic and rain-lit.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Shafts of daylight cut through high windows into a small studio with light bamboo flooring inside an old adobe building, hanging desert plants and rolled mats along one wall; the room is perfectly quiet. Three adults train and nobody else, all fully in frame with feet on the bamboo: a tall Somali-American woman in a white dobok top and black leggings, a stocky Bolivian man in a blue rashguard, and a rangy Estonian man with a blond crop. Anchored to their own square of floor, they whip spinning hook kicks past a freestanding pad, chamber and fire back kicks, then double up with a jumping back kick, landing on the same spot each time. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-out, crisp bright sports-ad energy.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Daylight falls in wide shafts through high windows onto the red foam mat of a wrestling room in an old desert schoolhouse, chalked boards and medicine balls along the wall. Three adults use the mat, all fully in frame with feet on the foam: a lithe Haitian woman in a cropped rose top with braids, a broad Portuguese man in grey holding focus mitts, and a middle-aged Chinese woman in black holding a second pair. The boxer works between them, ripping jab-cross-hook onto one set, pivoting a couple of meters, then slipping and doubling up on the other, gloves cracking. Loose paper confetti drifts down through the light beams and settles on the mat. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-out, soft dreamlike music-video color.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Storm light turns an elevated linear park on an old rail viaduct steel-grey, tapered concrete planks running between beds of dry bunch grass with a red mesa filling the horizon; fine dust blows low along the deck. Two adults work up here: a muscular Vietnamese-American woman in a black rashguard and a tall Nigerian man in a faded orange tank holding hand paddles. Both begin fully in frame, feet on the planks. She explodes into jumping front kicks, then a flying switch kick that cracks both paddles, driving a few meters down the walkway. Onlookers watch from a stairway landing behind the railing, off the deck. One continuous shot, a slow orbit; at the end he backs toward the lens and half exits frame.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Low practice lamps leave deep shadow in a tiled concrete pedestrian underpass beneath a desert freeway, a wet gutter line running its length and a neon sign flickering at the far mouth while a searchlight sweeps past the opening. Four adults fill the tunnel, no one else, all fully in frame, feet on the tiles: a bald Lebanese man in a black shirt, a tall Swedish woman in a grey vest, a stocky Guatemalan woman with a topknot, and a slender Kenyan man in maroon. In two facing pairs a few meters apart, they blaze through club passing — fast doubles, singles across the diagonal, a duck-under exchange under a lobbed club. One continuous shot, a handheld camera slowly circling at chest height, hard-edged neo-noir.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Low grow-lamps leave deep pools of shadow along a wide concrete walkway inside a long glasshouse on the salt flats, dark vine rows either side, condensation crawling down the panes; the air is entirely still. Six adults and nobody else stand fully in frame, boots on the walkway: a burly Serbian man, a small Thai woman in a soaked apron, a tall Sudanese woman, a grey-bearded Chilean man, a broad Korean man, a freckled Irish woman. They chain full pails from a standpipe down the length of the aisle, grunting through each handover, the last two tipping into a trough and skidding the empties back along the wet concrete. One continuous shot, the camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, cold noir palette.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: The top deck of a desert parking garage floats in sunrise mist, faded stall paint peeling on the concrete, a low wall and stairwell block behind, red buttes half-dissolved beyond; nothing stirs but the pair. Two adults are up here, both fully in frame with feet on the deck: a Spanish-Roma woman in her forties in a black ruffled skirt and dark blouse, and a slim Vietnamese man in his twenties in a grey waistcoat and boots. Rooted to one square of painted concrete, they trade zapateado bursts — heel-toe drum rolls, a hard planta stamp, arms curling into slow braceo, chins snapping toward each other on the accents. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-in, brooding grey-and-amber noir.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: A dark pre-rain sky presses on a cobbled square in an old desert mining town, arcaded stone shopfronts around it, a dry basin fountain at its heart, one flickering neon sign buzzing above a doorway while a searchlight sweeps the rooftops. Two adults take the stones: a compact Filipina in a white tank and cutoffs, and a tall Ghanaian-German man in a black long-sleeve. Both stand fully in frame, feet on the cobbles, then kick to handstands and race each other several meters, palms slapping the rounded stones, breaking into hopping handstand bounds before rolling out. Bystanders watch from beneath the arcade behind the balustrade. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-out, moody neo-noir.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Colored stage lamps rigged to the ceiling wash a sealed concrete loading dock bay in a desert warehouse, roller doors half down and steam creeping from a floor vent past a stack of pallets. Four adults are inside and no one else, all fully in frame with feet on the concrete: a scarred Brazilian man in black shorts, a stocky Uzbek woman with a braid, a rangy Sudanese man in a red singlet, and a compact Danish woman in grey. Two brace kick shields while the others stay planted on one spot, snapping spinning hook kicks over the top, then reloading and driving jumping back kicks into the shields, the holders bracing without stepping away. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-in, raw documentary grain.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Mist lies on a mown grass balloon launch field beneath red-rock spires, folded nylon envelopes and a propane trailer at the treeline, while a road sign's neon flickers and a searchlight beam swings slowly overhead. Four adults use the field alone, all fully in frame with feet on the turf: a lanky Ukrainian man in a tracksuit, a muscular Black woman in a magenta top, a short Japanese woman in denim, and a bearded Iranian man in a work shirt. They send big hoops out in backspins, chase them a few meters, dive cleanly through the rolling rings and shoulder-roll up onto the wet grass, then toss them back crosswise. One continuous shot, a slow pan from left to right, unpolished documentary feel.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: A chalk downland plateau above a red desert basin surfaces out of sunrise mist, short springy turf broken by a wind-bent thorn and a stacked survey cairn; down at the basin road a neon motel sign stutters and a searchlight sweeps the ridge. One man works there alone: a heavyset Hungarian man in his forties, sleeves cut off, chalk dust on his boots. Fully in frame, feet planted in the turf and never leaving that square meter, he rips two heavy battle ropes into alternating waves, escalates into thundering double slams that batter the grass flat, then drops to a knee and keeps the waves running. One continuous shot, a handheld camera slowly circling at chest height, monumental and cinematic.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Heavy snow falls on a bare grey granite plateau above a whitening desert basin, boulder erratics scattered around a fissure venting steam across the rock. Five adults, nobody else: a broad Tongan woman in red, a wiry Norwegian man in black tights, a tall Colombian man in yellow, a stocky Indian woman in a blue thermal, and a bearded Black man in grey. All five stand fully in frame, boots on the granite, then drop — prone, seated, falling sideways — and explode upright on a clap, bursting a few meters across the rock before resetting. One continuous shot, the camera craning down from high above to eye level; on the last rep one sprinter charges the lens and crops at the waist.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Hazy afternoon light hangs over a drained paddy of cracked dry mud in a desert basin, low earth bunds and a rusted sluice gate; not a breath of wind moves. Five adults hold the field alone, all fully in frame, feet in the mud: a burly Fijian man in a torn blue jersey, a tall Dutch woman with a blonde plait, a compact Peruvian man, a broad Nigerian woman in white, and a lean Vietnamese man in green. Shoulder to shoulder they surge across the mud, passing flat and backward down the line, looping the ball around a runner, cutting inside and offloading through contact within a few meters. One continuous shot, a handheld camera slowly circling at chest height, bright and playful.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Only half the practice lamps burn above a Utah velodrome, leaving the flat grey infield concrete pooled in deep shadow beneath the steep pine track and a hanging lap-counter board. The building is silent and still. One athlete crosses it: a compact Puerto Rican man in his late twenties, dense muscle, buzzed hair, wearing a white sleeveless top and blue shorts. He sprints a curving approach, punches a hurdle step into a round-off, whips a back handspring, and snaps a tight back tuck to a stuck landing. Spectators watch from seats above the track banking. He starts fully framed with feet down; in one continuous shot the camera cranes from high above to eye level as he runs past, ending partly out of frame.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Floodlights blaze on a marble quarry's cutting floor, the sawn white stone glowing blue-white beneath a wire-saw gantry, stacked blocks and coiled hose lining the bench edge; the desert night is silent and still. A single athlete works the slab: a tall Ethiopian-American woman in her twenties, close-cropped hair, in a red training top, black shorts and chalk-white palms. She begins fully in frame with both feet on the marble, then chains cartwheel into cartwheel, spins to a one-armed cartwheel and finishes with a snapping round-off rebound, tracking a few meters along the stone. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-in toward her, clean high-contrast sports-ad energy.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Light rain glazes the red brick pavers of a small desert town square, arcaded adobe fronts and an iron bell frame mirrored in the wet stone while torn paper confetti tumbles through the drizzle. Four adults stand fully in frame, shoes planted on the bricks: a slender Korean man in a soaked white shirt, a curvy Mexican woman in a green dress, a tall Black woman in charcoal, and a grey-haired Greek man in a vest. Each holds a single spot, whipping double and triple pirouettes, then long fouetté sequences, water spraying from turning shoes, arms cutting the rain. Villagers watch from under the arcade behind a low railing. One continuous shot, the camera craning down from high above to eye level, documentary grain.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Floodlight masts blaze over a rolled dry-clay cricket strip laid on a desert flat, a rope boundary running to portable stands and a black sandstone ridge behind; the night air is glassy and still. Two adults face down the pitch: a towering Jamaican man in a white singlet and blue shorts, and a compact Kazakh woman in a black speedsuit with a dark braid. Both start fully in frame, feet on the clay, then drive out low, arms tearing, stride lengthening, and thunder the full length of the strip neck and neck to a chalk finish line, dust bursting off the clay. Spectators fill the stands beyond the rope. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-in, epic cinematic scale.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Soft overcast daylight flattens a compacted red-dirt service strip running between long rows of tilted solar panels on a desert bench, a squat inverter shed humming at one end, and far off the highway smears headlight trails across the grey haze. Three adults are alone out here: a lean Somali woman in a grey hoodie, a broad Portuguese man in a black tee, and a lanky Korean-American man in orange. From a still start, all three fully in frame with feet in the dirt, they break into a running tag game the length of the lane, cutting hard around panel legs, faking, lunging for a shoulder tap and immediately reversing the chase. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-out revealing the endless rows, epic and moody.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Colored stage lamps and cold neon tubes light a foundry casting hall, its floor a broad expanse of packed black sand, dormant ladles and a still overhead rail crane framing the space; nothing moves but the dancers. Three adults hold the floor: a tall Russian woman in electric blue, a muscular Nigerian man in white, and a slim Mexican man in scarlet. Beginning fully in frame with bare feet in the sand, they chase one another along a long diagonal, chaining chassé into grand jeté, saut de chat, and tour jeté, black sand kicking up under each landing as they cross the entire hall. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-out, vivid high-energy commercial color.

region: Utah salt flats and red-rock desert, USA
caption: Heavy snow drifts over a flat dark basalt lava field, the black pavement showing through in wind-scoured patches, a cinder cone rising behind and far away headlights drawing long trails along the desert highway. Two adults stand out here alone: a heavyset Dominican man in a navy thermal and a tall Norwegian woman with a blonde braid in a red jacket. Both are fully in frame, boots on the stone, then they begin a long-toss session — full windup, leg lift, hard drive off the back leg, snow bursting off their landings — backing steadily apart until they hold the far edges of the frame, throws whistling between them. One continuous shot, a slow orbit around them, epic and monumental.

A bruised pre-rain sky hangs over a Nairobi freight yard where rust-red containers stack four high and a bent yellow gantry waits, motionless. One adult woman, tall and lean, dark brown skin, cropped bleached curls, in a citrus-orange crop top and white shorts, stands fully in frame, shoes on the grey concrete paver blocks. She snaps into a clean triple pirouette, lands, then drives a long series of fouetté turns, working leg slicing, arms punching open on every revolution, her footprint never leaving one square metre. The air is dead calm before the rain; only she moves. Nobody else is present. One continuous shot with a slow dolly-out gradually revealing more of the surrounding stacks, pavers bright beneath her.

Golden hour bathes a black volcanic sand cove, where thin steam curls from cracked ground vents between tide-polished lava boulders. One adult man, mid-thirties, stocky and broad-shouldered, brown skin, shaved head, wearing a lime tank top and navy shorts, stands fully in frame with bare feet planted on the dark grit. He claps once, charges three quick steps, then launches headfirst into a flat belly-flop dive, skidding a couple of metres and throwing up a spray of black sand. He bounces up, jogs back, and fires off another running dive, grinning. The beach is otherwise deserted. One continuous shot, static tripod camera at eye level, warm light glittering on every airborne grain.

Dust hazes an apron beside a corrugated hangar on the Kenyan coast road, faded yellow taxi lines curving across painted concrete, a windsock snapping above the fence. Three adults stand fully in frame, shoes on the paint: a wiry young woman with box braids in a red athletic top, a broad Kenyan man in his forties in a white vest, and a slim East African man with a short afro in yellow. Each folds one leg up, grips the ankle, and hops in, shoulders barging, ricocheting apart, staggering, then hopping back for the next collision, all inside one small painted square. Beyond the fence, ocean waves crash white on a breakwater; nobody else is here. One continuous shot, static tripod camera at eye level.

Low golden light skims a weathered timber promenade on the Kenyan coast, a rusted lamp standard leaning over moored dhow masts beyond the seawall. The evening air is dead calm. Four adults start fully framed, feet on the planks: a heavyset Kenyan man in a faded green vest, a short Vietnamese woman in orange, a tall Danish woman with cropped bleached hair, a wiry Peruvian man in grey. Two crouch tight; the others vault them palm-first across five meters of decking, land, drop into crouches themselves, and the chain rolls on. Vendors watch from benches behind the railing. One continuous handheld shot circles slowly at chest height; at the end the vaulting man lands near the lens, partly out of frame.

Sodium floodlights on the silo gantry carve hard cones of light across a dusty concrete loading slab outside Nairobi, grain chutes hanging dark overhead, a parked hopper trailer casting a long black shadow. Nothing else moves. Five adults sprint a relay along the slab: a rangy Kenyan woman in maroon, a thick-set Korean man in black, a tall Nigerian man in silver, a pale Ukrainian woman with a shaved head, a broad Colombian woman in grey. They flash blind handoffs at full speed, the baton slapping into open palms, fists driving. All five start fully framed with feet on concrete; in one continuous shot the camera cranes from overhead to eye level as the anchor runs past, ending partly out of frame.

Neon reds and greens bleed across a small Nairobi courtyard floored in patterned ceramic tile, steam sighing from a kitchen vent, a wrought-iron balcony ringing the space above. Six adults stand fully in frame, feet on the tiles: three women with braids, buzzcut and long ponytail in white, teal and orange; three men in loose linen, a black vest and grey shorts, ages twenty to fifty. They swing a low capoeira ginga, ducking under sweeping kicks, breaking into cartwheels and ducking esquivas within a few metres. Drinkers lean over the balcony railing above, none on the tiles. Late on, one man cartwheels toward the lens and finishes partly out of frame. One continuous shot, slow dolly-out revealing more courtyard.

Afternoon wind drags a fine haze over a Nairobi junction repainted as a plaza, its asphalt covered in bold mural blocks of teal and coral, planter barrels marking the edges, bunting snapping hard on a line strung above. Two adults stay fully in frame on the painted surface: a muscular woman in her late twenties, medium brown skin, high ponytail, wearing a violet jersey, and a lanky man in his thirties, pale freckled skin, ginger crop, in a lemon tee. They run three-step spike approaches, arms swinging back then hammering an old volleyball over an imaginary net, chasing it a few metres before resetting. Bystanders cheer from behind the barriers. One continuous shot, slow orbit around the pair.

Mist hangs across a terraced olive grove on a ridge outside Nairobi; gnarled trunks frame a flat pad of dusty pale earth, and far below a flickering roadside sign and a sweeping searchlight throw stuttering colour up the slope. Three adults hold that pad, fully in frame, feet planted, never straying past arm's reach: a tall Kenyan woman with locs in a plum bodysuit, a compact Filipino man with a black bowl cut in white, and a fair-skinned woman in her forties, blonde bob, in silver. Their colour guard flags whirl in tight figure eights, snap flat, then rocket upward in synchronised double tosses, caught blind and rolled back into spins. No one else is here. One continuous shot, static tripod camera at eye level.

Midday sun stands directly overhead in a clearing hacked from coastal forest north of Kilifi, packed earth and dry leaf litter underfoot, a fallen strangler fig at one edge and surf crashing white through a gap in the trees. One woman holds a single spot barely a meter wide: mid-thirties, Kenyan, tall and long-limbed, hair in twists, wearing a lime tank and white cargo pants. She carves fast drop spins beside her hip, rolls the silk into a cone above her head, then rips a five-rotation toss straight up, arms crossed, and snatches the pole out of the glare. Filmed in one continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level; she stays fully framed, feet planted.

Sunrise mist softens a broad interdune flat of firm red sand ringed by ochre ridges; torn paper scraps tumble low across the ground. Five adults stand fully in frame, bare feet on the sand — a broad-shouldered woman with a shaved head in cobalt, a slight man in white, a tall Kenyan man in orange, a freckled woman with a red plait in black, a stocky man in his forties in green — then settle prone in a line, chins down. On a shout they scramble up, sprint fifteen metres and hurl themselves into full-stretch dives at a row of stubby cloth flags, sand exploding around them. The dunes are otherwise empty; the nearest sprinter ends partly out of frame. One continuous shot, slow dolly-in.

Two banks of practice lamps light one corner of a Nairobi club gym, leaving the blue spring carpet mostly in shadow beneath a wall of faded pennant bunting and a stack of chalk-dusted mats. Industrial fans push loose paper and glittering dust through the beams. A single gymnast works a lane a few meters long: early thirties, Kenyan-Indian, compact and powerful, hair in a tight bun, wearing a dusty-rose leotard. She skips into a side aerial with both arms wrapped, lands clean, punches straight into a front aerial, then floats a switch-leap and sinks into a soft dive roll. Teammates watch from benches beyond the floor's border tape. One continuous handheld shot circles her at chest height; she stays fully framed.

On a whitewashed cement rooftop above a Nairobi spice warehouse, trays of scarlet chilies sit pushed under a tin lean-to, water beading on the parapet and a cistern drum. Fine rain glosses the cement to a wet grey shine; the air itself hangs motionless. Two adults plant themselves a stride apart: a heavy-shouldered Kenyan man in a soaked black tee, and a lean Filipino woman in her forties, hair tied back, wearing a rust-red top. They hoist weighted balls overhead, drive them down onto the slick cement with a flat crack, catch the low bounce, and slam again, breath ragged. One continuous shot as the camera orbits slowly around them; both stay fully in frame, feet rooted.

Blue hour settles over a broad shelf of smooth red sandstone above a Kenyan valley, wind-carved runnels underfoot and a long escarpment fading violet behind. One adult man, early forties, tall and sinewy, deep brown skin, close-cropped grey-flecked hair, in a black singlet and white shorts, starts fully in frame with both shoes on the rock. He accelerates along the bench, drops into angled crossover steps with the javelin drawn back level, plants his block leg hard, and whips the shaft away over the drop, following through with a scrambling brake. He jogs back with a second javelin and builds the run-up again. The rock is deserted, the air motionless. One continuous shot, slow orbit around him.

Dawn mist drifts between towering timber stacks in a Nairobi sawmill yard, the floor a soft carpet of sawdust over dirt, a rusted band-saw shed at the rear, and far off above the town, fireworks pop in pale bursts. Four adults stand fully in frame on the sawdust: a cheerful Kenyan woman with short twists in white, a lanky Indian man in a grey jacket, a stocky woman in her fifties with a blonde braid, and a young man in a blue vest. In two bright pairs they explode into fencing lunges with sport foils, blades ticking, parrying, riposting, retreating a metre and attacking again, laughing between hits. No one else is around. One continuous shot, static tripod camera at eye level.

An emptied Nairobi exhibition hall stretches away under low moody work lights, half-struck booth frames casting skeletal shadows on grey commercial carpet while a rented searchlight rig sweeps flickering neon bars across the far wall. Four adults hold their marks on the carpet, fully in frame: a broad Kenyan woman with a low fade in electric blue, a wiry man with a topknot in white, a heavyset Pacific Islander man in red, and a tanned woman in her late thirties in yellow. Each faces a black plyo box, swings the arms, and detonates upward into a tight tucked box jump, steps down, and reloads instantly, feet never wandering. The hall holds nobody else. One continuous shot, slow dolly-in toward them.

Deep shadow pools along a curling sheet inside a Nairobi ice rink, dim practice lamps glowing over pebbled ice, painted house rings blurred beneath frost, a dead scoreboard hanging above. Scraps of torn paper drift lazily through the cold air. Three adults hold their ground on the ice, fully in frame: a tall woman with silver-dyed waves in teal pads, a young man with dark curls in white, and a broad man in his forties, ruddy-skinned, in maroon. In goalie gear they drop again and again into butterfly slides, knees flaring, blocker and glove snapping out at imagined low shots, popping back to their skates on the same spot. Spectators watch from tiered seats behind the boards. One continuous shot, slow dolly-out.

Fog rolls thick over a floodlit Nairobi tennis court, its blue acrylic surface pocked by falling rain, chain-link fencing dissolving into white, a sagging net barely visible. Five adults stand fully in frame, shoes splashing on the wet coating: a woman with long braids in a lilac hoodie, a slim man in a white shell jacket, a heavyset man in olive, a short-haired woman in her forties in red, and a young man in denim. Each toprocks in a tight bounce, then drops a hand and cycles into six-step footwork, legs scything through puddles, rising back to toprock and dropping again, each holding one small square. Watchers cluster behind the fence, off the court. One continuous shot, slow orbit around them.

Flat overcast light drains color from a wide tidal sand flat at low water south of Mombasa, the rippled wet sand cut by shallow drain channels, a stranded mooring buoy and a black wreck rib far out. Nothing moves but the people. Five adults train in pairs: a huge Kenyan man in grey, a wiry Japanese woman in navy, a tall Nordic man with a beard, a stocky Brazilian woman, a shaven-headed Egyptian man. Four hoist partners across their shoulders and pound thirty meters through the sand, swapping carriers halfway, while the fifth calls time. All five start fully framed, feet down; as the camera pans slowly from left to right, one carrier charges past it, ending partly out of frame. One continuous shot.

Thick fog sits in a quarry bench outside Machakos, blurring the terraced rock face and parked screening plant; compacted aggregate crunches underfoot, the air hangs still. Six adults form a line across the bench: two Kenyan women in white, a burly Samoan man in charcoal, a slight Malaysian woman in teal, a bald Russian man in maroon, and a freckled American woman in olive. They swing flags flat at waist height, then send them arcing sideways down the line, each dancer stepping a meter or two to catch a neighbor's pole and push it on, before a unison horizontal spin. All six remain fully framed, boots on the rock, in one continuous shot as the camera cranes down from high above to eye level.

Hard floodlights blast in from one side of a Nairobi indoor sprint hall, throwing long stripes across blue polyurethane lanes; big wall fans push loose paper and dust skating over the surface. One adult man, late twenties, thickset and cheerful, dark brown skin, a bright bandana over short hair, wearing a striped tank top and red shorts, stands fully in frame with both shoes on the track. He squats, cups a battered steel keg, drives up through his hips and slings it backward over his shoulder, spinning to watch it thud and roll a couple of metres, then chases it, hauls it back, and repeats the heave with a whoop. The hall is otherwise empty. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling at chest height.

Half the overhead lamps are dark in a maintenance hangar at a Nairobi airfield, leaving painted grey concrete lit in pools beside a wingless fuselage on jacks and a rolling stair unit. Nothing stirs. Three adults in worn judo gi work a few meters of floor: a broad Kenyan man in white, a lean Japanese woman in blue, a tall Nigerian-British man in white. Two grip lapels and trade uchi-mata entries, hips loading, until one lifts and turns his partner over in a controlled landing, both rolling back to their feet while the third resets grips. All start fully framed, feet down; in one continuous handheld orbit at chest height, one man steps toward the lens and ends partly out of frame.

Sunrise mist lies over a decommissioned runway outside Nairobi, faded threshold bars ghosting through the grooved asphalt, and far beyond the perimeter fence the headlights of early traffic streak past in long ribbons. Two adults stand fully in frame on the asphalt: a tall Kenyan woman, late twenties, locs tied back, in a green keeper jersey and padded gloves, and a stocky man in his fifties, weathered pale skin, silver crew cut, in orange. They take turns firing a scuffed ball low and wide while the other explodes sideways into full-stretch diving saves, smothering, popping back up, and shuffling a few metres for the next serve. The runway is empty of anyone else. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-out revealing the vast strip.

Rain glazes the pale limestone forecourt of a Nairobi museum until the whole square shines wet; a dry fountain basin sits dark at its centre, bronze plinths flanking it, and far off above the skyline fireworks bloom in muted gold. One adult woman, mid-thirties, tall and whip-thin, brown skin, wet hair slicked into a knot, wearing a black rashguard and charcoal trousers, stands fully in frame with bare feet on the stone. She chambers, snaps a spinning hook kick that flings a rope of water, lands, pivots, and drives a hard back kick, then steps a metre sideways and repeats the combination the other way. The square holds nobody else. One continuous shot, static tripod camera at eye level.

Blue hour drains the colour from an estate basketball court in Nairobi: black painted asphalt with faded key lines, a bent hoop with no net, laundry lines strung dark above the wall. The air does not move. Two adults hold their ground fully in frame, shoes squeaking on the paint: a broad-shouldered man in his forties, deep brown skin, shaved head, in a slate hoodie with the sleeves cut off, and a lean woman in her late twenties, tan skin, black ponytail, in a graphite tee. Facing scarred wooden plyo boxes, they load deep, punch the arms through and rip upward, knees tucking, landing silent on top, dropping off and rebounding again in tightening rhythm. Nobody else is present. One continuous shot, slow dolly-in.

Bruised storm clouds pile above a Nairobi ballpark, the raked red dirt infield glowing against the darkening sky while steam creeps from drain vents along the dugout wall. One adult man, early thirties, powerfully built, dark brown skin, hair in short twists, wearing a white uniform top and crimson leggings, starts fully in frame with cleats set in the dirt. Long silver streamers knotted at his wrists, he tears away in a curving sprint that carries him right across the frame, ribbons snapping in a bright wake, then cuts hard around an imaginary bag and gallops back the other way in huge bounding strides. Spectators fill the covered stand far behind the fence, none on the dirt. One continuous shot, slow dolly-out.

A red-painted cycle lane runs beside a Nairobi expressway at night, closed off by plastic barriers, neon signage from a shuttered mall washing the tarmac magenta and cyan; a dead traffic mast leans overhead. The air is completely still. One man drives a loaded steel sled up the lane: forties, Kenyan, thick through the chest and shoulders, shaved head, in a torn white sleeveless shirt and black shorts, calves flexing with every stride. He grinds twenty-five meters, resets, and goes again, the sled scraping loud on the paint. He begins fully framed with both feet planted; in one continuous shot the camera dollies slowly in until he pushes past its edge, partly out of frame.

Soft overcast light flattens a grid of salt evaporation pans on the Kenyan coast, low earth walls dividing sheets of ankle-deep brine over crusted white salt, a rusted sluice gate and pyramid of harvested salt nearby. No wind touches the water. Five adults chase and splash a few meters across one pan: a tall Kenyan woman in a soaked yellow dress, a stocky Portuguese man in blue, a slender Thai woman in white, a bearded Canadian man in grey, a broad Zambian woman in green. They stomp great sheets of brine at each other, scoop and fling handfuls, twist away laughing, and kick low arcs of spray. One continuous shot; the camera orbits slowly around them, all five fully framed with feet in the shallows.

Late golden light slants through a hillside apple orchard outside Nairobi, gnarled trees in ragged rows, leaning wooden fruit crates stacked at the headland, and a low skein of dust blowing across the clover and grass underfoot. One adult woman, early forties, sturdy and sun-worn, tan skin, greying brown hair in a short ponytail, wearing a faded green keeper jersey, scuffed gloves and black shorts, stands fully in frame with boots pressed into the turf. She sets, shuffles two steps, then hurls herself sideways to smother a low ball among the fallen fruit, rolls, springs up, and immediately dives the other way, grass torn loose in her wake. The orchard holds no one else. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling at chest height.

A low black storm front hangs over a five-a-side turf pitch wedged between Nairobi tower blocks, chain-link fence sagging at one corner, steam pouring from a laundry vent on the neighboring roof and drifting across the green synthetic grass. Two adults cover the full length of the pitch: a long-limbed Kenyan woman in a coral leotard and a compact Bulgarian man in black, both trailing six-meter satin ribbons. They carve overhead spirals, run diagonal lines whipping snake patterns behind them, and punch into split leaps and fast chaîné turns at the far touchline. Neighbors watch from balconies above the fence. Filmed as one continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, both stay fully in frame, feet on the turf.

Blue-hour light lingers over a highland lavender farm above the Rift escarpment, chalky gravel path cutting between hedged purple rows, a stone drying shed with two work lamps burning at its door. A freak cold-front flurry drifts through those beams. Two adults train on the gravel: a tall Kenyan man in a black dobok with the jacket tied at his waist, and a muscular Colombian woman in white, hair braided tight. They snap alternating spinning hook kicks past each other's heads, pivot low, and fire back kicks into a held pad, shuffling a couple of meters between exchanges. One continuous shot as the camera cranes from high above down to eye level; both stay fully framed, feet on gravel.

Snow falls hard on the highlands above Nairobi, dusting a strip of dry cracked soil at the edge of a field of frost-bent sunflowers; over the far ridge, fireworks crack in bright, muffled bursts. Two adults stand fully in frame with boots set in the soil: a powerfully built woman in her thirties, brown skin, hair wrapped in a red band, wearing a bright yellow thermal top, and a wiry man in his fifties, weathered dark skin, grey stubble, in blue coveralls. One swings a heavy grain sack low between her knees, heaves it high across the two-metre gap; the other catches it chest-first, absorbs, pivots and slings it straight back, breath steaming. Nobody else is out. One continuous shot, slow orbit around them.

Light rain patters over a Nairobi brickyard, the fired clay tile floor gone glossy with puddles under a rattling tin awning, drying racks of unfired blocks stacked along one wall. Five adults keep to their spots, all fully in frame, shoes on the tiles: a bouncing young woman with box braids in a pink crop top, a stocky Kenyan man in a white vest, a tall woman in her forties with a blonde bun in teal, a slim Korean man in yellow, and a broad man in grey. In pairs plus one rotating, they crack out one-two-hook-uppercut combinations into focus mitts, gloves popping, mitt-holders answering with playful counters they duck. No one else is around. One continuous shot, slow pan from left to right.

Inside a highway tunnel closed for repairs beneath Nairobi's ring road, only maintenance lamps glow, half of them dead, so the asphalt lies in long stripes of dim orange and deep shadow; steam curls from a ventilation grille in the tiled wall. Three adults tumble down the empty carriageway one after another: a rangy Kenyan man in red shorts, a broad Chinese woman in a black crop top, and a curly-haired Spanish man in grey. Each sprints, drives a round-off, snaps two flic-flacs in a row, and finishes with a punched back tuck, feet slapping the asphalt. One continuous shot; the camera tracks sideways at a steady walking pace, keeping all three fully in frame.

Neon spill from a nearby matatu stage paints a freight depot platform outside Nairobi in pink and green, stacked pallets and a spray-marked boxcar looming behind, dust streaming low across the weathered concrete. Two adults race side by side: a lanky Kenyan woman in a lime tracksuit, hair in a high puff, and a heavyset Samoan man in orange shorts, both grinning. Each shoves an empty steel drum ahead with both palms, sprinting it thirty meters down the platform, correcting a wobble, spinning the barrel around a bucket marker and hammering back. Both begin fully framed with feet on the concrete and remain in frame throughout, filmed as one continuous shot with the camera orbiting slowly around them.

Sunrise mist hangs low over Nairobi's northern line, where a commuter platform's tactile-edged concrete runs damp past a bent timetable frame and two empty luggage trolleys beside a peeling canopy post. Beyond the fence, headlights streak in long trails along the flyover. Five adults line up with ankles bound in cloth strips: a broad Kenyan man in a red vest, a slim Ugandan woman in yellow, a tall grey-haired Polish man in green, a stocky Indonesian woman in blue, and a lean Ghanaian man in white. Two pairs stagger and lurch forty meters down the platform, gripping shoulders, while the fifth chases as caller. All five stay fully in frame, feet slapping concrete, in one continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level.

Portable floodlights on tripods blaze across a wind-packed snowfield high on Mount Kenya's shoulder, a research hut's neon strip flickering pink while two searchlights sweep the ridge. Six adults skirmish over forty meters of crusted snow: a tall Kenyan woman in a purple shell, a stocky Bolivian man in yellow, a broad Norwegian woman in red, a wiry Indian man in teal, a bald Ghanaian man in orange, a freckled Irish woman in white. They scoop and hurl packed snow, sprint between drift banks for cover, duck, and dive flat, spraying powder. Everyone starts fully framed with boots on the snow and stays in frame, one continuous shot, the camera craning from high above down to eye level.

Storm light presses down on the cloister of a hilltop mission monastery above the Rift, worn flagstones ringed by whitewashed arches, bougainvillea spilling over a cast-iron bell frame; fog banks roll through the arcade in slow grey waves. Two adults each hold a single flagstone: a wiry Kenyan man in a faded blue shirt, barefoot, and a broad-shouldered Croatian woman in her thirties, cropped blonde hair, green shorts. They keep a scuffed ball airborne between them — inside-foot taps, thigh bounces, a shoulder flick, headers traded back and forth — never letting it touch stone. Robed figures watch from the shadowed arcade behind the columns. One continuous shot, the camera dollying slowly in; both stay fully framed, feet down.

Soft overcast light sits evenly on a coffee drying patio outside Thika, its smooth concrete slab swept clean, raised drying beds and a stack of jute sacks at the far edge, hills flattened to grey behind. The morning is completely calm. Three adults ring a battered truck tire lying flat: a broad Kenyan woman in a mustard tee, a lean Peruvian man in denim overalls, and a heavyset Maori man in a white vest. Each swings a long sledgehammer overhead in turn, driving it down into the rubber with a thudding crack, hips snapping, hammers rebounding, all three rooted to one spot. Filmed as one continuous shot, the camera dollies slowly toward them; everyone stays fully framed, feet on the concrete.

Bright even worklights fill a small Nairobi proscenium stage, its black painted plywood scuffed pale at the marks, velvet legs hanging heavy either side, a scaffold of neon tubes upstage flickering while two follow spots sweep the deck. Three adults trick within a few meters of one another: a lean Kenyan man in loose grey, a powerful Trinidadian woman in a black unitard, and a shaggy-haired Italian man in white. He swings through a raiz, she answers with a hyper-hook into a corkscrew twist, and the third launches a cheat-gainer that lands square on the plywood. An audience watches from the raked seats beyond the stage lip. One continuous shot, camera panning slowly left to right; all stay fully framed.

Black cloud stacks over a raised park terrace on Nairobi's Karura edge, its crushed decomposed granite raked flat, a low stone retaining wall and a bent flagpole with nothing flying. The air is heavy and dead still. One man occupies a single spot: early fifties, Kenyan-Somali, tall and rangy, greying temples, a sleeveless charcoal shirt and long shorts, batting gloves worn through. He loads over his back foot, drives a wooden bat through a ball resting on a rubber tee, sends it out over the wall, resets another, and hammers again, hips rotating hard on each cut. One continuous handheld shot circles him slowly at chest height; he stays fully in frame, feet on the gravel.

Hazy afternoon light hangs like gauze over a Moscow coal plant stockyard, where black coal dust lies packed and flat beneath a rusted conveyor bridge and two pale cooling towers. Six adults stand fully in frame, feet planted on the dark ground: a tall Black woman in a violet crop top, a stocky white man with a grey beard in orange shorts, a lean East Asian man in teal, a red-haired woman in white, a broad Latino man in navy, a shaven-headed woman in lime. In one continuous shot they explode forward together, clearing a long row of low hurdles and covering the whole yard. Air is dead still; only the runners move. A static tripod camera at eye level watches, dreamy and soft-edged.

Inside a columned arcade walkway in central Moscow, polished terrazzo runs between rows of veined marble pillars, brass planters and fogged glass doors. Three adults work here: a heavyset South Asian man in a grey singlet, a freckled woman with a copper braid in black tights, and a wiry older man with silver stubble in a maroon rash guard. Two shoot repeated double-leg takedowns, levels dropping, hips driving, bodies lowering and lifting within a few paces while the third feeds resistance and resets. All stay whole in frame, feet on the stone, one continuous shot, camera orbiting slowly around them. Harsh floodlights rake in from one side; the air is dead calm. Spectators lean over a railing far behind the columns, off the floor entirely.

A cavernous turbine hall on Moscow's outskirts: checker plate steel underfoot, a row of chipped green generator casings, an idle overhead crane parked in the dark. One man occupies it — mid-thirties, Middle Eastern, close-cropped hair, a black double-breasted jacket over charcoal trousers, a snare drum slung at his hip. He begins fully in frame, boots on the plate, then marches the length of the hall in one continuous shot, hammering rolls and rimshots, snapping crisp pivot turns at each column before driving on again. Harsh floodlights from a single side carve his silhouette; everything else is motionless. The camera tracks sideways at a steady walking pace, keeping him whole against the neo-noir blacks and cold metallic greys.

Thick fog sits on a film studio backlot street outside Moscow, where painted asphalt fakes a boulevard beneath plywood shopfronts, a dummy tram pole and a dead streetlamp bleeding milky halos. Two dancers hold the empty road: a tall Nordic woman with an ash-blonde bun in a slate leotard and a compact Afro-Brazilian man in a black tank and cropped trousers. Both stay fully visible, feet turned out on the painted surface, working a tight column of pirouettes — doubles into triples, then whipping fouetté turns, arms snapping to spot the lens, footprint never wider than a metre. Nothing else stirs in the still, heavy air. One continuous shot from a static tripod camera at eye level, moody neo-noir contrast.

On a disused military parade ground of flat grey asphalt, whitewashed kerbs and a row of bare flagpoles frame long barracks in golden-hour light. Fog banks roll low across the far end, swallowing the buildings and glowing amber. Six adults stand rooted on the tarmac, fully in frame: a barrel-chested Slavic man in a rust vest, a muscular Kenyan woman in blue, a tattooed Filipino man in white, a grey-haired woman in olive, a red-bearded man in green, a broad woman in mustard. Each squats, swings a battered metal keg between the knees, and hurls it backward over one shoulder, resetting on the spot. Onlookers watch from a raised concrete stand behind railings. One continuous shot, slow dolly-out widening the yard.

Storm light presses on a cracked white salt crust stretching toward a wind-beaten reservoir, its surf audible and visible as grey waves crash along the far bank; leaning survey posts and a stranded skiff mark the flat. Four adults run it: a lanky Ethiopian man in yellow, a broad-shouldered Korean woman in crimson, a pale man with a dark ponytail in white, and a heavyset woman with cropped silver hair in blue. All start fully in frame with shoes on the salt, then tear across it, slapping a baton hand-to-hand at full sprint speed, the exchange repeating down the line. One continuous shot, camera orbiting slowly around them, gritty documentary grain under a bruised, rain-heavy sky.

Down in a Moscow underground parking garage, epoxy-coated concrete gleams under magenta and cyan tubes strung between numbered bays; big industrial fans on stands push loose paper scraps and dust skittering across the floor. Two adults own one bay: a tall Sudanese woman with box braids in a silver puffer and black joggers, and a stocky white man in his forties, buzzcut, wearing a chrome-zip tracksuit. They stay planted on a single square metre, firing robotic pop hits, chest isolations, ticking neck snaps and long arm waves that pass cleanly between them. Both remain fully in frame, feet on the concrete. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-out revealing more ramp and pillars, bright energetic colour.

Between four panel blocks in a Moscow apartment courtyard, interlocking concrete pavers form a small floodlit clearing beside a splintered sandbox and sagging washing lines. Neon from a corner shop flickers on the walls while a searchlight sweeps the towers above. One woman is here: mid-forties, Vietnamese, wiry, hair pinned tight, wearing a faded grey sweatshirt tied at the waist over black leggings and worn canvas shoes. She holds one spot on the pavers, rising into repeated pirouettes, then whipping a run of fouetté turns, her free leg lashing, breath visible under the lamps. She stays fully in frame throughout. One continuous shot, the camera orbiting slowly around her, documentary-plain and unglamorous.

Hazy afternoon wind carries dust across a hotel pool deck high over Moscow, pale travertine tile still wet at the pool lip, folded loungers strapped down, a neon strip on the next tower flickering while searchlights swing over the skyline. Five adults each claim a tile square: a rangy Russian woman in electric blue, a stocky Ethiopian man in orange, a tattooed Brazilian woman in white, a bald Filipino man in green, a tall German woman in yellow. Ropes hum as they run fast boxer steps, fold into criss-crosses, then explode into bursts of triple-unders, forearms whipping. One continuous shot, the camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace; all five stay fully framed, feet on the tile.

Light rain lacquers granite setts along a pedestrianized Moscow shopping street, doubling the iron lamp posts, a shuttered flower kiosk and a dripping arch in the wet stone. One man works the open lane: early thirties, Afro-Caribbean, lean and long-limbed, barefoot, in loose black trousers and a dark open jacket. He begins fully in frame, soles on the setts, then travels a few metres up and down the slick lane, unloading spinning hook kicks that sling water off his heel, chambering a hard back kick, resetting his guard and repeating in the other direction. He never leaves the frame. Sheltered onlookers watch from beneath a colonnade behind barriers, never on the stones. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-in, neo-noir blacks and cold reflections.

Golden hour turns a packed-dirt farmyard honey-coloured: a timber barn with peeling blue doors, stacked tractor tyres, a lopsided hay stack, air perfectly still. Five adults spar across a few metres of level dirt — a freckled Irish woman with a ginger bun in a pink tank, a solid Uzbek man in a white vest, a tall Black man in yellow shorts, a wiry woman with a dark bob in green, and a silver-haired man in a blue singlet. Gloves up, they trade jabs and hooks, slipping and rolling under punches, ducking and bobbing with grins, feet shuffling but never leaving the yard. All stay fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a walking pace.

Thick fog swallows a Moscow athletics oval, leaving only red rubber tartan and its chalk-white lane lines glowing beneath a drowned mast light. The air itself is motionless, heavy as wool. One dancer stands on the third lane: a woman in her fifties, Spanish, strong-shouldered, black hair coiled low, in a long charcoal skirt and a deep-red fitted top, heeled shoes striking the track. She never leaves her spot, driving thunderous zapateado bursts — heel, toe, heel — arms curling overhead in slow braceo before snapping down for another volley. She stays fully in frame. Spectators sit far off in a fogged concrete stand behind the railing. One continuous shot, the camera craning down from high above to eye level, epic and vast.

A cold storage warehouse near Moscow: frosted concrete floor, towering pallet racks of shrink-wrapped crates, milky plastic strip curtains, and vents breathing slow ribbons of freezing steam across the aisle under flat, bright overhead light. Five adults take a short run-up in turn — a rangy Somali man in a black hoodie, a compact Japanese woman in grey, a heavyset man with a shaved head in navy, a tall woman with bleached hair in maroon, and a bearded man in olive. Each attacks a low steel crate with a kong vault, hands punching the top, legs shooting through, landing and jogging back within a few metres. All remain fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, cold neo-noir tones.

Fog drifts low over a powdery white gypsum flat, dunes fading into milk while pale fireworks burst silently far above a black treeline. One woman stands on the crust: late twenties, Brazilian, athletic, dark curls tied back, wearing a cropped grey top, loose white trousers rolled at the ankle, barefoot. She keeps to a single patch, coiling and unleashing spinning kicks that fan great arcs of gypsum dust into the fogged air, dropping to a low sweep, then rising for another rotation. She stays fully in frame with feet on the flat throughout. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-in toward her, moody neo-noir palette of bone white and deep blue-black.

A municipal badminton hall in Moscow has been rigged for a jam: green vinyl mats, sagging nets pushed to one wall, and a truss of magenta and cyan lamps that flicker while a searchlight sweeps the block walls. Four adults hold their own squares of court — a lean Ghanaian man in a white tracksuit, a stocky woman with a bleached crop in denim, a tall Kazakh man in red, and a woman in her forties with long black hair in a purple hoodie. Each toprocks in place, shoulders bouncing, then drops to hands and cycles crisp six-step footwork before popping back up. All stay fully in frame. One continuous shot, slow dolly-out. Spectators crowd bleachers along the far wall.

Storm clouds bruise the sky above a hydroelectric dam crest roadway, concrete marked with fading white lane lines, spillway gates yawning on one side and a valley of streaking traffic light trails far below. Six adults line up fully in frame, boots on the concrete: a burly Slavic man in a brown jacket, a tall Congolese woman in teal, a wiry man with a topknot in grey, a broad woman in a red anorak, a bearded man in denim, a shaven-headed woman in yellow. Each climbs into a coarse sack and they hop the length of the crest, two tumbling and scrambling upright to chase the rest, all staying fully in frame. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling slowly at chest height.

Golden light slides down a canal-side quay in Moscow, grey cobble setts running past iron mooring rings, a rust-streaked barge and a low bridge, while fireworks bloom small and distant above the rooftops. One man works the walkway: mid-thirties, Chinese, compact and powerful, black hair short, in a red sleeveless top, wide black trousers and flat cloth shoes. He begins fully in frame, feet on the cobbles, then drops into deep crouches and explodes forward in long lion-dance pounces, landing wide, springing again, covering the quay toward the lens until his shoulders and head crop past the edge of frame. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-in, neo-noir amber and shadow.

A decommissioned Moscow metro platform runs long and tiled, chipped mosaic pillars marching beside a black track trench; warm tungsten work lamps hang on cables while a stray searchlight and a flickering neon tube wash the arched ceiling. Five adults take the platform: a slim Sri Lankan man in white shorts, a muscular blonde woman in black, a tall Black woman with a shaved head in orange, a stocky man with a moustache in grey, and a lean red-headed man in blue. From standing, all kick up and race hand-walking down the platform, some breaking into bouncing handstand hops before dropping and running back. Everyone stays fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera orbiting slowly, dreamy haze.

Misty sunrise softens a closed city street in Moscow — asphalt with a broad white crosswalk, sagging tram wires, a shuttered bakery and orange barriers at both ends. The air is completely still. Five adults sprint the length of it: a tall Puerto Rican man in a white jersey, a broad-shouldered woman with dark curls in green, a lean Estonian man in navy, a stocky bald man in yellow, and a fast woman with a braided ponytail in pink. They break crisp routes across the crosswalk, cutting hard, then reaching back for over-the-shoulder catches of a spiralling ball, whooping. All stay fully in frame. Bystanders cheer from behind the barriers on the pavement. One continuous shot, camera orbiting slowly.

Only two work lamps burn in a faded ballroom of a Moscow hotel awaiting renovation, throwing deep shadows over herringbone parquet, a chandelier bagged in plastic overhead, mirrors turned to the wall and draped. Nothing in the room moves but three adults, each rooted to their own patch of floor: a broad Russian man in a black tank, a compact Kenyan woman with locs in maroon, a slim Vietnamese-French man in grey. In turn they wind and rip standing full twists, drop straight into low butterfly twists, and finish with an aerial hooking into a landing barely a step wide. Filmed in one continuous shot, the camera cranes from high above down to eye level; all three stay fully framed.

Hazy afternoon light drifts over a train station forecourt in Moscow, dark basalt setts spread beneath a green clock tower, striped kiosk awnings and a flatbed cart heaped with hay. The air is oddly still. One man works there: late twenties, Russian-Armenian, thickset, dark stubble, in a sweat-darkened grey shirt with rolled sleeves, canvas trousers and heavy boots. He starts fully in frame on the setts, hooking bale after bale and heaving them up onto a growing stack, striding a few metres between cart and pile. On his last throw he steps toward the lens and his torso crops out of frame. Travellers watch from behind a barrier by the station doors. One continuous shot, a slow pan from left to right.

Night on a short-grass prairie beyond Moscow's ring: cropped dry grass runs to a leaning fence line, and a lone roadhouse throws pink and green neon across the field. Leaves and dry petals swirl low over the ground, chasing the runners' heels. Two adults face a taped finish line far off: a tall Sudanese woman with a shaved head in a black crop and shorts, and a broad Slavic man in his forties, blond, in a faded red singlet. Both start fully in frame, spikes in the grass, then explode into a head-to-head race, arms driving, shoulders level, tearing across the field to the tape, neither leaving the frame. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, raw handheld documentary texture.

One woman commands the aluminium stage deck of a riverside festival platform in Moscow, scaffolding towers and long banner cloth snapping above her. She is tall and broad-shouldered, mid-thirties, Afro-Caribbean, with bleached twists, a lime windbreaker and cropped orange trousers. For the first seconds she stands fully framed, boots flat on the ribbed metal. Then she drives a jab-step forward, snaps two sharp chest pulses, whips one arm across her body into a low buck-hop, and repeats the combination two meters across the deck. Beyond the barricade, a packed crowd fills the field below the deck. Blue-hour sky, one continuous shot, a handheld camera slowly circling at chest height as she stalks toward the lens and her shoulder leaves the frame.

Light rain slicks a gravel service road threading an oil refinery outside Moscow; puddles between the stones mirror pipe racks, a squat storage sphere and a flare stack burning pale against low cloud. Everything else is motionless. One thrower stands on the gravel: a man in his forties, Pacific Islander, enormous through the shoulders, hair cropped, in a bright blue compression top, white shorts and studded boots. Fully in frame, he crouches with a steel shot tucked at his neck, glides back across a single metre, whips his hips open and launches with a shout, then resets and repeats, boots grinding wet stone. He never leaves his spot. One continuous shot, a slow pan from left to right, crisp and energetic.

Rain falls steadily on a beach volleyball court beside the Moskva, raked fine sand darkening under it, a sagging net and blank banners strung between poles while shreds of confetti and paper scraps tumble through the wet air. Five adults work the sand: a towering Icelandic man in a black long-sleeve, a Black woman with braided hair in white, a compact Peruvian man in red, a strong woman with a blonde crop in grey, and a bearded man in green. One drops back three steps and fires tight spirals; the others break, plant and catch, all within a few metres. Everyone stays fully in frame. Spectators fill low bleachers behind the boundary. One continuous shot, slow dolly-out, epic and cinematic.

Night. A stretch of fine white coral sand glows under strings of pink and blue neon slung between driftwood posts, with lit boats moored motionless offshore and the air completely still. Four adults each take a patch of sand: a lean Indian man in loose white trousers, a tall woman with silver-dyed hair in a black bodysuit, a broad Māori man bare-chested in blue shorts, and a woman in her fifties with a grey braid in a teal wrap. Rooted in place, they whip spinning kicks that throw fans of glittering sand up through the neon, drop into low crouching sweeps, then reload. All stay fully in frame. One continuous shot, a slow pan from left to right, dreamy and saturated.

Soft overcast daylight flattens a scrap metal recycling yard in Moscow: oil-stained concrete, stacked cubes of crushed cars, bales of bright wire and a magnet crane hanging dead still. Nothing moves in the yard but one woman — early thirties, Korean, sinewy, hair in a tight ponytail, in a mustard windbreaker, black leggings and scuffed trainers. Fully in frame at first, she drops flat to the concrete, then bursts upright into a short sprint; she flops seated, spins and explodes again; she lets herself fall sideways and scrambles up mid-stride. Her final start carries her at the lens until her upper body leaves the frame. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling slowly at chest height, hazy dreamlike softness.

Bright even light fills a long cathedral nave in Moscow, worn stone flagstones running between painted piers and iron candle stands; votive flames flicker and a work lamp swinging on a cable rakes the vaults like a searchlight. One man plays the aisle alone: late twenties, Ethiopian, whippet-thin, hair in short twists, wearing a green jersey, black shorts and battered boots. Fully in frame with feet on the stone, he drives a ball the length of the nave, chases it down, and hammers power shots into a stack of padding, then flicks it up and smashes full volleys out of the air, jogging back to repeat, never leaving the frame. One continuous shot, static tripod camera at eye level, bright and playful.

Thunderheads press low over a cathedral forecourt in Moscow, sandstone paving spreading wide before onion domes and iron lampposts; a nearby neon strip stutters and a sweeping searchlight rakes the facade. One woman crosses the square: mid-twenties, Mexican, athletic, dark hair loose, wearing a canary tracksuit and white trainers, gripping two long ribbon streamers in orange and turquoise. She starts with both trainers planted on the sandstone, then sprints the paving corner to corner, breaking into big galloping bounds and whirling the streamers into long twisting trails behind her, never slipping out of frame. Tourists watch from behind the low chain barrier at the edges, never on the paving. One continuous shot, slow dolly-out revealing more of the square, bright and playful.

Misty sunrise turns a frozen lake outside Moscow into pale grey glass, snow dusting the ice in streaks, two plywood fishing huts and a birch shoreline dissolving in the haze. The air is entirely still. Two adults skate a cleared patch: a tall Ukrainian man in his forties, greying, in a black thermal top and navy trousers, and a compact Black woman in a maroon fleece and grey leggings. Each holds one spot, sinking into a two-foot spin, then pulling arms in tight for a fast scratch spin that shaves fine white powder off the ice, coasting out and setting up again. Both stay fully in frame. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, plain documentary realism.

Harsh midday sun bleaches a flat shelf of wave-worn rock at a reservoir shore, smooth stone sloping to green water beside a rusted ladder and a bleached stump; a strip of festival neon on the far bank flickers while a searchlight beam wanders the cliffs. Three adults work the shelf: a broad Georgian man with a black beard in white, a strong Black woman with a high ponytail in navy, and a small, springy woman with a copper pixie cut in gold. The two bases lock hands and launch the flyer straight up in a basket toss, catching her clean, then resetting and tossing again from the same spot. All stay fully in frame. One continuous shot, slow orbit, dreamy shimmering light.

Five adults line up on a wave-patterned black-and-white mosaic promenade beside a Moscow reservoir beach, where kiosk neon stutters and a moored boat sweeps searchlight beams across the tiles under flat grey daylight: a stocky bald Korean man in a red singlet, a freckled redhead woman in denim shorts, a lanky South Asian man in yellow, a silver-haired white woman in teal, and a muscular Black man in white. All five start fully in frame, feet on the mosaic, then crouch and shove empty blue plastic barrels at a sprint down a four-metre lane, spin them around a chalk mark and drive back, laughing. Onlookers cheer from a raised seawall. One continuous shot, static tripod camera at eye level; all five stay fully framed.

Rain glazes a rooftop helipad above Moscow, its painted concrete circle and worn chevron markings mirroring antenna masts, a dripping parapet and a stack of grey towers beyond. The air itself is still, only the drizzle falling. Six adults each claim a wedge of the circle: a heavyset Turkish man in black, a lean woman with red-dyed hair in silver, a tall Black man in white, a compact Japanese woman in orange, a bearded man in denim, a shaven-headed woman in green. Standing at first, they drop and burn continuous windmills, swing wide flares, and spin headspins that fling water off the concrete, staying on their own spots. All remain fully in frame. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-in, epic and cinematic.

Inside a mothballed Moscow car plant, five workers grip hands in a chain across glossy epoxy-coated concrete between stripped body shells and a dead overhead conveyor. A broad Slavic man with grey stubble anchors; behind him a wiry Vietnamese woman in coveralls, a tattooed white woman in a grey vest, a heavyset Turkish man in a brown jacket, and a rangy Black man in blue at the tail. They start fully framed, boots planted, then wind up a long crack-the-whip run, the chain curving until the tail man is slung twenty metres across the empty bay, skidding to a stop. Failing neon strips stutter and a crane beacon sweeps the floor. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace.

Under the glass canopy of a Moscow interchange hall, four adults face off on grey porcelain tile beside a shuttered flower kiosk and dead ticket machines. Two women — one tall, Nigerian, in a purple tracksuit, one compact and Kazakh with a black bob — square against a ginger-bearded man in green and a slim Filipino man in orange. All four begin fully in frame, shoes squeaking on the tiles. They snap foam balls at each other with hard sidearm throws, twist their hips clear, and one dives into a shoulder roll before firing back from his knees. Commuters watch from the mezzanine railing above. The air is still; daylight falls in shafts from high windows. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-in toward the four.

Snow falls thickly on the red-oxide steel deck of a river freighter moored at a Moscow inland port, an orange crane arm overhead and pale ice floes nudging the hull. Six adults in bright quilted jackets — a tall Brazilian woman, a short white man with a grey beard, a twin-braided Chinese woman, a broad Ethiopian man, a freckled woman in mint, a wiry Korean man — begin fully framed, boots on the painted plating. Each whips a long satin ribbon into spirals, then runs the length of the deck, leaping and turning so the ribbons corkscrew through drifting fog banks. Nobody else is aboard. One continuous shot from a static tripod camera at eye level.

A compact training cage in a Moscow gym: an octagon of vinyl-covered mat ringed by chain-link fence and blue wall padding, bright even overhead lighting leaving no shadows, air perfectly still. One man trains inside — early thirties, Kazakh, densely muscled, black hair shaved at the sides, wearing a sleeveless charcoal top, red shorts and taped ankles. Standing on one square of mat before a stacked plyo box, he loads and fires jump after jump, landing soft on top, stepping down, resetting his hips and exploding again, breath sharp. He never leaves his spot and stays fully in frame throughout. Onlookers watch from tiered seats beyond the fence, off the mat. One continuous shot, camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, epic and heroic.

Warm tungsten work lamps hang low over a Moscow ice rink, throwing amber pools on white ice striped with red and blue lines; steam drifts lazily from floor vents along the boards. Five adults each take their own circle: a tall Nigerian woman in a turquoise dress, a lean white man with long hair in black, a compact Chinese woman in fuchsia, a broad man in his fifties in grey, and a young woman with a blonde braid in orange. All hold their spots, entering spins and drawing arms in to accelerate into blazing scratch spins, blades shaving bright dust before they check out and set up again. Everyone stays fully in frame. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling slowly at chest height.

Rain lacquers a herringbone brick plaza before a university library in Moscow, the glass facade reflecting bike racks, a bronze bust and stuttering neon from a café sign while a searchlight sweeps the upper storeys. Three adults grip up on the wet brick: a heavyset Mongolian man in a white jacket, a tall Black woman with cornrows in blue, and a wiry man in his forties with a scarred brow in faded grey. Holding one small patch, they alternate hip throws — a partner is loaded across the hips, turned over, lands rolling, and springs back up to feed the next attempt. All stay fully in frame throughout. One continuous shot, camera orbiting slowly around them, epic contrast and cold reflections.

A shuttered Moscow roller rink: glossy maple boards, a dead disco globe, a boarded snack bar. Three adults in sneakers — a towering Sudanese man in black, a stocky Russian woman with a blonde crop and red shorts, a lean Peruvian man in grey — stand fully framed, feet flat on the wood. Two drop into tight crouches; the third sprints, plants both hands on their backs and vaults over each in turn, then they rotate roles twice, faster. Daylight cuts through high windows; broken neon stutters and a service lamp sweeps the boards. Spectators lean over the barrier rail. One continuous shot, handheld camera circling slowly at chest height as the last vaulter lands close and his torso crops out of frame.

Inside a municipal thermal-bath hall above Huaraz, two adults dance on non-slip ceramic tile beside a still turquoise lane pool, with a mural of terraced hillsides peeling on the far wall and two industrial fans stirring loose paper scraps and dust across the floor. One is a tall Black man in his thirties, lean and long-limbed, in a rust-orange shirt; the other is a broad-hipped Quechua woman in her forties with a black braid and a teal wrap skirt. They stay on one spot, driving fast double and triple salsa spins into sharp cross-body leads, heels snapping on tile. Bright even overhead lighting floods everything. One continuous shot, the camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace, both fully framed throughout, epic and cinematic.

Golden light rakes the striped tarmac of a high-altitude Peruvian race circuit's pit lane, empty garages open behind, mountains sinking into rolling fog. Two adults stand fully in frame at the far end: a compact Andean woman with a long black plait in a magenta crop top and white leggings, and a tall Dutch man with a sandy ponytail in a blue tank. They set off together down the lane, punching a run-up into round-offs, snapping back handsprings and finishing with tucked backflips, landing side by side and immediately turning to tumble back the other way, whooping. Fans clap from the balcony above the garages. One continuous shot, a handheld camera circling slowly at chest height, both athletes always fully visible.

A cavernous sound stage outside Cusco: matte black floor, a half-built plaster archway, coils of cable at the wall. Five adults in soft pastel athletic kit — a lanky Mexican man, a curvy Ghanaian woman with locs, a pale Irish woman, a broad Japanese man, a silver-haired Argentine woman — stand fully framed, trainers on the black paint. Haze pours in and a spotlight swings as they run a long relay across the stage, slapping batons into upturned palms at full speed, arms extended, each handoff cleaner than the last. Floodlights blaze from one side, throwing long shadows. Nobody else is here. One continuous shot, slow dolly-in until the final runner sprints past and clips out of frame.

Inside a colonial courthouse in a highland Peruvian city, four adults occupy a checkerboard marble hall lined with empty wooden benches and a tall shuttered window. There is a willowy Quechua woman in a saffron dress, a bearded white man in a slate suit, a shaven-headed Ivorian man in cream, and a short Japanese woman in violet. All four begin fully in frame, shoes on the polished squares. On an unseen call they burst forward three or four strides, then lock rigid mid-stride, arms frozen, before bursting again — a dreamy, stuttering game. Steam creeps from floor vents; a hard floodlight throws their shadows sideways. One continuous shot, a slow dolly-in until the nearest woman drifts close and her arm leaves frame.

Rain falls light and steady on a glacial outwash plain below a hanging valley, fine grey gravel darkened and gleaming, braided meltwater threading between moraine ridges, a rusted survey stake tilting nearby. The air is otherwise dead calm. A single adult woman occupies the frame: mid-thirties, Andean, thick-shouldered, hair pulled into a wet knot, wearing a soaked black thermal top and faded ochre shorts, mud striping her shins. She starts upright, both feet on the gravel, then drops and drives a punishing bear crawl a few meters out and back, palms slapping wet stone, gravel spraying from her toes, breath fogging. She stays fully in frame. One continuous shot, the camera panning slowly from left to right. Gritty documentary grain, desaturated and cold.
