Night on a bare granite shelf above a Greek island harbor, where a solitary chapel's blue neon cross and the pink glow of a quayside lamp stain the rock; an iron survey marker juts from a crack. Three adults move across the slab: a sinewy Malaysian man in gold shorts, a strong Greek woman with a shaved head in white, and a tall Nigerian-British man in red. They sink into deep crouches, heads cocked, then pounce forward in unison, land soft, spring sideways in low bounding leaps, and one launches onto the others' braced thighs before dropping back to stone. The night is windless and silent. One continuous shot, a handheld camera circling slowly at chest height, all three fully in frame.

A drained rice paddy in the Axios delta lies cracked and hard after harvest, stubble rows fading into the dark; a truck's parked headlights and a red-and-green channel beacon on the dyke are the only color. Two adults square off on one patch of dry mud: a heavy-shouldered Albanian man in a soaked black tee, holding curved pads low at thigh height, and a compact Filipina woman in navy, shins wrapped. She hammers repeated low kicks into the pad, alternating legs, then steps in and rips a rising middle kick that knocks him half a pace back; they reset without moving off the spot. Snowflakes drift through the headlight beams. One continuous shot, the camera orbiting slowly, both fully framed.

Only the maintenance lamps burn inside an old Athens velodrome; their tungsten glow rims the steep timber banking and pools on the flat grey concrete of the infield, where lane cones sit stacked and a track bike leans unattended. Two adults train on one square of floor: a rangy Sudanese man in a sleeveless grey top, gloves scuffed, and a stocky Portuguese woman with a short braid, mitts up, jaw set. She calls numbers; he answers with a jab-cross-hook, rolls under her return sweep, digs a hook to the body mitt and comes back upstairs, feet grinding a tight pivot. The empty bowl swallows the sound. One continuous shot, the camera craning from high above down to eye level, both fully framed.

Thick fog fills a marble quarry on a Greek island, softening the sawn white floor into pure glare; blade-cut benches step away into the murk, a wire-saw rig stands abandoned and stacked blocks loom like ruins. One woman is on the cutting floor, nobody else: early thirties, Māori-Greek, tall and long-limbed, dark hair tied back, navy singlet, white shorts, spikes chalked with marble dust. She stands fully in frame, feet on the stone, then drives into a long approach run, breaks into crossover strides with the javelin drawn back level, plants hard and hurls it away into the fog, the shaft vanishing before it lands. Snowflakes drift through the pale light beams. One continuous shot from a static tripod at eye level, epic and cold.

Storm light turns a small Attic village square theatrical: red brick pavers still dry, a huge plane tree thrashing overhead, a shuttered kafenio with stacked chairs, black cloud stacking behind the tiled roofs. One woman dances there — late twenties, Brazilian-Japanese, compact and strong, hair pinned in a low bun, magenta leotard over black shorts, canvas shoes. Villagers watch from the kafenio terrace behind its low railing, none on the bricks. She stands fully in frame, both feet on the pavers, then rips a triple pirouette, holds the spot, and chains fouetté turns, whipping leg after leg without travelling a step. Beyond the square, distant headlights streak past in long ribbons. One continuous shot, camera craning down from high above to eye level.

Snow falls thick over the rolled dry clay strip of an abandoned riverside cricket ground in Lisbon, where cracked sightscreens lean and a flickering neon sign buzzes above rusted floodlight masts while searchlights sweep the sky. Exactly three adults begin fully in frame, boots planted on the clay: a tall Black woman in a scarlet tunic, a wiry East Asian man in slate grey, a broad Latina woman in ochre. In one continuous shot they carry snare drums the length of the strip, hammering rolls and snapping into quick pivot turns. A handheld camera slowly circles at chest height; the woman in scarlet then strides toward the lens and ends partly out of frame.

Fog rolls thick between rows of tilted solar panels on a cliff-edge array above the Atlantic west of Lisbon, condensation beading on the glass, a bent inverter cabinet humming, surf booming unseen below the bluff. Two adults stand on the compacted red dirt access strip, both fully in frame the whole time: a stocky Middle Eastern man in a mustard windbreaker and a lean white woman with a silver-blonde braid in teal. In one continuous shot they hold one spot, alternating hard bat swings off a battered tee, resetting the ball, coiling and uncoiling with dust puffing under their heels. The camera dollies slowly out, revealing more panels swallowed by drifting grey.

Inside a disused foundry casting hall on Lisbon's industrial fringe, packed black sand covers the floor, cold ladles hang from a dead crane rail, and steam creeps from a floor vent into shafts of daylight falling from high clerestory windows. One adult occupies the space: a tall South Asian man in his thirties, shaved head, black vest and rust-red track pants, feet firmly on the sand and fully in frame as the shot opens. In one continuous take he explodes into a long sprint down the hall, then a bounding gallop, two silver streamers whipping behind him. The camera cranes down from high above to eye level as he charges past, ending partly out of frame.

Noon glare hammers straight down on a flat dark basalt shelf where the Atlantic lava coast meets the sea near Lisbon; shallow tide pools glint, a leaning stone cairn marks an old fishing path, and heavy swells burst white beyond the ledge. A single adult stands there, fully in frame from the first second: a muscular white woman in her forties, close-cropped auburn hair, faded charcoal singlet and navy shorts, bare feet on the stone. In one continuous shot she drives through repeated shuttle sprints between scattered cones, dropping low to slap each one, cutting hard and accelerating back, breath sharp, shadow tight beneath her. A static tripod camera at eye level holds the whole run.

Floodlights blaze down a narrow canyon between stacked shipping containers at the Lisbon port yard, snowflakes drifting bright through the beams, a crooked lashing-rod pile against one steel wall, gantry legs looming beyond. Two adults hold the concrete paver blocks, fully in frame throughout: a slim Afro-Portuguese man in a fitted black shirt and high boots, and a curvy white woman in her fifties wearing a deep red skirt that snaps with every turn. In one continuous shot they stay on one spot, trading thunderous zapateado bursts, heels rattling the pavers, arms curling overhead in sharp braceo. The camera cranes down from high above to eye level, snow crossing the lens.

Golden hour lies still and warm over a black volcanic sand cove tucked below the Lisbon coast road, a bleached driftwood spine half-buried near the tideline and a rusted mooring ring bolted into the cliff. Nothing moves but three adults, all fully in frame with feet in the sand: a heavyset Pacific Islander man in board shorts, a freckled white woman in a green rash top, a lanky Black man in cut-off denim. In one continuous shot they take short run-ups within a few meters and launch headfirst belly-flop dives, skidding across the sand, scrambling up grinning, spraying black grit. A slow pan travels left to right, gritty and unpolished.

Blue hour settles over a painted concrete apron beside a shuttered hangar at a small airfield near the Lisbon estuary mouth, faded yellow taxi lines curving away, a chained tug cart under a dead lamp, surf audible from the dunes past the fence. Three adults stand fully in frame, shoes on the paint: a tall Korean woman in a white warm-up, a broad Nigerian man in cobalt, an older white man with grey stubble in maroon. In one continuous shot they work a few meters of apron, snapping crossovers, between-the-legs combos and hesitation pulls, balls cracking off concrete. The camera orbits slowly; the Nigerian man drives at the lens and exits frame partly.

Late golden light rakes a weathered wooden promenade above an estuary beach south of Lisbon, planks silvered and warped, two lamp posts tilted from old storms, snowflakes turning gold as they drift through the low beams. Two adults hold the decking, fully in frame the whole time: a compact Vietnamese man with a knotted headband in olive shorts, and a tall Somali woman in a slate long-sleeve and cropped leggings. In one continuous shot they kick up into handstands and race the length of the boards, walking on their hands, breaking into springy handstand hops, crashing down and resetting. A handheld camera circles slowly at chest height, documentary-plain and unflattering.

Snowflakes sift through the shafts of light between silos at a grain loading yard on the Lisbon plain, where flat overcast daylight drains color from the dusty concrete slab, corrugated chutes tilt overhead and a spilled cone of pale grain has crusted near the wall. Five adults grip hands on the slab, all fully in frame: a burly white man in a canvas jacket, a Black woman in a purple hoodie, a wiry Filipino man in grey, a tall Turkish woman in orange, a middle-aged Latino man in denim. Their chain whips into a crack-the-whip spin, flinging the tail runner sprinting across the yard, one continuous shot with the camera tracking sideways at a steady walking pace.

Soft overcast light fills a still azulejo courtyard inside an old Alfama palace in Lisbon: blue-and-white patterned ceramic tile underfoot, a dry stone basin in one corner, ironwork balconies stacked above. Spectators lean on those upper railings and behind a low arcade rail, never setting foot on the tile. Four adults work the floor, fully in frame throughout: two men — one Japanese, one bearded white — and two women, one Ethiopian, one Portuguese, in worn white and indigo gis. In one continuous shot they stay on a single patch, drilling repeated o-goshi hip throws in rotating pairs, hips loading, partners arcing over and slapping the tile. The camera tracks sideways at a steady walking pace.

A bruised storm sky presses down on a painted intersection plaza in a Lisbon suburb, its asphalt covered in a huge geometric mural of ochre and blue, oil-drum planters marking the corners, shuttered kiosks waiting for the first rain. Five adults stand on the paint, all fully in frame at the start: a burly Samoan man, a tan white woman with a grey ponytail, a slender Indian man, a broad Black woman in yellow, a young Portuguese man in stripes. In one continuous shot they heave weighted sacks between partners across a few meters, catching low, staggering, hurling again. A slow pan crosses left to right as one man carries a sack toward the camera, ending partly out of frame.

Hazy afternoon wind lifts pale dust across a flat olive terrace above the coast west of Lisbon, gnarled trunks casting spindly shade, a stacked dry-stone retaining wall along one edge, breakers thudding far below the slope. One adult fills the space, fully in frame at the start with sandals planted on the dusty earth: a joyful South Asian man in his late twenties, wide grin, gold-embroidered vest over a bright turquoise kurta. In one continuous shot he bursts into high bhangra hops, springing squat kicks and shoulder bounces, arms punching overhead, covering a few meters between the trees. A handheld camera circles slowly at chest height until he bounds close and ends partly out of frame.

Heavy snowfall settles on a small forest clearing in the hills behind Lisbon, mossy stumps ringing the packed earth and leaf litter, a rusted iron vent cover breathing steam that curls through the flakes. Three adults stand there, all fully in frame with boots on the ground and never leaving it: a cheerful ginger-bearded white man in a red beanie, a compact Brazilian woman in a lime jacket, an older Chinese man in a padded blue coat. In one continuous shot they hold their spots and race to shovel, flinging bright arcs of snow over their shoulders, laughing, scraping down to bare leaves. A handheld camera slowly circles at chest height, warm and playful.

A dark storm ceiling hangs motionless over a firm red sand flat between dunes in a coastal reserve south of Lisbon, marram tufts stiff at the margins, an old survey post half-swallowed by sand, the air heavy and utterly still. Two adults stay fully in frame across the flat: a rangy Kenyan man in a white singlet and a strong Polish woman with a blonde bun in navy. In one continuous shot they run long approaches down the sand, break into crossover steps, plant hard and launch javelins in long arcs, then jog back grinning to repeat the run-up. The camera pans slowly from left to right, tracking their sweep across the open ground.

Bright even overhead lighting fills a worn municipal gymnastics hall in Lisbon: sprung carpet floor scuffed pale, chalk dust ghosting the air, foam mats folded against a scarred wall of wall-bars. Onlookers sit on pull-out bleachers behind the safety rail, none of them on the floor. Five adults grip a thick rope, all fully in frame with feet planted: a heavy white man in a grey tee, a sinewy Cape Verdean woman, a tattooed Latino man, a tall Nordic woman in blue, a stocky Japanese man. In one continuous shot they heave and slide a few meters back and forth, heels burning across the carpet until two collapse laughing. The camera dollies slowly in, the picture unpolished and unstyled.

Rain sweeps through low golden sun on a Lisbon rooftop where split chilies dry on woven trays, a canvas awning half-collapsed and terracotta chimneys steaming. Two adults hold their ground on the wet whitewashed cement: a stocky Portuguese woman in her forties, hair pinned, hugging a thick belly pad, and a lanky Cape Verdean man in soaked grey shorts. He drives three round kicks into the pad, right, left, right, each landing with a flat crack; she steps in and he checks her return kick with a lifted shin, then finishes with a clinch knee before both reset. Puddles burst under their pivot foot, the terrace holding no one else. One continuous shot, a handheld camera circling slowly at chest height, both fully framed.

An abandoned sandstone quarry near the Portuguese coast leaves a broad red bench of smooth rock, saw-cut walls striped behind it, cut blocks stacked and a rusted hoist anchor. Four adults spread across the shelf under flat overcast light: a tall Angolan man in a white tee, a freckled Irish woman in green, a stout Japanese man in navy, a broad-shouldered Dutch woman with a blonde ponytail. One snaps a long spiral pass while the others run crisp stem-and-break routes over thirty meters, cutting hard on the stone and hauling the ball in over an outside shoulder at full stride, then loop back grinning. The air is still. One continuous shot, a slow pan from left to right, all four staying fully in frame.

Light rain has stopped and left the sawdust-covered dirt of a timber yard outside Lisbon dark and reflective, stacked pine logs banded in steel, a silent bandsaw shed with its doors open, puddles holding the pale sky. The air is calm; nothing stirs but one adult, fully in frame with boots on the ground the entire time: a lithe Brazilian woman in her thirties, dark curls loose, wearing a soft grey wrap top and wide olive trousers. In one continuous shot she stays on one spot, spinning a long wooden staff into blurred figure-eights, rolling it across her shoulders and tossing it up to catch behind her back. The camera dollies dreamily in.

A vast Lisbon convention hall stands emptied after teardown: grey commercial carpet stretching between skeleton booth frames, taped cable runs, bright even overhead lighting cut by haze-machine fog and spotlights roaming slowly across the floor. Three adults occupy it, all fully in frame with feet down at the start and never leaving frame: a rangy Sudanese man in a black singlet, a compact white woman with a bleached crop in charcoal, an older Mexican man in dark grey. In one continuous shot they sprint the long carpet lane and snap relay baton handoffs at full speed, palms slapping back blind, accelerating away through the fog. The camera dollies slowly in toward them, cool and shadowed.

Warm tungsten work lamps hang low over a small converted rink in Lisbon, pebbled ice glittering under them, the painted house circles faded, a rack of granite stones and a scuffed board wall at the edge. Spectators crowd behind the plexiglass and along a mezzanine rail, none on the ice. Three adults hold the sheet, fully in frame with skates planted: a broad Ukrainian man in navy pads, a sharp-eyed Black woman in white, a stocky Portuguese man in red. In one continuous shot they stay on their creases, dropping into butterfly slides, snapping pad saves and glove stops, popping up again fast. A static tripod camera at eye level watches, grand and shadowed.

Mist hangs over a municipal tennis court in a Lisbon park at sunrise, its acrylic-coated concrete faded green and rust, the net sagging, plane trees dripping beyond a low chain fence where early walkers stop to watch from the path, none of them on the court. Three adults stand fully in frame, feet on the paint: a stocky Greek man, a tall Black woman in a yellow tee, a wiry white man with wet grey hair. In one continuous shot two race a wheelbarrow crawl a few meters across the baseline, palms slapping, the third holding ankles then swapping in. The camera dollies slowly in as one crawls close and ends partly out of frame.

Low tide bares a vast rippled sand flat in the Tagus estuary, hazy afternoon light flattening the distance; a beached wooden fishing boat lists on its keel and a channel stake leans in the shallows. Two adults splash across an ankle-deep pan: a barrel-chested Portuguese man with grey stubble in rolled-up work trousers, and a tall Ghanaian woman in a soaked blue dress. He stamps a heel down to blast a sheet of water at her legs; she scoops a double handful and hurls it back, then charges through, dragging a boot to throw a long curtain of spray, both shouting. Paper scraps skitter over the wet sand. One continuous shot, the camera orbiting slowly, both fully framed, feet in the shallow water.

A vast storm sky, still and bruised purple, looms over a wide bench cut into a limestone quarry outside Lisbon, terraced grey walls rising behind, an abandoned conveyor frame rusting at one end, compacted rock aggregate stretching flat underfoot. Five adults begin fully in frame, boots on the aggregate, and remain in view: a tall Ghanaian woman in gold, a silver-haired white man in slate, a young Iranian woman in crimson, a broad Brazilian man in white, a lean Korean woman in violet. In one continuous shot they cover the whole bench with running leaps and turns, long ribbons carving spirals and helices overhead. The camera pans slowly left to right across the immense grey terraces.

A Lisbon training hall holds a long indoor sprint track, blue polyurethane lanes glossy under shafts of pale daylight dropping from high clerestory windows; a stack of hurdles leans against the far wall beneath a dark scoreboard shell. Spectators sit on raised bleachers behind a railing, off the track entirely. Two adults keep their feet on the lanes and stay fully in frame: a striking Nordic woman in charcoal trailing a silver ribbon, and a Black man in his thirties, shaved head, dressed in deep burgundy. Bounding leaps and pirouettes carry them the full length of the lanes in one continuous shot, ribbons carving slow spirals through the light. The camera pans slowly from left to right.

Warm tungsten work lamps pool light across the painted grey concrete of an aircraft hangar near Lisbon, a half-stripped fuselage on jacks in the background, red tool chests along one wall, steam drifting lazily from a floor vent. Two adults hold a single spot, fully in frame throughout: a grinning Dominican man with thick forearms in a sleeveless yellow shirt, and a tall white woman in her twenties with a high ponytail in a mint tee and grey shorts. In one continuous shot they take turns swinging hard off a batting tee, hips whipping, balls cracking away into a hung net, resetting fast and trash-talking. The camera orbits them slowly, bright and cheerful.

Harsh midday sun bakes a decommissioned runway on the plain outside Lisbon, grooved asphalt seams sprouting dry weeds, a toppled distance marker and a boarded control shack far down the centerline, while pale daytime fireworks pop and smear against the sky over the distant hills. One adult stands fully in frame from the first second, shoes on the asphalt: a cheerful Puerto Rican man in his thirties, compact and powerful, in a lime tank top and black shorts. In one continuous shot he drives long resisted sprints down the runway, leaning hard into a stretched band and a dragging sled, covering ground. A static tripod camera at eye level watches him shrink and return.

Light rain glosses the pale limestone forecourt of a Lisbon museum, the low fountain basin dry and full of leaves, a bronze abstract sculpture catching grey light, steam curling from a grate near the steps. Five adults hold their own squares of stone, all fully in frame with feet down for the whole shot: a huge Angolan man in black, a lean white woman in orange, a middle-aged Indian woman in grey, a young Portuguese man in white, a broad Turkish man in blue. In one continuous shot they hammer out burpees in unison, chests slapping the wet stone, then exploding upward into jumps, water spraying off their hands. A static tripod camera at eye level holds steady.

Thick fog swallows a housing-estate basketball court in eastern Lisbon, the painted black asphalt slick with condensation, one rim bent and netless, a graffiti-scarred wall looming at the baseline while fine dust skims low across the surface on a ground-level draught. A single adult works there, fully in frame with sneakers on the asphalt the entire time: a wiry Cape Verdean man in his late twenties, braids tied back, faded grey hoodie sleeves pushed up. In one continuous shot he attacks the rim within a few meters, driving hard layups, snapping euro-step finishes, spinning back out to reload. A handheld camera circles slowly at chest height, raw and unpolished.

Nothing shades the raked red dirt of a disused baseball infield on the Lisbon outskirts at noon, the sun straight overhead, a sagging backstop net, a dead scoreboard with blank panels, weeds crowding the empty dugout. The air is dead still. Six adults stand fully in frame with cleats on the dirt: a heavyset white man, a tall Black woman, a compact Filipino man, a sinewy Portuguese woman, a bearded Iranian man, a young Latina in a bandana. In one continuous shot they sprint from the mound to the outfield unreeling a heavy fire hose hand over hand, then slam the coils down flat and race back. A static tripod camera at eye level records it all.

A rail viaduct on the Lisbon waterfront shadows a red painted tarmac cycle highway, light rain leaving it glossy and mirror-bright, faded lane arrows stretching into the distance, a dripping paint-streaked pillar and a bent bollard marking the curve. The air is still, only water running in the gutter. Six adults start fully in frame, shoes on the tarmac: two men and four women, among them a Black woman in green, a bearded white man in grey, a Vietnamese woman in orange, a Somali man in navy. In one continuous shot they run the lane in staggered pairs, all six staying fully in frame, snapping baton handoffs at full speed, spray kicking from their heels. The camera dollies slowly in.

Noon sun blazes off crusted white salt flats in the evaporation pans of the Lisbon estuary, conical heaps of raw salt drying beside a warped wooden sluice gate, the pan walls cracked and dazzling under a windless sky. Three adults stand fully in frame with feet on the crust: a sun-browned Portuguese woman in a straw hat and blue smock, a tall Nigerian man in a white shirt, and a stocky Japanese man in a red bandana. In one continuous shot they run a bucket brigade far along the pan, sprinting sloshing pails hand to hand. The camera dollies slowly in until the man in white passes close and ends partly out of frame.

Hard noon sun cuts through gnarled apple trees in an orchard on the hills north of Lisbon, dappling a level floor of clover and grass, windfalls scattered by the trunks, a low pipe vent behind the shed exhaling drifting steam. Two adults stay fully in frame with feet on the grass: a broad-shouldered Black man in his thirties in red gloves and grey shorts, and a lean white woman with a dark braid in blue gloves and a black tank. In one continuous shot they spar within a few meters, snapping jabs, slipping and rolling under hooks, pivoting on the springy turf. The camera orbits them slowly, crisp and energetic.

Fog banks roll steadily across a full-size artificial turf pitch at a suburban Lisbon club, green synthetic blades beaded with damp, a sagging goal net and a fence hung with faded cloth banners appearing and vanishing in the murk. Supporters watch from a small covered stand behind the barrier, never on the turf. Two adults stand fully in frame, feet on the pitch: a heavyset Indian man laughing already, and a tall white woman with cropped grey hair. In one continuous shot they hop the length of the pitch inside burlap sacks, both kept fully in frame, crashing down, rolling and scrambling upright to hop again. The camera dollies slowly out, revealing more of the drowned green.

A chalky gravel service path cuts through a lavender field on the Lisbon plateau, wet and shining after light rain, the purple rows heavy with water, a squat stone hut with a blue door at the far end, fog banks rolling steadily across the crop. One adult works there, fully in frame with boots on the gravel from the first second: a beaming Ethiopian woman in her thirties, hair wrapped in a yellow scarf, wearing a bright coral jacket and rolled work trousers. In one continuous shot she shovels furiously within a few meters, flinging glittering arcs of wet gravel sideways, racing an unseen clock. The camera orbits her slowly, playful and bright.

The dirt strip along the edge of a sunflower field on the Lisbon plain lies slicked by light rain, dry cracked soil darkened, heavy heads drooping and dripping, a leaning irrigation pipe and a rusted gate post breaking the yellow wall, the air otherwise dead calm. Five adults stand fully in frame, shoes on the wet soil: a big bearded white man, a Black woman in a red raincoat, a wiry Peruvian man, a tall Dutch woman in denim, a young Moroccan woman in green. In one continuous shot they sprint hard down the strip, then freeze mid-stride in wobbling statues, then explode forward again. The camera cranes down from high above to eye level, plain and gritty.

Night settles on a sun-baked brick yard behind a Lisbon kiln, magenta and green neon from a garage sign washing across the fired clay tiles, stacks of unglazed bricks casting long shadows, dry petals swirling low across the ground in an eddy of warm air. Two adults stay fully in frame with feet on the tiles: a lean Colombian man with a scarred brow in black gloves and grey trunks, and a tall Nordic woman with a platinum crop in oxblood gloves. In one continuous shot they spar across a few meters, slipping and rolling under punches, pivoting off the line, breath fogging in the neon. The camera dollies out slowly.

Bright even ceiling strips flood a road tunnel under central Lisbon that has been closed to traffic, white tiled walls streaked with soot, painted lane lines running away into the depth, sodium fixtures dark and a lone maintenance barrier at the mouth. Nothing moves but five adults, all fully in frame with shoes on the asphalt: a huge Black man in cobalt, a quick white woman in white, a Korean man in yellow, a tall Latina in red, a broad Portuguese man in grey. In one continuous shot they blaze long routes down the tunnel, cutting hard and hauling in over-the-shoulder catches. The camera tracks sideways at a steady walking pace.

Golden hour floods a freight depot platform on the Lisbon rail yards, low sun raking the weathered concrete, sealed boxcars parked alongside, a faded loading gauge arch and a stack of splintered pallets throwing long shadows. The air is completely still. One adult holds the platform, fully in frame with sneakers planted the entire time: a slim Chinese man in his late twenties, hair slicked back, wearing a matte black jacket and tapered trousers. In one continuous shot he stays on one spot, snapping robotic popping hits through his chest and shoulders, rolling smooth arm waves and freezing into hard angles. The camera dollies slowly out, the depot widening around him in cool shadow.

Soft overcast daylight lies flat and windless over an open-air suburban railway platform outside Lisbon: tactile-edged concrete with a worn yellow strip, a scratched glass shelter, a dead departure board and rails curving away between eucalyptus. Four adults stand fully in frame, feet planted and never moving off their spots: a towering Nigerian man in charcoal, a broad white woman with a grey braid in navy, a compact Peruvian woman in maroon, a bearded Serbian man in black. In one continuous shot they hoist heavy medicine balls overhead and slam them into the concrete, dust jumping, catching the rebound and driving up again. The camera dollies slowly out, revealing the long empty platform.

Blue hour glows over a wind-crusted snowfield on the highest sierra above Lisbon, buried fence posts marking an old boundary, a stone shepherd's shelter half-drifted over, distant fireworks blooming and fading along the horizon. Six adults stand fully in frame, boots gripping the packed snow and staying on their spots: a broad Black man in orange, a lean white woman in electric blue, a Japanese woman in white, a bearded Portuguese man in red, a tall Indian man in grey, a Ukrainian woman in yellow. In one continuous shot they rip speed jump-rope work, crossovers snapping into double-unders, snow dust flicking up. A static tripod camera at eye level frames the bright line of them.
